spec.name: Bauhaus Songbird on a Branch
spec.description: A small perched songbird built as a Bauhaus composition of circles, triangles and squares in flat red, yellow and blue, gripping a black branch that rests on a white plinth with two posts.
spec.layout: Real songbird scale: about 15 cm from beak tip to tail tip, standing about 16 cm above the floor (beak side +Z). Everything is centred on x = 0, the bird sits in the middle of a horizontal branch that runs along X, and the branch is held on two thin posts over a flat plinth lying on y = 0, so the plinth is the only thing touching the floor. The bird is seen in profile or three-quarter view and is a stack of simple solids, each a different primary shape. The body is a squat red ellipsoid (radii about 0.052 x, 0.05 y, 0.068 z) centred at [0, 0.17, 0]. Its head is a yellow sphere of radius 0.034 at [0, 0.228, 0.052], pushed forward and up. A blue pyramid or cone beak points forward from the head, with a smaller dark-blue lower beak on the jaw. The two blue wings lie folded against the flanks, slightly apart from the body and angled back and down, built as layered rectangular feathers. A fan of five rectangular tail feathers (yellow and blue) points back and slightly down to z = -0.19. Two thin yellow-dark legs come out of the belly and end in four-toed feet whose toes wrap over the branch top at y = 0.102. The style on every part is Bauhaus: bold geometry, flat primary colours (red, yellow and blue, plus black and off-white), no gradients, no organic detail. Circles are thin discs, squares are boxes, triangles are cones with 3 sides or extruded triangles. Each detail is a small separate part in its own flat colour, seated on the surface: eyes are stacked concentric discs (black outline, white, black pupil), bands are thin rings or boxes, and a black thin outline disc sits behind each coloured disc (about 0.0015 m larger) so shapes read as printed. Use low segment counts (8 to 12 around, 6 to 8 up) so facets show. Keep symmetric left/right pairs exact mirrors. Only the perch is on the floor. The bird's body, head, wings, tail and legs all sit above y = 0.10.

parts.builds: The whole head and neck collar. A yellow sphere head, radius 0.034, centred at headCenter, slightly flattened in y. A blue half-disc crest, an extruded semicircle about 0.028 wide, stands on the crown with a thin black outline disc behind it and a small red circle at its middle. On each side is a red cheek disc, radius 0.012, with a black outline disc behind it. The eyes sit on the front-sides of the head at about x ±0.022, y 0.235, z 0.075, each made of stacked discs: a black outline disc r 0.0125, a white disc r 0.0105, a black pupil disc r 0.006 and a tiny white highlight disc. A thin black brow bar sits above each eye, slanted slightly. The upper beak is a blue 4-sided pyramid or cone about 0.032 long, base radius 0.014, from beakBase pointing +Z, on the head bone. The lower beak is a smaller blueDark wedge on the jaw joint, with a thin black mouth-line box between them and two black nostril dots. Under the head is a neck collar: a white flat ring (short wide cylinder) with thin black rings above and below it, and a small red triangle bib point on the throat. Yellow-dark triangular feather points sit on the back of the head as a nape detail. Seat every detail on the sphere surface with stick.
parts.attaches: Neck collar sits on the top of the torso near neckBase. Head parts ride neck and head, and the lower beak rides jaw (hinge at jawHinge). Nothing in front of the face.

parts.builds: Body mass only, with the rump and the front of the chest. A red ellipsoid body (radii ~0.052, 0.05, 0.068) at bodyCenter, built as a loft or scaled sphere with 10 to 12 sides. An off-white belly half-ellipsoid or half-disc sits on the underside and front, hugging the body surface. A yellow chest bib triangle (extruded, pointing down, ~0.04 wide) sits on the front of the chest, outlined by a slightly larger black triangle behind it. Three thin black ring bands cross the breast, below the bib. A blueDark back saddle of overlapping rectangles lies along the top of the back. A yellow square rump patch is above the tail root. Thin black dividing bars separate the colour blocks. Two blue shoulder discs (r 0.014, black outline behind) sit on the flanks at the shoulderL and shoulderR mounts, but under the wings. Small red thigh-cover bumps (half spheres) sit at the hipSockets. All details are seated on the body surface using b.surface and stick.
parts.attaches: Head part's collar overlaps the top-front at neckBase. Wings start at shoulderL/R on the sides. Tail starts at tailRoot at the back. Legs come out below at hipSocketL/R.

parts.builds: Both wings and the tail, mirrored exactly. Each wing is a folded slab group that lies along the flank starting at the shoulder mount and angling back and slightly down and out (wingL1/2/3 and wingR1/2/3 bones). It has a blue covert panel (rounded/pointed extruded rectangle) over the shoulder, then 5 overlapping long primary feathers: rectangles with pointed ends in alternating blue and blueDark, longer toward the back, a yellow stripe bar across the middle, a red circle on the covert (with a black outline disc behind), and a white small square tip on each primary. A thin black edge line follows the leading edge. The tail is a fan of 5 rectangular feathers (thin boxes), 0.02 wide and 0.11 to 0.13 long, starting at tailRoot, running back and slightly down to z -0.19, spread by about 8 degrees each. The colours alternate yellow and blue, with the middle feather yellow, and each has a black end band and a white tip square. A red circle sits on the tail base, with a black outline behind it. Feathers on tail1/tail2/tail3 and wing bones by span.
parts.attaches: Wings start at the shoulderL/R mounts on the torso's flanks and sit just outside the body (x about ±0.052 to ±0.066). The tail starts at tailRoot, at the torso's back.

spec.name: Cyanotype Spitfire Mk I
spec.description: A low-poly Supermarine Spitfire rendered as a living cyanotype blueprint: deep Prussian-blue panels traced with glowing cyan seam lines, paper-white roundels, rivets and hand-inked annotations, standing nose-up on its taildragger undercarriage.
spec.layout: A Spitfire facing +Z, nose at z≈+4.9, tail at z≈−5.0, resting on three wheels: the two main wheels (radius 0.35, hubs at y=0.35, x≈±2.05, z≈0.75) touch y=0, and the small tailwheel at z≈−4.2 keeps the fuselage level with a slight nose-up stance. The elliptical monocoque fuselage runs from the engine cowl (z 4.3) tapering back through the cockpit (z≈0.3) to a slim tail cone ending at z=−3.6; belly line y≈1.15, spine y≈2.5. The wing is one low-mounted elliptical plate spanning x −5.6..+5.6 at y 1.25..1.75, meeting the fuselage belly at mount wingRoot, with a rounded tip, a dihedral-free flat top, a radiator bath under the port wing and gun fairings forward of the outer panels; ailerons hinge at the trailing edge from x≈2.8 outward. The empennage fills z −5.3..−3.4: a broad elliptical tailplane with hinged elevators and a tall rounded fin to y=3.4 with a hinged rudder reaching back to z≈−5.0, plus a tailskid above the tailwheel. The nose and canopy part owns the pale-steel spinner cone at mount spinnerBase with five propeller blades on joint propHub, and the framed bubble canopy rising from mount canopyBase to y≈2.95. Style everywhere: every panel is a flat cyanotype blue; seams, rivets, panel edges, hatch outlines, registration letters, serials, roundel rings and little inked callout arrows are separate thin parts in glowing cyan and paper white laid on the blue; spinner, hubs, gunsight and pitot are pale steel-blue; cockpit glazing is pale cyan; the only warm note is a tiny amber beacon on the fin tip.

parts.builds: The whole monocoque hull except nose spinner and canopy: build the body as a smooth low-poly loft/sweep along z from the firewall (z=4.3, roughly 1.1 wide × 0.95 tall ellipse at y≈1.9) swelling through the cockpit bay (z≈0.3, widest ~1.05 half-width, belly y≈1.15, spine y≈2.5) and tapering to the tail cone at mount tailRoot (z=−3.6, about 0.32 half-width, centred y≈1.85). Sections read as faceted ellipse sweeps (circle sections with modest sides, or loft stations). Wear hullBlue with panelBlue sectors on the upper spine and cowlBlue on the forward engine cowl ring. Details as seated thin parts: a ring of cyan panel-seam lines around the cowl (3 hoops of thin rods), exhaust stubs (six small dark angled frustum boxes, 3 per side at z 3.3..2.6 along the flank, deepInk with steelPale rims), paper-white rivet dots scattered in neat rows along two spine seams and around each panel line, a white serial text block on the rear flank ('P7350 AR·F' style, built from tiny inkWhite quads or extrude strokes), a small inked callout arrow (thin lineCyan stick with a chevron head) pointing at the fuel hatch on the starboard flank, an oil-stain patch (thin oilStain plate) low on the belly under the cowl, and the aft fuselage/wing fairing fillet reaching down to mount wingRoot. Also build the belly pitot-less fairing strip. Rides joint airframe.
parts.attaches: Nose face at mount spinnerBase hands over to the nose & canopy part; rear end at mount tailRoot hands over to empennage; underside fairing meets the wings at mount wingRoot; all rides joint airframe.

parts.builds: Both wings as one low elliptical plate: span x −5.6..+5.6, chord from z≈−0.6 (trailing edge) to z≈2.0 (leading edge), thickness y 1.28..1.72 with a rounded leading edge and knife trailing edge, meeting the fuselage belly at mount wingRoot. Wing tops wear hullBlue with panelBlue outer panels; the underside reads darker radiDark. Signature cyanotype details: a full set of paper-white national roundels on both upper wings (inner ring disc steelHub, outer ring lineCyan, built as thin stacked discs seated on the surface, radius ~0.55 at x≈±3.6, z≈1.0) and small inkWhite fin-flash rectangles are NOT here (they belong to empennage); gun fairings: two shallow blister boxes per wing forward of z≈1.4 at x≈±2.2 and ±2.9 in hullBlue with inkWhite rivet rows; the radiator bath: a recessed under-wing scoop at x≈−1.0, z≈0.9 with a slatted grid of thin steelPale bars; a paper-white wingtip light plate at each tip (x≈±5.5); ailerons: hinged trailing-edge flaps from x 2.8 to 5.2 on each side, thin wedge slabs hanging on joints aileronL/aileronR, hullBlue with a lineCyan hinge line and small white trim-tab marks; cyan panel-seam hoops crossing the wing chord at z≈1.6, 0.6 and −0.2 on both sides; an inkCyan annotation arrow near the port aileron; and a tiny pitot tube (thin steelPale rod) under the starboard wingtip leading edge. Wing geometry rides airframe; the ailerons ride aileronL/aileronR.
parts.attaches: Root chord sits on the fuselage fairing at mount wingRoot; the undercarriage legs hang from mounts gearAnchorL and gearAnchorR built by the undercarriage part; ailerons hinge on joints aileronL/aileronR.

parts.builds: The tail: from mount tailRoot (z=−3.6) build a slim tail cone continuation for the first 0.3 m, then the empennage. Tailplane: a flat elliptical plate spanning x −2.1..+2.1, chord z −4.9..−3.6, at y≈1.9, hullBlue on top with paper-white roundel-less plain panels, cyan seam line across each side at z≈−4.2, and hinged elevator wedges (the outer chord from z −4.9..−4.2 on each half) on joints elevatorL/elevatorR with lineCyan hinge lines and a white trim tab mark on the port elevator. Fin: a tall rounded dorsal blade rising from the spine (y≈2.1 at z=−3.6) sweeping back and up to y=3.4, reaching back to z≈−4.6, hullBlue forward face with a panelBlue leading-edge strip; its rudder (from z≈−4.35 aft, on joint rudder) wears the same hullBlue with three thin horizontal lineCyan hinge lines, a white rudder trim tab at its lower corner, and the classic paper-white fin flash: three vertical stripe plates (steelHub / roddGreen / steelHub, each ~0.12 wide) near the fin's leading edge. Rudder geometry rides joint rudder; fin and tailplane ride airframe. Add a small tailskid: a short angled steelPale rod above the tailwheel position (z≈−4.1, down to y≈0.45), a tiny amber beacon dome (beacon, small lathe dome with a lineCyan rim) on the fin tip, and an inked lineCyan arrow pointing at the tailplane adjuster on the underside.
parts.attaches: Forward faces meet the fuselage cone at mount tailRoot; elevators hinge on elevatorL/elevatorR, rudder on rudder; the tailwheel fork top is shared with the undercarriage part at [0, 0.55, -4.1].

parts.builds: The taildragger running gear, the only part touching the floor. Two main legs: from mounts gearAnchorL/gearAnchorR (x≈±0.62 on the wing underside) angled raked-forward-and-outward steelPale frustum rods down to wheel hubs at [±2.05, 0.35, 0.75] (on joints wheelFL/wheelFR); each leg gets a small V-brace (thin steelPale rod back to the wing underside near x≈±1.1, z≈0.4) and a hinged retract cover plate (thin hullBlue slab with a lineCyan edge) between the legs. Wheels: flat-cylindrical tyres (tyre, radius 0.35, width 0.16, low-poly with 12 flat side facets) with a steelHub hub disc, five lineCyan spoke studs, a deepInk tread ring seated on the rim, and a tiny inkWhite serial dot. Both wheels ride wheelFL/wheelFR. Tailwheel: a smaller wheel (radius 0.14) at [0, 0.32, −4.2] on joint tailwheel in a short steelPale fork that reaches up to [0, 0.55, −4.1] to meet the empennage tailskid, same hub treatment scaled down. Add small dust-grey mud marks (oilStain thin patches) low on the leg roots and a tiny inkCyan annotation arrow by the starboard leg.
parts.attaches: Leg roots bolt to the wing underside at mounts gearAnchorL/gearAnchorR; hubs on joints wheelFL/wheelFR and tailwheel; tail fork top meets the empennage tailskid.

parts.builds: The nose and cockpit furniture. Spinner: a pale-steel (steelPale) lathe cone from mount spinnerBase (z=4.3, base radius 0.42) tapering to a rounded tip at z≈4.9, with three lineCyan spin-ring hoops and a small inkWhite crest dot at the tip; ride it on airframe. Propeller: five blades on joint propHub — each a tapered flat wooden blade (roddGreen, ~1.55 long, widest ~0.17 near the root) with a paper-white tip band (~0.2 at the outer end), a steelPale root cuff cylinder, and an inkWhite rivet line; blades fan evenly around the hub. Cockpit: from mount canopyBase build the windscreen and sliding bubble canopy as a low-poly framed glazing — a shallow glass dome (glazing, faceted sphere segment) from y≈2.42 to y≈2.95 over z 0.35..−0.75, carried on a light steelPale frame of thin hoops and rails with inkWhite rivets, plus a fixed 3-panel windscreen wedge at z≈0.55 tilting back. Inside and behind: a steelPale pilot seat back plate, a deepInk headrest block under the spine fairing, a tiny gunsight (steelPale post with an inkWhite ring) on the coaming, and a small lineCyan instrument glow quad on the dash face. Add two tiny inkWhite wiper/annotation ticks beside the canopy rail. Rides airframe; the propeller blades ride propHub.
parts.attaches: Spinner base sits on the fuselage nose face at mount spinnerBase; canopy base sits on the fuselage spine at mount canopyBase; blades on joint propHub.

pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: Spitfire fighter plane.
Style: cyanotype blueprint.

spec.name: Blueprint Spitfire
spec.description: A Supermarine Spitfire fighter on its landing gear, rendered as a living cyanotype blueprint: deep Prussian-blue hulls covered in white-cyan drafting linework, glowing panel seams and a gridded drafting sheet under it.
spec.layout: Museum-level stance, all three wheels resting on a flat drafting sheet at y=0; the plane itself sits level, nose to +Z. From the front: a five-blade propeller disc (r 1.65, hub centre y 1.85) on a tapered steel spinner reaching z 4.95, behind it the rounded cowling barrel (y 1.35..2.1). The low elliptical wing spans x -5.55..5.55 at y 0.95, chord 2.7 at the root tapering to a rounded 1.15 tip, with cannon barrels through the leading edge, a radiator bath under each wing and ailerons at the trailing edge. Above the wing root: an open cockpit trough at z 1.2..2.1 closed by a framed canopy whose top is y 2.45. The fuselage loft tapers from the bulged cockpit section to a slender tail cone at z -3.4, which the tail part continues to z -4.5, carrying the swept fin (top y 2.9, hinged rudder) and the elliptical tailplane with elevators. The style shows everywhere: every hull surface is flat blueprint blue (lighter on top, deeper below), panel seams, rivets, port rims and outlines are seated lineWhite strips, studs and decals, leading edges, canopy glass and hub rings glow cyan, tiny amber accents mark wingtip lights and prop-blade tips, and the sheet under the whole plane carries the grid, border, title block, dimension lines and section flags.

parts.builds: The monocoque spine from the cowling front face back to the tail cone at z -3.4. Build one loft along z from [0,1.85,3.3] to [0,1.35,-3.4]: cowling barrel widest at the nose (half-width 0.49, from y 1.35 to 2.1), slimming over the forward fuselage, a bulged cockpit section (half-width 0.5), then tapering to a slender cone (half-width 0.18) at z -3.4. Main loft hullBlue; a panelBlue band rings the cowling at z 2.9..3.3, and a deepBlue belly strip runs under the cockpit. Add a dorsal spine ridge fairing (panelBlue) along the top from z 1.0 to z -3.4. Cockpit at z 1.2..2.1: recessed trough rim, then a closed canopy — steel frame ribs, glowCyan glass panes, and lineWhite seam strips on the frames. Drafting details: five panel seam bands of thin lineWhite strips (0.012 thick, seated 0.005 proud) ringing the loft at z 2.8, 1.9, 0.9, -0.6 and -2.2, with ~50 tiny lineWhite rivet studs along them; two gun cowl ports above the cowling at z 2.55, x +/-0.28 (deepBlue discs with lineWhite rims); six exhaust stubs (steel, three per side) along the cowl sides at z 2.95..3.55 at y 1.55, raked back; a steel antenna mast on the spine at z -1.0 with a faintCyan antenna wire stub; an oil cooler scoop (deepBlue with a glowCyan grill face) under the nose at z 2.4; and a lineWhite crosshair inspection circle decal on each side of the tail cone. Attaches: its front face at z 3.3 meets the propeller at mount noseRing; its lower flanks join the wings at mounts wingRootL and wingRootR; its rear face at z -3.4 hands over to the tail.
parts.attaches: Front face at mount noseRing (propeller); lower flanks at mounts wingRootL/R (wings); rear face at z -3.4 (tail).

parts.builds: Both elliptical wings, built as one piece per side with loft stations running out along x from 0.95 to 5.55: chord 2.7 at the root tapering smoothly (elliptical planform) to 1.15 at the rounded tip, thickness about 12% of chord, wing plane centred at y 0.95 with 0.06 of dihedral. Upper surfaces hullBlue, undersides deepBlue, split along the leading-edge crown line. A thin glowCyan strip runs along the leading edge of each wing. Trailing edge: ailerons (panelBlue slabs, x 3.1..5.3, offset 0.03 behind the wing with lineWhite seam gaps and small hinge studs) and inboard flaps (deepBlue, x 1.1..3.0) with the same seam treatment. Cannon: two per wing — steel barrels (r 0.045) protruding 0.5 from the leading edge at x +/-2.55 and +/-3.9, y 1.0, each with a panelBlue fairing bulge and a lineWhite port ring; two further machine-gun ports (lineWhite-rimmed deepBlue discs) at x +/-4.7. Radiator bath under each wing at x +/-1.75, z 0.35: a deepBlue scoop 0.55 long with a glowCyan grill face and a lineWhite edge. Drafting details on the upper wing: a concentric paper crosshair roundel (lineWhite rings, outer 0.9 diameter) at x +/-2.3, and ~10 small faintCyan inspection patches (thin rectangles with corner rivets) scattered on the upper skin. Tip details: amber disc lights at both wingtips, a steel pitot tube below the left (+x) tip and a faintCyan nav light disc under the right tip. Attaches: each root meets the fuselage flank at mounts wingRootL and wingRootR; the undersides at mounts gearTopL and gearTopR take the landing-gear struts.
parts.attaches: Roots at mounts wingRootL/R (fuselage); underside strut mounts gearTopL/R (landing gear).

parts.builds: Everything aft of z -3.4. First the rear fuselage cone: a continuation of the spine loft from half-width 0.18 at z -3.4 down to 0.10 at [0,1.35,-4.5], hullBlue with one lineWhite seam band and a few rivet studs. The fin: an extruded flat slab with the swept Spitfire profile, root spanning z -3.6..-4.5 at the spine, top at y 2.9, leading edge leaning back; hullBlue, with a panelBlue rudder slab hinged on the rudder joint covering the rear half of the fin, edged in lineWhite seam strips, with small lineWhite hinge studs and a lineWhite crosshair circle decal at y 2.3. A panelBlue fillet fairing blends the fin root into the spine. The tailplane: two elliptical flat slabs, each spanning out to x +/-1.85, at y 1.95, z -4.0, hullBlue on top and deepBlue below, each with a panelBlue elevator slab covering the rear 30% and lineWhite seam gaps; a lineWhite crosshair circle on the upper tailplane. A small steel rudder actuator rod runs under the tail cone. Attaches: its front face at z -3.4 meets the fuselage rear face at mount finRoot; the cone underside at mount tailwheelTop takes the tail wheel.
parts.attaches: Front face at z -3.4 (fuselage, mount finRoot); underside at mount tailwheelTop (landing gear tail wheel).

parts.builds: The propeller assembly on the propHub joint at mount noseRing [0,1.85,3.3]. Spinner: a lathe of steel, radius 0.34 at its base tapering to a blunt rounded tip at z 4.95, with a lineWhite ring at its base and a small lineWhite crosshair decal on the tip. Behind the spinner, a steel back-plate disc (r 0.4) at z 3.35 with a glowCyan hub ring. Five blades radiating from the hub, one pointing straight up, the others at 72 degree steps around the z axis: each a flat extruded blade from radius 0.3 to 1.65, 0.24 wide, twisted about 20 degrees along its length, deepBlue, with a thin lineWhite edge line on each face and the outer 0.25 of each tip painted amber. Blades are thin (0.02..0.05 thick, lens-shaped), so the disc reads as five crisp lines. Attaches: the hub root seats into the cowling front face at mount noseRing; the whole assembly rides the propHub joint.
parts.attaches: Hub root at mount noseRing (fuselage); blades spin on joint propHub.

parts.builds: The ground stance; the only aircraft part whose wheels touch the sheet at y 0. Two raked main legs, each a steel capsule strut (r 0.055) from mount gearTopL [1.6,0.9,0.8] (and mirrored gearTopR) down and outward to the axle at [2.55,0.55,0.95] (mirrored), with a thinner steel drag brace (r 0.035) from a point at z 1.35 on the wing underside back to mid-leg, plus a small faintCyan inspection band on each strut. Wheels at the axles: r 0.55, 0.18 wide tires in deepBlue with a lineWhite tread seam ring, steel hubs r 0.20 each with a lineWhite bolt circle of 8 tiny studs and one small amber greaser dot. Tail wheel: a steel leaf-spring strut (a short flat slab) from mount tailwheelTop [0,0.55,-4.05] down to the axle [0,0.2,-4.05], with a small deepBlue tire (r 0.2) and steel hub with a lineWhite stud ring. All three wheels rest exactly on the sheet; nothing else of this part goes below y 0.05. Attaches: leg tops at mounts gearTopL/R (wings); tail-wheel strut top at mount tailwheelTop (tail).
parts.attaches: Leg tops at mounts gearTopL/R (wings); tail wheel top at mount tailwheelTop (tail).

parts.builds: The cyanotype drafting sheet the plane stands on — flat slab 12.4 x 10.8 (x +/-6.2, z +/-5.4), 0.03 thick, top surface at y 0.03, in sheetBlue, with a gridCyan grid paint of 0.5 m squares and a double border frame (a lineWhite strip inside a glowCyan strip) 0.15 in from the edge, plus lineWhite corner registration crosses. Title block at the near-right corner (x 3.6..6.0, z -5.3..-3.9): ruled lineWhite rows and svg decals in lineWhite reading SUPERMARINE SPITFIRE MK.IX, PROJ 1942, SCALE 1:24, SHEET 3 OF 12, with one small amber stamp disc. Drafting overlay around the plane: one lineWhite dimension line with arrowheads running along x at z -2.2 measuring the wingspan, one lineWhite height dimension beside the nose at x 2.2 with tick marks, three circled section flags (glowCyan rings with lineWhite letters) floating beside fuselage and wing around x +/-3.4, y 2.6, and a faint glowCyan arc on the sheet at z 4.3, r 1.65, marking the propeller disc sweep. All annotation decals sit in model space on the airframe bone; the sheet itself is a static prop.
parts.attaches: Lies flat under the whole model; the three gear wheels rest on its top face at y 0.

calls.reasoning:
I need to write a spec JSON for a team building a Spitfire fighter plane in cyanotype blueprint style. Not module code — just the JSON spec.

Cyanotype blueprint style: deep Prussian blue background/ink, white/cyan line work. For a 3D model of a Spitfire in blueprint style: the plane's surfaces are deep blue with white/cyan linework, panel lines, rivets, annotations drawn as decals/parts, glowing white-cyan edges. Palette: blueprint blue (#1a3a6b or classic cyanotype #0b3d91 / #16305c), lighter blue mid tone, white line color (#eaf6ff), cyan glow (#3fd9ff), maybe accent pale. The plane stands on floor — landing gear down, so it sits on y=0 on wheels/tail skid. Real Spitfire: length ~9.1 m, wingspan ~11.2 m, height ~3.0 m (with prop). That's big. Maybe keep real-world size: 11.2 wide, 3.7 tall (prop disc), 9.8 long. That's within limits.

Spitfire layout: elliptical wings, round tail, spinner with 5-blade prop, bubble-ish canopy (Spitfire has rounded canopy), radiator under wing, exhaust stubs, roundels (could be blueprint annotation circles instead — in blueprint style, roundels as circles with crosshairs). Blueprints have title blocks, dimension lines, rivet dots, section markers.

Parts (3–6):
1. Fuselage: monocoque body, nose/engine cowling, canopy, tail boom to fin, cockpit frame.
2. Wings: elliptical wing pair, radiators, cannon, fuel vents.
3. Empennage: tail fin, rudder, horizontal stabilizers.
4. Propeller & engine front: spinner, 5 blades, exhaust stubs.
5. Landing gear: main wheels, gear struts, tail skid, ground stance.
6. Blueprint annotations: title block, dimension lines, crosshairs — but every piece must belong to exactly one part. Could make a "blueprint drafting layer" part that owns annotation overlays across the model. But box constraints — annotations span whole model. Hmm, annotations could be attached per-part. Or a 6th part "annotation overlay" with a box spanning the whole model — allowed since parts are defined by box but annotations float near the plane. Better to assign annotations to each builder's part? The spec says each part owns its details. But a drafting overlay (title block on the floor, dimension lines) — the floor rest: title block as a ground plane decal under the plane? That's scenery though — but blueprint style strongly suggests a drafting sheet background. The brief says scenery only where named; the blueprint style could name a drafting-sheet ground. I could make the floor: a large blueprint sheet with grid, title block. That's part of the pitch's style, acceptable: "its style is unmistakable." I'll make a "drafting sheet" ground plane as part 6 with floor: true, and plane parts floor: false except landing gear.

Actually "floor: true marks the parts whose lowest points rest on y = 0" — the wheels rest on y=0; the sheet at y=0 too. Fine.

Parts:
1. fuselage — spine, nose cowling, canopy, cockpit. Box roughly [-0.8, 0.9, -4.2] to [0.8, 2.4, 3.2]... Let me lay out coordinates.

Spitfire dims (scaled): length 9.2 m, height 3.7 m (prop top), wingspan 11.2 m. Center on x=0, front +Z. Let nose at z=+4.6, tail at z=-4.6. Ground y=0; wheels radius ~0.45, axle at ~1.4? Actually Spitfire main wheels are ~0.5 diameter... Let's approximate: axle height 0.75, wheel radius 0.75? Real Spitfire wheel diameter ~0.57m. Let's say wheels radius 0.55, axle at y=0.55 under wings at z≈+0.6, x≈±2.6. Tail wheel small, radius 0.18, at z≈-4.2.

Wing: elliptical, chord at root ~2.6m, span from centerline to tip 5.6m each side. Wing plane at y≈0.75 (low wing). Tail plane at y≈1.9, z≈-4.0, span 3.2.

Prop: spinner tip at z=+4.9, prop disc radius 1.7 at y≈1.9. Height: prop blade tips reach y≈3.6. Size [11.2, 3.7, 9.8].

Size: width 11.2, height 3.7, length 9.8.

Colors (≤24):
- ink: #0e2a5e deep blueprint blue (main hull)
- inkMid: #1d4a8f lighter blue panel tone
- inkDeep: #081a3d darkest
- paper: #dfeeff white-cyan linework / annotations
- cyan: #3fd6ff glow lines
- cyanDim: #7fb8d9 faded annotation
- steel: maybe gear metal in blueprint tone — keep in blue family: gearBlue #29477e
- propInk: #143366
- accent amber? Blueprint usually mono; keep a faint warm accent maybe not. Keep all blue/white/cyan. Add "grid" #16355f for sheet grid, "sheetBlue" #0d2f63 sheet background... Sheet is big flat plane with grid via paint? Parts are flat colors — grid lines as parts would cost too much. Use paint? Palette limited but paints allowed? The spec format says every surface is one flat colour. Grid could be a texture? Keep it simple: sheet = deep blue with cyan border frame and corner marks as parts; grid via paint is riskier to spec. I'll specify grid as paint on the sheet (paints are allowed in the SDK; the spec's palette is flat colours). I'll mention paint for grid. Or simpler: grid drawn as thin strips — too many parts. Use paint stripes? I'll spec: sheet is one flat deep-blue plane with a cyan border and title block drawn as parts, plus a subtle grid via a paint of fine lines. Fine.

Joints: static model? The system prompt says static models may omit joints. But spec template includes joints. A plane on the ground — static is fine, but propeller could spin? It's a display model; give prop a hinge joint? Joints for a display model: maybe none. Simpler: static, joints: []. But the template shows joints with roles. I'll make it static except maybe prop spin — riggers appreciate. Let me include a root "airframe" joint and a "propHub" hinge, "rudder" hinge maybe. Hmm, if joints exist, the model is rigged; roles must be from list. Prop = "hinge"? Rotating prop is a hinge. I'll do: root joint "airframe" at [0,0,0] role "spine"; "propHub" at [0,1.85,4.55] dir [0,0,1] role "hinge" group "prop". Keep it minimal: 2 joints. Wheels as joints? Could add wheelFL/FR and gear struts, tailWheel for animation. Let's add: wheelFL, wheelFR (role "hinge", group "gear"), tailWheel hinge, rudder hinge. 6 joints. Parts list which joints they ride.

Parts (6):
1. fuselage — nose to tail cone, cockpit, canopy, fillets. Box [-0.9, 0.6, -4.5] to [0.9, 2.35, 3.4]. Budget 220.
2. wings — both elliptical wings, ailerons, radiators, cannon barrels/ports, wingtip lights. Box [-5.6, 0.55, -1.2] to [5.6, 1.5, 2.4]. Budget 220.
3. tail — fin, rudder, tailplane, elevators, tailwheel assembly? Tail wheel under fuselage part? Assign tail wheel to tail part: box [-1.9, 0, -4.6] to [1.9, 2.6, -3.0]. Budget 140.
4. propeller & nose gear of engine — spinner, 5 blades, exhaust stubs, hub. Box [-1.75, 0.35, 3.2] to [1.75, 3.7, 5.0]. Budget 150. Blades: 5 blades from hub radius 0.35 to 1.65, tips reaching y 3.6 at 12 o'clock... Actually blade disc center at y=1.85, radius 1.65 → tips y 3.5. Blade tips at lowest reach y=0.2 — above floor ok (floor false). But blade pointing down reaches y=0.2, fine.
5. landing gear — main struts, wheels, mudguards/spats. Box [-3.0, 0, 0.0] to [3.0, 1.0, 1.4]. floor true. Budget 120.
6. blueprint drafting layer — the sheet on the ground (11.5 × 10 sheet), grid, title block, dimension lines, crosshair roundels, callout labels, section marks. Box [-6.0, 0, -5.2] to [6.0, 0.04, 5.2]. floor true. Budget 150. Hmm but "subject is the hero... scenery only where the brief names them" — the brief is "cyanotype blueprint" style, which I interpret as naming a drafting-sheet presentation. I think it's right for this category. Size it to the plane footprint.

Mounts: 
- noseRing [0,1.85,3.45] where prop spinner meets cowling (fuselage ↔ prop).

spec.name: Blueprint Spitfire Mk V
spec.description: A Supermarine Spitfire fighter built as a living cyanotype blueprint: deep Prussian-blue surfaces traced with pale-cyan panel lines, glowing cyan roundels and bright technical linework on every part.
spec.layout: A low-wing single-seat fighter standing on its undercarriage, level on the floor: main wheels at z≈2.35 and a small tailwheel at z≈-4.35 touch y=0; everything else hangs above the floor. From front to back: a pointed brass-capped spinner with three wide propeller blades (tips banded in glowing cyan) at z≈4.1-4.9, then the rounded engine cowling with cooling gills and exhaust stubs (z 2.55-4.1), the elliptical monocoque fuselage with a flat spine deck under the bubble canopy (z -3.45 to 2.55), then the tapered rear fuselage into the tall swept fin (top y 3.45) and horizontal tailplanes (z -3.45 to -4.95). The elliptical wings span x ±5.6 at y≈1.5, root chord about 3 m tapering to 1.1 m at the rounded tips, with a slight dihedral. The style shows on every part: all main surfaces wear the deep Prussian blue of blueprint paper; every seam, panel line, rivet row, control-surface edge and stencil is a separate thin part in pale cyan or bright cyan, so the whole plane reads as a technical drawing made solid; roundels, walkway trim and the gun-sight glow provide the only strong accents (white, red, brass, glowing cyan).

parts.builds: Engine section and propeller. Cowling: a lofted tube from the firewall mount (z 2.55, radius ~0.62, slightly taller than wide) tapering to radius 0.42 at the spinner base (z 4.1), wearing paper blue; a row of ~10 vertical cooling-gill slats on each side between z 2.9 and 3.6, each slat a thin paperShade plate with a pale line-colour edge strip; two small raised access panels on the cowling top in panel blue with line-colour outlines. Exhaust stubs: three short faired stacks per side at z 2.8-3.4, x ±0.62, steelDark with a line-colour rim on each outlet. Spinner: a lathe cone from z 4.1 (r 0.42) to z 4.78 (r 0.07) in paper blue with a brass hub cap and a thin glow-colour ring where cowling meets spinner. Propeller: three blades on propHub, each a tapered, slightly twisted blade 0.95 long from the hub, paperShade with a line-colour leading-edge strip and the outer 0.12 banded in glow cyan; a thin glowing cyan arc ring of radius 0.95 at z 4.2 traces the prop disc like a blueprint annotation. Add thin line-colour panel-seam strips around the cowling at two frame stations.
parts.attaches: Cowling back face meets the fuselage at the firewall mount (z 2.55); spinner and blades ride the propHub joint at [0, 2.05, 4.15].

parts.builds: Monocoque hull. A loft along z from the firewall (z 2.55) back to the tailRoot mount (z -3.45): elliptical sections ~0.62 wide at the firewall, widest (~0.66) at the cockpit z≈1.0, tapering to ~0.30 at the tail, centreline y ~1.8-2.0 with a rounded belly; flat-ish spine deck at y 2.15 from the cockpit back (the deckTop mount plane), wearing paper blue with two or three large subtle panel-tone patches in panel blue inset on the flanks. Blueprint linework: thin line-colour frame-station strips wrapping the hull at 7-8 stations, two longitudinal stringer lines each side, and a spine ridge strip on the deck; a few tiny ink-colour vent and filler dots. Markings: RAF roundels on both flanks at z≈0.3, y≈1.85 — concentric flat discs (roundelBlue r 0.22, white r 0.15, red r 0.07) each with a hairline ink rim, seated slightly proud of the skin. A small steel antenna mast on the deck just behind the cockpit with a short ink antenna wire stub running back. Underside: two small ink-colour breather scoops under the belly near the wing root.
parts.attaches: Front face closes onto the nose at the firewall mount; rear face closes onto the tail at the tailRoot mount; top deck carries the cockpit at the deckTop mount; wing roots bury into the flanks at the wingRoot mounts.

parts.builds: Elliptical cantilever wings, mirrored left and right about x=0. Each wing runs from the root (x ±0.6, buried into the fuselage flanks at the wingRoot mounts) to a rounded tip at x ±5.6; root chord ~3.0 m (z 0.5-3.1 at the root, narrowing to ~1.1 m at the tip), thickness ~13% of chord at the root, a slight dihedral lifting the tip ~0.25 m. Build each as a loft of airfoil sections along the span, paper blue on top and bottom, with panel-blue panel patches on the upper surface, ink-colour rib lines running chordwise every ~0.5 m out to mid-span, a line-colour spanwise spar strip, and a row of tiny line-colour rivet dots along the root. Armament: two Hispano cannon per wing whose steel barrels (r 0.045, length 0.55) protrude forward from the leading edge at x ±1.7 and ±2.6, each with a brass muzzle ring and a tiny glow-colour muzzle cap; gun ports as small ink-colour oval plates on the wing top above each barrel. Markings: upper-surface roundels at x ±2.4, z≈2.3 (roundelBlue r 0.30, white r 0.20, red r 0.09, ink rim), a trim-colour walkway strip along the inboard leading edge, and a small glow-colour landing light set flush in the leading edge near the root (x ±1.2). A thin steel pitot tube under the left wing tip leading edge, 0.35 long with a glow tip.
parts.attaches: Roots bury into the fuselage flanks at the wingRootL and wingRootR mounts, sharing the fuselage box at z 0.5-3.1; undersides at x ±1.05, y 1.3, z 2.5 carry the gearMounts.

parts.builds: Empennage. Fin: a swept curved fin from the tailRoot mount deck (z -3.45) up to y 3.45, built as an extruded slab ~0.09 thick with a rounded leading edge, paper blue with a line-colour outline strip around its edges; the fin flash near the top leading edge — three vertical stripes (roundelBlue, white, roundelBlue) each ~0.10 wide, seated flat on the fin. Rudder: the rear half of the fin from the rudderHinge line (z -4.45) aft, a thinner slab with a small horn balance at its bottom, panel blue with a line-colour edge, riding the rudderHinge joint, plus a small trim tab at its base. Tailplanes: two horizontal slabs spanning x ±1.9 from the rear fuselage, chord ~0.9 tapering to a rounded tip, slight dihedral, paper blue with ink-colour edge lines. Elevators: the outboard rear halves riding elevatorL and elevatorR, panel blue with a line-colour edge and a small horn balance each. A tiny glow-colour tail lamp at the very tip of the fin, and three thin line-colour frame-station strips wrapping the fin.
parts.attaches: Front faces close onto the fuselage rear at the tailRoot mount (z -3.45); control surfaces ride the rudderHinge, elevatorL and elevatorR joints.

parts.builds: Canopy and cockpit furniture sitting on the deckTop mount plane (y 2.15). Canopy framing: a windscreen frame of thin steel arcs at z≈0.5 with a flat framed glass pane in glass colour, then two hoop frames at z≈0.95 and z≈1.35, all steel, with glass-colour panes between, the bubble roof peaking at y 2.65 and fairing down to the deck at z≈1.75; a line-colour seam strip follows the canopy base rail. Interior hints (readable through the side panes): a seat-colour seat slab with an ink-colour frame rail at z 0.9-1.2, and a small headrest fairing. Ahead of the windscreen: a dark ink-colour instrument panel cowl at z≈0.45 with four tiny line-colour dial discs and hairline ink needles, and a reflector gun sight on a steel stalk at z≈0.55, y≈2.45 — a small brass-colour body with a glowing cyan sight dot. Thin steel canopy side rails run along the deck at x ±0.5 from z 0.4 to 1.7.
parts.attaches: Base sits on the fuselage spine deck at the deckTop mount (y 2.15, z 0.15-1.8), fully inside the fuselage box footprint.

parts.builds: Undercarriage — the only part touching the floor. Main gear, mirrored: a raked main leg from each gearMount (x ±1.05, y 1.3, z 2.5) down-forward to the wheel hub (x ±1.15, y 0.33, z 2.35), built as a two-piece steel strut — a thick main leg with an ink-colour seam strip and a smaller rear drag strut joining mid-leg to the fuselage belly; a small steel torque-link detail beside each leg. Wheels ride the wheelFL and wheelFR joints: radius 0.33, width 0.14, ink-colour rubber tire with a thin paperShade sidewall ring, and a steel hub disc carrying five small ink-colour holes arranged in a ring and a line-colour rim. Tailwheel: a steel fork from the tailWheelMount (y 0.55, z -4.3) down to a small wheel at the tailWheel joint — radius 0.16 at y 0.16, z -4.35, ink-colour tire with a steel hub. Both main wheels and the tailwheel rest exactly on y = 0.
parts.attaches: Leg tops meet the wing undersides at the gearMountL and gearMountR mounts; the fork meets the rear fuselage underside at the tailWheelMount; wheels ride the wheelFL, wheelFR and tailWheel joints.

- Markings: a fuselage roundel (line, skinDeep, lineSoft, roundelCore rings, radius ≈ 0.38) on each flank at z ≈ -2.4, y ≈ 1.58, and code letters and a serial drawn as small line-coloured parts or an svg decal on the flanks.
- Lines: a dashed lineFaint centre line along the top spine, rivet rows along the flanks, and a white line along the wing-root join.
The wing and gear attach to it, and it does not build the wing root fillets.
parts.attaches: Front face at noseBase meets the propeller part's spinner back plate. Rear face at tailRoot meets the tail part's cone. The wing root buries into the belly at wingRootL and wingRootR. Rides joint fuselage.

parts.builds:
Both elliptical wings as lofts through the wing stations, with dihedral, in skinTop above, skinShade below, and a white `line` leading-edge strip.
- Surfaces: rib lines (lineSoft thin strips) every ~0.35 m across the upper surface, spar lines, and a dashed lineFaint span axis.
- Roots: wing-root fillets blending into the fuselage.

- Gear: wheel-well outlines in skinDeep under the wings near the gear mounts.
- Markings: a roundel on each upper wing at x ≈ ±3.7 and one on each lower wing (outer line ring, skinDeep ring, lineSoft ring, roundelCore centre, radius ≈ 0.5), in sunk-in flat discs seated on the skin.
- Tips: rounded wingtips with a small navigation light in accentCyan.
- Rivets: rivet rows in lineSoft along the spar and root.
parts.attaches: Roots start at wingRootL and wingRootR and bury 0.12 m into the fuselage. Ailerons ride aileronL and aileronR at the aileronHinge mounts. The main legs attach to the underside at gearAttachL and gearAttachR. The rest rides joint fuselage.

parts.builds:
The tail cone from tailRoot to tailTip (a tapering loft in skinBase with a skinShade belly and a rounded end) and all the empennage.
- Fin: an elliptical fin extruded in skinBase with a skinTop edge, carrying a broad rounded rudder on the rudder joint. The rudder has horizontal rib stripes in lineSoft, a trim tab, a white hinge line and a white outline.
- Tailplane: two elliptical tailplanes at y ≈ 1.47, in skinTop above and skinShade below, with leading-edge line strips, rib lines and rivet rows.
- Elevators: one on each side, riding elevatorL and elevatorR, with rib stripes, a small trim tab on the left and a line outline.
- Markings: a fin flash on each side of the fin, made of three stacked vertical stripes (line, skinDeep, roundelCore), a small rear navigation light in accentCyan at the rudder base, and a dashed lineFaint centre line on the fin.
The tail wheel and its strut belong to the gear part.
parts.attaches: The cone starts at tailRoot, flush with the fuselage rear face, and ends at tailTip. The stabs start at stabRootL and stabRootR, and the elevators hinge at elevatorHingeL and elevatorHingeR. The fin sits on the spine at finBase and ends at finTop, and the rudder hinges at rudderHinge. The tail wheel strut hangs from tailWheelMount, below the cone.

parts.builds:
The whole propeller assembly, on the propeller joint (axis +Z).
- Spinner: an ogive lathe from z = 3.5 (radius 0.34) to the tip at z = 4.6, in spinner with a lineSoft ring near the base, a thin line ring mid-way, and a faceted highlight stripe.
- Back plate: a skinDeep backplate disc at z = 3.5 to 3.56, with a ring of small metal bolts.
- Blades: three broad scimitar-shaped blades, radius 1.5 from the hub, twisted a little, at clock angles 180° (down), 60° and 300° from up. Each is skinBase with a skinTop leading edge, a lineSoft tip band, a white `line` leading-edge strip, and a tiny line serial stamp.
- Roots: a metalDark root cuff and a metal blade-root collar per blade.
The tip of the lowest blade clears the floor at y ≈ 0.2.
parts.attaches: The back plate sits flush on the fuselage front face at noseBase, centred on propHub. Spinner tip at spinnerTip.

parts.builds:
All the running gear.
- Main legs: two main legs in metal and metalDark, from gearAttachL and gearAttachR down to the wheel centres, splayed outward a little. Each has an oleo strut with a lineSoft scissor link and a brake line, plus a hinge pivot fairing at the wing.
- Wheels: two wheels riding wheelL and wheelR, each with a faceted tyre (tyre colour, radius 0.36, width 0.16), a metal hub disc, a skinDeep brake drum, a ring of bolts in lineSoft, a white `line` hubcap ring, and a few tread notches.
- Doors: an outer gear door hanging from each leg, in skinShade with a white outline and a skinDeep inner face.
- Tail wheel: a tail wheel riding tailWheel (radius 0.12, tyre colour, metal hub) on a tailStrut oleo from tailWheelMount, with a small fork.
The lowest points of the three wheels touch y = 0.
parts.attaches: The main legs top out on the wing underside at gearAttachL and gearAttachR. The wheel hubs are centred on wheelCenterL and wheelCenterR. The tail strut hangs from tailWheelMount (under the cone), and its wheel centre is tailWheelCenter.

spec.name: Spitfire Blueprint
spec.description: A Supermarine Spitfire Mk I at real size, built as a cyanotype blueprint: every surface is a flat Prussian blue, and panel seams, rivets, ribs and roundels are drawn on in white and pale cyan line-work.
spec.layout:
Single-engine low-wing monoplane, nose toward +Z, level attitude on two main wheels and a tail wheel, centred on x = 0. Extents: wingspan x = ±5.62, spinner tip z = +4.15, rudder trailing edge z = -4.97, propeller top y = 3.35. Only the main wheels and the tail wheel touch y = 0.

SHARED AIRFRAME FORMULAS (all parts must obey them so the pieces meet):
- Fuselage centreline height: y = 1.85 for z >= -0.9, falling linearly to y = 1.52 at z = -4.6. The propeller axis is y = 1.85, x = 0.
- Fuselage stations (z: centre y, half width, half height): 3.45: 1.85, .40, .40 | 2.9: 1.85, .45, .46 | 2.2: 1.85, .47, .50 | 1.9: 1.85, .46, .48 | 1.0: 1.85, .44, .52 | 0.2: 1.84, .43, .58 | -0.9: 1.82, .38, .50 | -2.0: 1.76, .30, .38 | -3.0: 1.68, .22, .30 | -4.0: 1.58, .15, .22 | -4.6: 1.52, .07, .12. Cowl = z 3.45 to 1.9. Rear fuselage = z 1.9 to -4.6.
- Wing planform (elliptical, semispan 5.62): chord c(x) = 2.5*sqrt(1-(|x|/5.62)^2). The quarter-chord line is the straight line z = 0.30. Leading edge z = 0.30 + 0.25c, trailing edge z = 0.30 - 0.75c. The wing is continuous through the fuselage as one piece from x = -5.62 to +5.62.
- Wing height: dihedral centre line y_c(x) = 1.25 + 0.098*|x|. Thickness t(x) = 0.05 + 0.32*(1-|x|/5.62)^0.8, thickest near 30% chord. Root top is about y 1.41 and root underside about y 1.09. Tip centre is y 1.80.
- Wing hinge line (ailerons and flaps) is at 70% of chord from the leading edge, z = 0.30 - 0.45c. Ailerons run x 2.9 to 5.0, split flaps x 0.75 to 2.8.
- Tail: tailplane centre y = 1.62, z from -3.7 (leading edge at root) to -4.5 (hinge), elevator trailing edge at z = -4.85, half span 1.67, tip rounded. The fin leading edge goes from (y 1.75, z -3.3) up to (y 3.0, z -4.4). The rudder hinge line runs from (y 1.75, z -4.55) up to (y 2.95, z -4.68). The rudder trailing edge is at z = -4.97, with a rounded top at y = 3.0.
- Landing gear: main wheel centres at x = ±1.12, y = 0.34, z = 0.40, tyre radius 0.34, tyre width 0.18. The leg runs from the wing underside at (±1.0, 1.2, 0.35) down to the axle. The tail wheel centre is at (0, 0.14, -4.02), radius 0.14, on a strut from the fuselage belly at (0, 1.38, -3.95).

STYLE (every part): cyanotype blueprint. The aircraft is solid Prussian blue in flat tones. Upward-facing surfaces use skinTop, side and leading-edge surfaces use skinMid, and undersides use skinUnder. Cavities (cockpit, wheel wells, exhaust holes, intakes) are skinDeep. All the drawing is thin white or cyan parts seated 1 to 2 mm proud of the surface: panel-line strips about 6 mm wide, rows of tiny rivet discs (r about 5 mm, 5 to 6 sides) at 8 to 10 cm spacing along seams, wing rib lines, hatch outlines and roundel rings. Draughtsman marks appear too: a dash-dot centreline of short lineCyan dashes along the top of the fuselage and across each wing, and small ruler ticks along the leading-edge spar line. The roundels are concentric flat rings (outer lineWhite, then lineCyan, then lineWhite, centre skinDeep). Faceted low-poly shapes; no gradients, one colour per part.

parts.builds: Merlin cowling and propeller, everything forward of cowlRear (z 1.9). (1) Cowl: loft or lathe through the cowl stations (z 3.45 to 1.9), skinMid with a skinTop upper half. Two long cowl-top bulges (gun troughs) run from z 3.2 to 1.9, with a small raised carburettor-hump panel on top at z 2.4 to 1.9. A skinDeep front opening ring at z 3.45 with an inner rim in lineCyan. (2) Cowl panels: three lineWhite ring seams at z 3.1, 2.6 and 2.2, a horizontal lineWhite seam on each side at engine-centre height, rivet rows along every seam, and four rectangular lineFaint access-hatch outlines per side. (3) Exhausts: six fishtail stacks on each side at x = ±(0.44 to 0.47), y 1.95 to 2.05, z 3.2 to 2.3, spaced evenly. Each is a short skinDeep tapered box with a steelLight collar, and the six stacks sit under a long lineCyan fairing strip. (4) Chin: an under-nose carburettor and oil intake scoop at z 2.2 to 2.9, y about 1.38, a skinUnder box with a skinDeep mouth and a lineWhite frame. (5) Spinner: a pointed cone/lathe from z 3.52 (radius 0.30) to the tip z 4.15 in spinner, with a lineWhite ring seam at z 3.7 and a skinDeep backplate disc of radius 0.34 at z 3.5. (6) Propeller on joint prop: a central hub, three broad blades radiating at 0°, 120° and 240° about the z axis from radius 0.28 to 1.5 (tip y = 3.35). The blades are flat, twisted extrudes, widest about 0.2 at r = 0.7 and tapering to 0.12 at the tip, in skinTop with a lineWhite blade-root band, and the outer 0.18 m of each tip is lineWhite. Each blade has a lineCyan centre-line strip and a small lineCyan stencil mark. Build the propeller and hub on joint prop, everything else on body. Keep clear of the face of the cowl; nothing else sits in front.
parts.attaches: Cowl rear edge meets the fuselage at mount cowlRear (z 1.9, same station: half width .46, half height .48). Propeller and hub are on joint prop at mount propHub.

parts.builds: Fuselage from cowlRear (z 1.9) to the tail cone end (z -4.6), including cockpit and canopy. (1) Main body: one smooth loft through the fuselage stations from z 1.9 to -4.6 (skinTop, skinMid and skinUnder via sectors or bands: skinTop on the upper 70° either side, skinUnder on the belly, skinMid between), with a turtle-deck spine behind the canopy and a dorsal fin fillet blending into the tail part's fin at z -3.3. (2) Canopy on joint canopy: a glass bubble from the windscreen (base mount windscreenBase, z 1.25, y 2.4) rising to apex canopyApex (z -0.1, y 2.62) and ending at canopyRear (z -1.35). Build a sloped front windscreen plus a bullet-proof flat front panel, a sliding hood with three lineWhite frame hoops and two longitudinal rails, and rear fixed glazing. Glass in glass, frames in lineWhite. (3) Cockpit visible through the glass: skinDeep tub floor, a seat at cockpitSeat in skinMid, a headrest armour plate behind the pilot in steelLight, a control column with a spade grip, an instrument panel at z 1.0 with several small lineCyan dial discs and a reflector gunsight (small ring glowing navGlow). (4) Panel lines: lineWhite strips for the cockpit door outline on the left side, circumferential seams at z 0.8, -0.6, -1.5, -2.4, -3.2 and -3.9, a lineWhite stripe running along the mid-height of each side, rivet rows on all seams, and a dash-dot lineCyan centreline along the top. (5) Markings: a roundel on each side at z = -2.4, y about 1.72, outer radius 0.30 (ring lineWhite, lineCyan, lineWhite, centre skinDeep), seated on the curved flank. Two-letter code in lineWhite block strokes (about 0.22 m tall) forward of the roundel on each side at z -1.6, and a small serial number on the rear fuselage. (6) Details: a thin aerial mast on the spine at z 0.6 with a lineWhite wire sweep to the fin, a small lineCyan ID light, a belly skinDeep access hatch outline, and a retracted-tail-wheel doorless slot at the belly z -3.95. Stay clear of the wing: the wing builder owns everything outside the fuselage skin, but the fuselage loft passes straight through the wing root.

subject: brutalistBlock
pitch:
Category: Architecture.
Subject: brutalist housing block.
Style: raw concrete brutalism.

spec.name: Brutalist Housing Block
spec.description: A raw board-marked concrete slab-block of 88 loggia apartments on massive tapered pilotis, with rear access galleries, three stair and lift towers, a glazed lobby, and a sculptural rooftop terrace, in the style of Le Corbusier's Unité d'Habitation.
spec.layout:
Static model, no joints. The long slab runs along X (x from -22.8 to 22.8, about 45.6 m wide) and is 14 m deep (z from -7 to 7). The front facade faces +Z. The slab rests on 5 m tall tapered concrete pilotis (y 0..5) and has 8 residential storeys above (y 5..29), then a roof slab (y 29..29.5) with a low parapet (to y 30.2) and the rooftop terrace on top (to y 34 at the mast).

MASTER GRID, which every builder must use. There are 11 bays of 4 m. Bay i (i = 0..10) spans x from -22+4i to -18+4i, so its centre is x = -20+4i. Bay edges, where the cross walls stand, are at x = -22, -18, -14, -10, -6, -2, 2, 6, 10, 14, 18, 22. Storey k (k = 0..7) has base y = 5+3k. Its floor slab occupies y = 5+3k .. 5+3k+0.35, and the finished floor is 5+3k+0.35. The storey top is 5+3k+3. The front face has loggias: the slab edge is at z = +7 and the recessed loggia back wall is at z = +5 (2 m deep). The rear face has open access galleries: the slab edge is at z = -7 and the rear wall is at z = -5 (2 m deep walkway).

Solid concrete core fill is at x ±21.6, z ±5, y 5..29, so there is no hollow behind the facade planes.

Stair towers: left tower centred at x=+10 and right tower at x=-10, each 5 m wide (x centre ±2.5) and z -11.5..-7, rising from y=0 to 31.4. A central lift tower sits at x -1.5..1.5, z -9.5..-7, y 0..31.0. All three abut the rear gallery edge at z=-7.

STYLE: raw béton brut everywhere. Large chunky masses, deep shadowed recesses, board-marked formwork lines (thin darker horizontal strips on big concrete faces), tie-hole dots, rain-stain streaks running down from slab edges and scuppers, and moss and rust at the base and under drips. Colour is rationed: Corbusier-style polychrome primary panels (red, yellow, blue, green, ochre, white) appear only in the loggia side walls and back panels, the rear doors and the gable mural. Windows glow warm in a scattered handful. Every surface is one flat colour, so build all details as small parts seated 1-3 cm proud of the surface.

PART COUNT RULE FOR ALL BUILDERS: many repeated identical pieces (bays, storeys, doors, ties, streaks) must be merged per colour with mergeGeometries after translating each copy into model space, then added as ONE part per colour with b.part(merged, color, { at: [0,0,0] }). This keeps the part count within each budget. Use SDK extrude, lathe and sweep for the sculptural pieces (pilotis, vaults, stacks, trees). Use rng(seed) for any variation.

parts.builds:
Ground level, y 0..5, under the slab, with the front plaza elements.

(1) Twelve tapered pilotis at x = ±22, ±14, ±6 and z = +4.5 and -4.5. Each is a chunky concrete column about 1.2 m wide at the foot flaring to 1.9 m wide at y=5, 1.4 m deep at the foot and 1.8 m deep at the top. Build them with extrude or frustumBox in the concrete colour. Give each a dark concreteDark plinth foot 0.3 m high, a bulky haunch at the top, 3-4 horizontal boardLine strips on each face, tie-hole dots, rain-stain streaks in concreteStain, and a moss patch at the foot. The end pilotis at x=±22 are wider (to x=±23, a 2 m wide pier) and serve as end buttresses.

(2) A raised glazed lobby box at x -4.5..4.5, z -3..3.5, y 0..4.3 on a 0.45 m high concreteLight plinth. It has a steel-framed glass front wall at z=3.5 with a mullion every 0.9 m, a central double door, a deep concrete surround frame, a lit interior (glassLit panes in places and glassDark in others), a roof edge in concreteLight, a bold mail-box wall in panelYellow and steel, and a black steel sign bar over the door.

(3) A projecting entrance canopy: a flat slab at x -6..6, z 3.5..9, y 4.0..4.4 in concrete with a concreteDark underside strip, held by two stout rectangular piers at x=±5.5, z=8.6. Hanging lamp discs (lamp colour) are set under it.

(4) Four wide concrete steps from z 3.5 to 9.5, each 0.12 m high, in concreteLight with shadow risers, plus concrete cheek walls.

(5) Two glazed shop or community units at x ±(8..13), z -3..3, y 0..3.6. Each has steel mullions, a coloured fascia (panelRed on the left unit, panelBlue on the right), and a canopy slab.

(6) Low concrete planters along the front at z 6.5..8, x ±(8..20), with soil tops and planterGreen shrub blobs. Add a few bollards, 2 lamp posts (steel with lamp heads), and a bike rack in steel.

Stay clear of the slab and rear zone. Tower bases belong to the back part.
parts.attaches: Pilotis tops end at podiumTop (y=5), where the frame's first floor slab begins. The entrance and steps are centred on the entrance mount. Rear pilotis stop at z=-5.4, short of the back part's towers (z < -7).

parts.builds:
The structural concrete skeleton of the residential slab from y=5 to y=30.3.

(1) Eight floor slabs, k=0..7, each x ±22.6, z -7..7, y 5+3k .. 5+3k+0.35, in concrete. Add a thin boardLine strip along each front and rear fascia, and a darker shadow groove line under the slab edges.

(2) The roof slab: x ±22.8, z ±7.1, y 29..29.5, in concreteLight, with a shadow underside strip.

(3) Ten interior cross walls at bay edges x = -18, -14, ..., 18 (thickness 0.4, z from -5 to 7, y from the slab top to the next slab bottom). Merge them. The tops, bottoms and inner faces in the loggias get boardLine strips every 0.3 m.

(4) Two gable end walls, 0.8 m thick (x from 21.8 to 22.6 on the left, mirrored on the right), z -7..7, y 5..29.5. Give them vertical ribs 0.2 m proud at z = every 1.4 m, in concreteDark. They also carry boardLine horizontal courses, a grid of tieHole dots, tall dark slit windows (shadow colour, 0.3 x 3 m) at z=±5.5 on a few storeys, and a big abstract relief mural on each outer face at x=±22.65: z -4..4, y 8..26, made of 5-6 thin plates and one disc in panelRed, panelYellow, panelBlue and panelWhite in modulor-like composition.

(5) The solid core fill block: x ±21.6, z ±5, y 5..29, in concreteDark. Merge pieces freely.

(6) The roof parapet: walls 0.4 thick and 0.7 high (y 29.5..30.2) around the perimeter at z=±6.8 and x=±22.4, with a concreteLight cap strip, a moss strip on top, and 6 chunky square scuppers (0.4 x 0.4 x 0.6) projecting from the front and rear parapet faces at x = ±4, ±12, ±20, each with a long rain-stain streak running down the fascia in concreteStain, to about 1.5 m.

(7) Weathering: vertical stain streaks and a few rust drips under scuppers and slab edges, in concreteStain, rust and moss.

parts.builds:
Everything in the 88 front loggias: bays i=0..10 and storeys k=0..7, in z 5..7.05 on the +Z side. Use the master grid. Let b0 = 5+3k+0.35. Merge repeated pieces per colour.

(a) A balcony parapet panel across each bay front: x edge±0.2, z 6.8..7.0, y b0..b0+1.0, in concrete with a concreteLight cap strip, and 2 boardLine lines. A few parapets (rng seed 11, about 1 in 6) carry a planter box, soil plus planterGreen blobs on top.

(b) Polychrome side walls: on the cross wall faces inside each loggia, thin 0.05 panels at z 5..6.8, y b0..b0+2.7. Each bay gets its left or right side wall painted, and alternate bays use the other side, in a rng-picked colour from panelRed, panelYellow, panelBlue, panelGreen, panelWhite and panelOchre. The other side stays bare concrete.

(c) Back wall of each loggia (z=5): a recessed panel 3.3 x 2.6 m (z 5.0..5.06) in concreteLight or a polychrome colour (about 1 in 3 bays, rng).

(d) A window and door set into the back wall: a window 2.0 wide x 1.4 high at x = bay centre - 0.7 with a sill at b0+0.9, in a steel frame 0.06 proud (z up to 5.12) with a glass pane (glass colour; about 1 in 8 panes use glassLit as lit windows, and a few glassDark). A balcony door 0.9 x 2.2 at x = bay centre + 1.2, in a steel frame with glass. Add steel mullions.

(e) Sunscreen details: on storeys 5-7 of every other bay, a deep concrete brise-soleil of 3 horizontal blades (z 6.4..7.0 deep, 0.08 thick, 3.4 wide) under the slab above. Add a vertical concrete fin (0.15 x full height x 0.8 deep) at the centre of every 4th bay.

(f) Fine details: small lamp discs (lamp colour) beside the doors, a few hanging laundry or plant pots as tiny colour boxes, and occasional dark shadow slabs lining the loggia ceilings (shadow colour, 3.6 x 0.02 x 2).

Do NOT rebuild the slabs or cross walls (the frame owns them).

The whole rear side, z from -5 to -11.5, y 0..31.8.

(1) The rear access galleries on all 8 storeys. The walkway is the frame's slab. This part builds the 0.3 thick parapets at z -6.95..-6.65, y b0..b0+1.1, in concrete with a concreteLight cap and a steel rail on top. (3) The two stair towers at towerL and towerR: x centre ±10, width 5, z -11.5..-7, y 0..31.4, in concrete with a boardLine pattern every 0.3 m, tie-hole grids, and stain streaks. Each tower has a tall glazed slot 1.0 wide on the rear face (z=-11.5) running y 1..30, in glassDark, with thin steel diagonal stair stringers and landing lines visible every storey. Add concrete fins on either side. Each storey has a doorway opening, a dark shadow rectangle 1.2 x 2.2 in shadow, on the face toward the gallery at z=-7.02. Each tower has a roof cap slab at y 31.4..31.8 with a 0.3 overhang in concreteLight. A big block numeral built from boxes (1 on the right tower, 2 on the left) in panelRed stands at y 25..28 on the rear face. The ground floor has a steel double door and a canopy slab.

(4) The lift tower at liftTower (x -1.5..1.5, z -9.5..-7, y 0..31.0), narrower and taller, in concreteDark. It has a vertical glass slit window in glassDark and one panelYellow band on its upper stretch, a roof overrun slab, and a ground-floor lift door.

(5) Moss and rust at the tower footings, a few rainwater down pipes (steel) running full height at x = ±16 and ±4 along the rear wall, and stain streaks.

spec.name: Brutalist Housing Block
spec.description: A raw board-marked concrete housing slab in the Unité d'Habitation tradition: seven storeys of deep loggias on chunky pilotis, a separate stair and lift tower, and a sculpted roof terrace with chimneys, a gym vault and a paddling pool.
spec.layout: Static architecture, 48 m wide (x), 34 m tall (y) and 20 m long (z, from -11 at the back to +9 at the front). The long main facade faces +Z. From the ground up: a thin plaza slab (y 0 to 0.25); a forest of massive tapered concrete pilotis (y 0 to 5) with a glazed lobby between them in the middle; the slab block itself (x -24..24, z -7..7, y 5..27, seven storeys of 22/7 m each, floor lines at y = 5 + 22/7 * k for k = 0..7); on the front a 2 m deep egg-crate of loggias (z 7..9) made of full-height fins and projecting floor slabs, each cell holding a recessed window and a coloured infill panel; a free-standing stair and lift tower against the back (x 14..22, z -11..-7, y 0 to 34) that rises 7 m above the roof; and a sculpted roof terrace (y 27 to 31) with chunky ventilation chimneys, a curved gym vault, a pool and a parapet. The style is raw concrete everywhere: heavy chamfer-free blocky masses, board-marked formwork lines (thin darker or lighter strips as small parts), staining under every ledge, and a few saturated primary-colour panels (red, yellow, blue, green) as the only accents. The silhouette is a long horizontal slab on legs with one tall vertical tower, and the whole thing reads as heavy and monolithic. No glossy surfaces. Windows are dark glass, and about one in five glows warm yellow.

parts.builds: Everything at ground level under the slab. A thin plaza slab (x -24..24, z -7..9, y 0 to 0.25) in concreteDark with paving joints as thin boardMark strips. Two rows of massive pilotis at z = -4.5 and z = +4.5, at x = -22, -14, -7, 7, 14, 22, each tapering from 2.6 m wide at the base to 1.6 m wide at y 3, then a chunky tapered 'foot-to-capital' shape up to y 5, with a pronounced squat blocky look. They are board-marked: thin horizontal darker and lighter strips every 0.4 m on the faces, plus stain streaks (concreteStain) in a tall thin box below the caps and mud at the feet. Extra heavy twin piers at x = ±24 on the end walls. Between x = -4 and 4 sits a recessed glazed lobby (z -3 to 5, height to y 4.4) with a dark glass front, steel mullions, a lit warm interior band (glassLit), a deep cantilevered concrete entrance canopy (z 5 to 8, y 4.2 to 4.7, concreteLight with a rust edge strip), a wide stepped approach (3 steps) and a side ramp with steel handrails, plus a letter-number emblem plaque 'B1' built from small parts in panelYellow next to the door. Add three rows of ribbed soffit beams (long thin boxes in concreteMid) hanging under the slab (y 4.6 to 5), two bike racks and two bench slabs, and two bollard lamps with lampWarm tops. Everything is made from primitives: boxes, tapered frustums, cylinders.
parts.attaches: Pilotis tops end exactly at pilotisTop / slabUnderside (y 5) where slabBody starts. The plaza top is plazaTop (y 0.25). The lobby sits at lobbyCentre. The tower stands separately at z < -7 and its foot is the tower part's.

parts.builds: The main concrete mass of the slab and its flanks: a core box x -24..24, z -7..7, y 5..27 in concreteMid (the front loggia part builds on its face at z = 7). The rear facade (z = -7) has a horizontal strip-window band on every storey (dark glass, thin steel mullions every 2 m, a few windows in glassLit) with projecting 0.3 m concrete sills and lintels in concreteLight, and a recessed shopping-street level on storey 4 (y 14.4 to 17.5) where the facade steps back 0.8 m behind a continuous glazed band with panelWhite shopfront boards. A slightly proud horizontal floor-edge band (0.3 m high, 0.1 m proud, concreteLight) at each floor line on the rear and ends. Top edge: a heavy 0.5 m concrete cornice ledge all round at y 26.5 to 27 (concreteLight). The inner joint with the tower on the rear face between x 14 and 22 is left plain: a recessed vertical slot (shadowSlot) 0.2 m wide at x = 14 and x = 22 on z = -7.
parts.attaches: Sits on pilotisTop (y 5). Its front face (z = 7, slabFrontFace) carries the frontFacade part, so keep the front face a plain concreteMid plane. Its back face (z = -7, slabBackFace) meets the tower part at towerJointToSlab. Its top (y 27, roofDeck) carries the roof part.

parts.builds: The egg-crate loggia facade covering the entire front (z 7 to 9, y 5 to 27, x -24..24): 13 full-height vertical fins at x = -24 + 4*k for k = 0..12 (0.5 m wide, 2 m deep, concreteLight, board-marked with thin strips, with the fin edges slightly darker at the soffit); 8 projecting floor slabs (z 7 to 9, 0.35 m thick) at the floor lines y = 5 + 22/7*k for k = 0..7 in concreteMid with a lighter front-edge strip; each slab has a thin steel railing (a top rail and a few posts) along its front edge z = 8.9, merged where possible. Use merged geometry per colour and bone for the repeated infills to stay in budget.
parts.attaches: Back plane at slabFrontFace (z = 7), flush with slabBody. Bottom at floorLine0 (y 5) over the pilotis part's canopy region; top ends at y 27 under the roof parapet. The fins' outer edge is frontBalconyEdge (z = 9).

parts.builds: The free-standing stair and lift tower behind the slab, x 14..22, z -11..-7, y 0 to 34 (height 34 m is the model's tallest point). Seven small cantilevered landings or access gallery stubs project from the slab-facing side of the tower at each floor line y = 5 + 22/7*k, built as short concrete bridges (x 16..20, z -7 to -7.001 stubs, 1.2 m deep platforms on z -7 to -8) with steel railings, and the entrance on the ground floor with a canopy, double doors in panelBlue, a big panelRed number '12' on the left side face, and a lamp. Left and right faces carry staggered square window punches (dark glass, concreteLight reveal frames). Rain stains below each ledge. A thin steel lightning mast with a red tip on the lid top.
parts.attaches: Its front face (z = -7) touches the slabBody rear face at towerJointToSlab; the landings stub into the slab at each floor line. Its foot is on the plaza level y 0 (a small paved step apron in concreteDark). Its shaft passes the roof deck at towerRoofLevel (y 27) and tops out at towerTop (y 34); the roof part stays at x < 14 or z > -7 and never overlaps the tower's box.

parts.builds: The sculpted roof landscape on top of the slab, y 27 to 31, x -24..24, z -7..7 (not inside the tower box). A continuous parapet of 1.0 m height (y 27 to 28) in concreteLight with a thin lighter coping strip on top and board-marked strips on the faces, with drainage scuppers (shadowSlot) and rain streaks. Terrace floor in concreteDark. Features: (1) a big curved gym or nursery vault (a half-cylinder shell lathe/sweep 10 m long, 5 m wide, peaking at y 31.0) near x -14, z 0, in concreteWarm with ribbed beams (thin boxes) every 1.5 m and a glazed end wall in dark glass and a door in panelYellow; (2) three chunky sculptural ventilation chimneys at x = -3, 3, 8 (tapered boxes with deep slots and a cantilevered cap, concreteMid, height to y 31, one with a panelRed band); (3) a rectangular paddling pool (x 10 to 13.5, z -4 to -1, recessed look with a rim of concreteLight and `pool` water slab, a few steps) and a shallow bench ring around it; (4) a sun-terrace with a running track made of thin curved boardMarkLight stripes on asphalt-colored paving (a flat rounded rectangle path) around x 0..8; (5) a staircase block up to the gym vault (stepped boxes); (6) a few planters with moss, three flagpole stubs or lamp posts (steel with lampWarm tips), skylight pyramids with glassLit panes near x = -20; (7) a rooftop water tank (a cylinder with steel bands) at x = -20, z = 2, height to y 30.6. All details must be seated on the deck; keep the lowest roof piece at y >= 27 and the tallest at 31.

spec.name: Calder Hanging Mobile
spec.description: An Alexander Calder-style hanging mobile: a cascade of four black wire balance arms stepping down from a ceiling anchor, each tipped and weighted with hand-cut flat sheet-metal lobes in red, yellow, blue and white on black.
spec.layout: The whole model hangs in mid-air; nothing touches the floor (the lowest shape bottom sits at y ≈ 0.82, the ceiling anchor plate at y = 2.40). spec.description: An Alexander Calder hanging mobile: a hair-thin black spine carrying five alternating balance arms with black counterweights, hung from a steel hook and ceiling plate, holding nine hand-cut flat leaves in bold primaries that float in mid-air.
spec.layout: A Calder mobile hangs in the air and never touches the floor: the top anchor (cream ceiling plate + steel hook ring) sits at y=2.70 and the lowest leaf bottom is at y=0.18. From the front (+Z): the hook and plate sit centred at x=0; a black spine rod drops 1.46 m down the centre. Five thin black balance arms pierce the spine at pivot collars, alternating direction: arm1 long to the LEFT (y=2.42), arm2 long to the RIGHT (y=2.14), arm3 long to the LEFT (y=1.84) with a second sub-arm branching further left from its tip, arm4 long to the RIGHT (y=1.52), arm5 long to the LEFT (y=1.24, the lowest). Each short side carries a black counterweight (ball or disc) that balances the long side; each long tip carries a hair-thin black string holding a flat, hand-cut Calder leaf in orange, yellow, blue, red or cream, one large black fan among them. All leaf plates face the viewer (+Z) with a slight y-rotation for life, and leaves sit at slightly different depths via the strings. The style is unmistakable Calder: razor-thin black rods and strings, flat organic cut-out shapes in primaries, black hardware, and perfect visual balance between weight and leaf.

spec.name: Calder Standing Mobile
spec.description: A Calder-style standing mobile: a black pedestal and curving stem carry a crown of sweeping wire arms from which three tiers of flat red, orange, yellow, white and black sheet-metal shapes hang in balanced suspension.
spec.layout: Front view (+Z): a low black pedestal disc sits on the floor at the origin; a slightly S-curved black stem rises 2.0 m to mount mastTop. From mastTop the wire crown sweeps one arm out left-forward to hookL [0.55, 1.94, 0.2] and one arm right-back to hookR [-0.5, 1.8, -0.1], with a short central branch bearing a small yellow triangle finial at the very top (~2.14). From each hook a thin vertical wire drop hangs the upper tier (canopy): on the left a big black leaf and a red petal, on the right a big white fan and a small orange disc; the drops continue down to pivotA (right-forward) and pivotB (left-back). The middle tier (midSwags) hangs from those pivots: an orange leaf forward-right and a black triangle behind it, a yellow half-moon and a small red disc to the left-back; the drops continue to pivotC and pivotD. The bottom tier (finials) hangs lowest: a large black blob-leaf on a balance arm with a solid counterweight sphere and a white disc at right-forward, and the model's boldest accent — a big red petal — with a yellow triangle and a single small cerulean disc at left-back. Lowest shape edges hover ~0.23 m above the floor; only the pedestal touches y = 0. Style on every part: nothing straight — every wire is one confident sweeping catmull curve in near-black; every shape is a flat cutout with visible 2-3 cm thickness so it reads as painted sheet metal seen both face-on and edge-on; hard-edged matte colours, asymmetric balance (heavy black mass left, bold red note right), black calligraphy lines holding coloured notes in the air.

The foot: b.lathe a low disc profile r 0.42, height 0.07, with a rounded lip and a shallow dome top, colour pedestal, resting on y = 0; on its top a small raised collar disc r 0.16, h 0.05, same colour, carrying a thin 2 mm white inlay ring (colour white) around its rim. The stem: b.sweep along catmull [[0,0.12,0],[0.025,0.7,0],[-0.02,1.35,0.02],[0,2.0,0]], radius [0.024, 0.015], colour wire — a gentle S-curve, never straight. At mastTop the stem ends in a tiny upturned hook: a half-torus (tube r 0.005, ring r 0.018, colour wire) opening upward, so the armature's attachment ring hangs in it; both parts build their meeting hardware at mastTop.

Front (+Z) view: an asymmetric pyramid of beams narrowing upward, with bright primary-coloured leaf silhouettes dangling at staggered heights and depths; thin black wire and hand-cut flat sheet-metal shapes in Calder's primary palette read instantly from any angle.

On the model's left (+X) arm2 hangs at (0.6,1.7,0). It is yawed about 40 degrees so it reaches forward and back (z -0.32 to +0.58). It carries a big red disc on its back end and a long wire from its front end down to the small lowest-tier arm4 at (1.29,0.9,0.58). Arm4 carries a tall black leaf and a small red ball. Arm5 carries a large blue disc at the back and a small black leaf at the front. The silhouette is asymmetric and airy, wide and sparse, with arms spread in x and in depth (z) so it reads in 3D from any side. Style: every arm is a thin wire rod (radius 0.006), the hanging wires are thinner (0.004), and every joint between a wire and an arm is a small tight loop (a thin torus or ring of radius about 0.015) with a tiny knot. Every shape is a flat sheet of painted metal, extruded about 0.012 m thick with a slight bevel, hung from one point on its upper edge through a small wire eyelet, and tilted or rolled a different amount (10 to 35 degrees) so the shapes catch the light unevenly. Each shape has a slightly darker thin rim strip or a pale highlight sliver as separate small parts, and a little black wire hook at its hanging point. Arm ends have tiny bead counterweights or small bent-wire hooks. Everything is flat colour and low-poly (6 to 10 sided wires and circles, 16 to 24 sided discs). spec.description: A kid in a homemade cardboard robot costume: a taped-up kraft box torso with drawn dials and a bottle-cap jetpack, a box helmet with the kid's real face peeking through a cutout window, cardboard tube arms with box mitts, and craft boots.
