spec.name: Captain Cardboard
spec.description: A stylized kid in a homemade cardboard-box robot costume: kraft box torso with a marker-drawn control panel, a box helmet with a taped visor window where the kid's face peeks out, an antenna, cardboard tube arms with mitts, cardboard boots, and a paper jetpack with zigzag paper flames on the back.
spec.layout: A kid about 1.3 m tall standing facing +Z, feet flat on y = 0, wearing a robot costume made of kraft cardboard boxes and duct tape. From front to back: the big cardboard torso box (0.74 wide x 0.58 tall x 0.50 deep, y 0.58-1.16) with its blue control panel, gauges, buttons and tape band on the front face; above it a 0.44 m cube cardboard helmet (y 1.14-1.58) with a taped visor window in its front face where the kid's real face peeks out - eyes, blush, fringe of hair, mouth - and a thin antenna with a red ball rising from the helmet top to y 1.86. Arms hang in a rest pose slightly out and forward: cardboard tubes from shoulder pads on the torso box down to round cardboard mitts at y ~0.73. Below the torso box the kid's own legs show: denim shorts, cardboard thigh guards with a bare-knee gap, red painted knee discs, shin guards, and chunky cardboard boots whose soles rest flat on the floor at [+-0.17, 0, ~0.15]. On the back, a smaller cardboard jetpack box with two toilet-roll nozzles and flat zigzag paper flames trailing down to y ~0.6. Every surface is kraft cardboard brown with lighter cut edges, corrugation fluting strips on vertical edges, duct-tape patches and straps, and marker-drawn gauges, buttons and stickers in crayon-bright flat colours.

parts.builds: The costume body: a big kraft-cardboard box worn round the kid's chest, 0.74 m wide x 0.58 m tall x 0.50 m deep spanning y 0.58-1.16, rigid on the body joint. Main box in `cardboard` with a `cardboardLight` rim strip along the bottom edge and thin vertical `fluting` strips (~8 half-round strips per edge) down the two front vertical corners to read as corrugated cardboard. Front face, all details seated 0.01 proud: a rounded control panel in `robotBlue` (0.30 x 0.22, centred [0, 0.92, 0.26]) with a `tape` border; on it a big gauge - a `panelWhite` disc 0.09 across with 12 tiny `ink` tick marks and an `ink` needle - plus a smaller `paintYellow` disc gauge beside it; two push-buttons below (a `robotRed` and a `paintGreen` cylinder, 0.025 across, 0.02 proud) and a small `paintGreen` switch lever. Below the panel a marker-drawn smiley: a `paintYellow` round sticker 0.10 across with two `ink` eye dots and an `ink` curve strip. A `tape` band 0.06 tall wrapping the box at y 0.66 with a `tapeDark` edge, a crossed tape 'X' repair patch at the lower front-right corner, and a few crayon squiggles as thin `robotRed` and `paintBlue` wavy strips flat on the lower front. Shoulder pads: quarter-disc cardboard pads (`cardboardLight`, 0.14 radius) on the box top corners at mounts shoulderL and shoulderR, each with a `bolt` stud on top. Collar: a `tape` ring 0.05 tall round the box top at mount collar, where the helmet sits. Side vents: three short `cardboardDark` slats low on each side. Bottom edge open with a short `cardboardDark` inner rim visible below the hips.
parts.attaches: Rides the body joint; its top edge meets the helmet at mount collar [0, 1.15, 0.02]; its shoulder pads sit on mounts shoulderL/shoulderR where the arm tubes root; its open bottom edge is above the legs part's shorts at mounts hipL/hipR; its back face is the surface the jetpack part presses against at mount backMount.

parts.builds: The costume head: a kraft-cardboard box helmet, 0.44 m cube centred [0, 1.36, 0.02] (y 1.14-1.58, z -0.20 to 0.24), rigid on the head joint; the kid's real face peeks through a visor window in the front face. Build the helmet as slabs, with the front face as four slabs around a window opening 0.26 wide x 0.17 tall centred [0, 1.385, 0.24]; frame the window with a `tape` border 0.02 wide. The kid's head inside: a rounded head sphere (`skin`, 0.105 radius) centred [0, 1.35, 0.06] riding the head joint, face turned to +Z; in the window show: two big eyes (each an `eyeWhite` disc 0.035 with an `iris` disc 0.02, an `ink` pupil 0.012 and a tiny white highlight dot), a `blush` disc 0.018 under each eye at its outer corner, a small `ink` nose dot, a fringe of `hair` tufts (5-6 small extruded triangular tufts) along the top of the window, and the mouth built as an upper lip strip on the head and a separate lower lip strip on the jaw joint at [0, 1.3, 0.1] so it can open. On the helmet: a thin antenna (0.008 rod, `bolt`) rising from the top at [0.10, 1.58, -0.02] to y 1.84 with a `robotRed` ball 0.035 on top; a crossed tape 'X' patch of two `tape` strips on the right side; a `paintYellow` round gauge sticker (0.06, `ink` needle) on the left side; two `bolt` studs on the sides; `cardboardLight` edge strips along the top edges and `fluting` strips down the front vertical edges; a small `hair` tuft poking out at the back bottom edge.
parts.attaches: Rides the head and jaw joints; its bottom edge meets the torso box top at mount collar [0, 1.15, 0.02]; its face sits inside the window so it reads from the front; nothing in front of the face.

parts.builds: Both costume arms: cardboard tubes in a rest pose hanging slightly out and forward. Upper arm: a tube (0.075 radius) from mount shoulderL [0.36, 1.13, 0] to elbow [0.52, 0.92, 0.07], and mirrored from shoulderR to [-0.52, 0.92, 0.07], riding the shoulder joints; forearm: a tube (0.065 radius) from each elbow to wrist [+-0.55, 0.73, 0.17] on the elbow joints. Each arm wears a `tape` ring 0.03 tall at the elbow seam, a `tape` cuff ring at the wrist, and a `bolt` stud on the shoulder cap at the mount. Mitts: rounded mitts on the wrist joints - a squashed sphere 0.095 in `cardboardLight` with a `cardboard` thumb nub on the inner side, a `cardboardDark` worn fingertip patch, and two short `ink` knuckle line strips. Details: a paper 'power meter' sticker on the left forearm (`paintYellow` rounded rect 0.07 x 0.05 with `ink` needle and tick marks), a `robotRed` painted stripe ring round the right upper arm, a `fluting` corrugation strip down the outer edge of each arm, and a small `tapeDark` repair patch on the right forearm.
parts.attaches: Tubes root at mounts shoulderL/shoulderR on the torso box's top corners, under its shoulder pads; they ride the shoulder, elbow and wrist joints; mitts hang free above the floor.

parts.builds: The kid's own legs in cardboard boots, from under the torso box down to the floor. Shorts: a `denim` band 0.12 tall round each thigh at y 0.50-0.62 under the box bottom edge, riding the hip joints at mounts hipL/hipR. Thigh guards: cardboard panels (0.10 wide, front and outer side) over each thigh from y 0.48 to the knee in `cardboard` with a `cardboardLight` edge strip; the knee shows through as a small bare `skin` patch 0.04 with a `robotRed` painted knee disc 0.055 riding the knee joints. Shin guards: cardboard slabs from knee to ankle with a `fluting` corrugation strip down the front of each. Boots: chunky cardboard boots on the foot joints - a box 0.13 wide x 0.14 tall x 0.22 long with a rounded `cardboardLight` toe cap, a `sole` slab 0.025 thick resting flat on the floor at y = 0 centred [+-0.17, 0, 0.15], a `tape` strap across the boot top with a small `bolt` buckle, and a `tapeDark` scuff patch on the toe. Feet point forward to z ~0.26.
parts.attaches: Rides the hip, knee and foot joints; the shorts tuck under the torso box's open bottom edge at mounts hipL/hipR; boot soles are the only parts touching the floor.

parts.builds: A homemade cardboard jetpack strapped to the torso box's back, rigid on the body joint at mount backMount [0, 0.95, -0.26]. Pack: a smaller kraft box 0.50 wide x 0.44 tall x 0.17 deep centred [0, 0.95, -0.36] (z -0.27 to -0.44) in `cardboard`, with a `tape` border round its top edge and a `cardboardLight` edge strip down its vertical edges. Back face: a `robotBlue` circle emblem 0.14 across with a `paintYellow` 5-point star on it and a thin `ink` outline ring, seated 0.01 proud. Nozzles: two toilet-roll nozzles (tubes 0.055 radius, 0.14 long) at the pack's bottom corners [+-0.16, 0.78, -0.38], angled down and outward, in `cardboardDark` with a `tape` ring where each meets the pack. Flames: flat paper cutout flames under each nozzle - an extruded zigzag flame 0.20 long in `paperOrange` pointing down-out with a smaller `paperYellow` flame inside it, trailing to y ~0.60, clearly paper, not fire. Two triangular fins (extruded, 0.14 tall, `cardboardLight`) at the pack's top sides, and two short `tape` strap loops on the pack's sides where it meets the torso box.
parts.attaches: Presses against the torso box's back face at mount backMount [0, 0.95, -0.26], fully behind the body box (z < -0.26) and behind the helmet's rear face; rides the body joint.

spec.name: Cardboard Box Robot Kid
spec.description: A six-year-old in a homemade cardboard-box robot costume: a box torso with a glued-on control panel, a box helmet with a face window and straw antennae, foil-wrapped tube arms with claw mitts, and a paper-cup-and-bottle jetpack.
spec.layout:
Humanoid, about 1.38 m tall including antennae, in a neutral A-pose. Arms hang about 35 degrees out from the torso, palms facing the body, claws open. Legs are straight and slightly apart. The model faces +Z, left is +X, and it is centred on x = 0. It reads as a child's craft project, not a polished robot.

FRONT TO BACK, TOP TO BOTTOM:
1. HELMET: a cardboard box (x +-0.17, y 0.93..1.23, z +-0.17) sits on the torso's neck hole. Its front panel has a square face window (x +-0.10, y 0.975..1.165) cut out. The kid's face sits 0.075 behind the window plane, so it is recessed and clearly readable from the front. Two straw antennae (y 1.23..1.38, x +-0.08) end in a foil ball and a bottle cap. A paper cup is glued on each side as an ear-cup, with a small LED dome on top.
2. TORSO: a taller box (x +-0.26, y 0.42..0.93, z +-0.18). The bottom is open, so the kid's legs go down out of it. The top panel has a square neck hole under the helmet. Each side has a round arm hole at y 0.84 with a corrugated cut-edge rim. The front carries a glued-on control board (about 0.30 w x 0.26 h, tilted 1.5 degrees) with a glowing screen, dials, bottle-cap buttons, toggles, LEDs and marker lettering.
3. ARMS: paper-towel-roll upper arms, foil-wrapped dryer-duct elbows, painted forearm tubes, and claw mitts (a palm box plus a thumb block and a finger block that can open). They start at the arm holes (x +-0.27).
4. BACK: a shoebox jetpack (z -0.18..-0.32) with two painted plastic-bottle thrusters, a vent and tape.
5. LEGS: blue jeans visible from y 0.42 down, foil-wrapped cardboard shin guards, and a cardboard foot box over each sneaker with the red toe-cap poking out the front. These are the only parts on the floor.

CARDBOARD CRAFT LOOK, which every part follows:
- Panels are thin slabs about 0.008 m thick, never smooth solids. Every cut edge shows a thin strip in cardboardEdge, and where an edge is big enough (arm holes, flaps, window frame) a second strip in cardboardDark or cardboardLight alternates with it to read as corrugation flutes.
- Packing tape is thin strips (width about 0.03, thickness 0.0015) in the 'tape' colour. They cross over seams and flap joints, sit a little crooked (+-2 degrees), and overlap with a visible end.
- Foil is wrapped around tubes in a few faceted rings alternating foil, foilBright and foilDark. Use low-poly rings (6 to 8 sides) so the crinkles read as facets.
- Painted details (red, blue, yellow) are flat panels, bands and discs laid on the cardboard. Black marker lines and letters are thin bars in 'marker', drawn slightly wobbly.
- Screens and LEDs are the only glowing parts (screenGlow, ledRed, ledGreen). Use the glow kit on them.
- Panels are slightly misaligned, with uneven flap angles, so it looks handmade.
- Everything uses flat colours from the palette. Small parts (buttons, tape, rivets, letters) are separate parts, seated on the surface and not floating.

SCALE CONSTANTS: kid height 1.15 m, head box 0.34 wide, torso box 0.52 x 0.51 x 0.36 (w x h x d), arm tube radius 0.055, thigh radius 0.045. The kid's head is slightly oversized and cute: skull radii about x 0.085, y 0.1, z 0.095, centred (0, 1.07, 0).

spec.name: Cardboard Box Robot Kid
spec.description: A grinning six-year-old in a homemade cardboard-box robot costume: a taped corrugated torso box with a marker-and-bottle-cap control panel, a box helmet with a face window and foil antennae, paper-tube arms ending in cardboard pincer claws, and foil-strapped shins over sneakers.
spec.layout: Front is +Z, the kid's left is +X, the model is centred on x = 0, and z runs from about -0.32 (backpack) to +0.26 (panel dials and toes). The kid is about 1.15 m tall and stands in a neutral T-pose with the arms out sideways, 5 degrees down, and the legs shoulder-width apart. From the floor up: white sneakers (y 0 to 0.08), blue leggings with cardboard shin and knee guards (y 0.08 to 0.50), and the TORSO BOX (x +-0.25, y 0.50 to 0.95, z +-0.18), which is open at the bottom so the legs come out of its hem. The HELMET BOX (x +-0.19, y 0.95 to 1.30, z +-0.19) sits on top of the torso box. A rectangular FACE WINDOW is cut in its front (x +-0.115, y 1.04 to 1.21), and the kid's round head with a big grin shows through it. Antennae (foil straws with caps and a spring) rise to y 1.42, and toilet-roll ear tubes stick out of the sides at x +-0.19 to +-0.26. The arms leave round holes in the torso sides at (+-0.25, 0.85) as paper-towel-tube sleeves with a segmented dryer-hose elbow, foil-wrapped forearms and a two-jaw cardboard pincer claw at x +-0.72 to +-0.86, open like a crab. The chest has a hand-built control panel with dials, bottle-cap buttons and glowing LEDs, and the back has a smaller cardboard backpack box with tubes and a foil vent. CARDBOARD CRAFT STYLE: every big surface is a plain box in brown corrugated tones, with thin darker edge strips and a few lighter or darker ridge lines for the corrugation. Packing-tape strips (lighter tan, slightly proud of the surface) cover seams and corners. Details are black marker lines, scribbles and hand-drawn shapes made of thin dark parts seated on the cardboard, painted accents in poster red, blue, yellow and green, crinkled low-poly foil (faceted, 6 to 8 sides), hot-glue blobs, and slightly wonky craft proportions (small 1 to 3 degree tilts on added pieces, never on the main boxes). Only LEDs, the claw eye-lights and the panel screen glow.

parts.builds: Both legs, mirrored, and the sneakers. Thighs and shins are thin tapered tubes in leggings blue (thigh radius about 0.06, knee 0.05, shin 0.045), bent with the hip, knee and ankle joints. Darker leggings knee patches sit on the front of each knee, and a few small marker-doodle stars and dashes in white and yellow on the thighs read as the kid's own drawings. Each shin has a cardboard shin guard: a thin curved box in cardboard with cardboardDark edge strips and corrugation ridges, held by two foil strips (foil) wrapped round the leg and tied with small tape tabs. A little red-painted stripe and a marker 'bolt' doodle sit on the guard. The upper thigh disappears inside the torso hem at y 0.50, and a thin cardboardInner shadow collar can show where the legs meet the box. The sneakers are chunky low-poly white shoes about 0.09 wide and 0.24 long, from z -0.04 to 0.20, with a toe cap bump, a sole slab in sole colour with a dark tread line, two red velcro straps or a lace row of small white bars with red aglets, a red heel tab and a small red side stripe. Soles rest on y = 0, sunk at most 0.002.
parts.attaches: Top of each thigh enters the torso hem at mounts legTopL and legTopR (y 0.50, x +-0.09) and rides hipL/hipR, kneeL/kneeR, ankleL/ankleR and toeL/toeR. The torso part owns the hem; nothing here extends above y 0.52.

parts.builds: The main costume box, the bare cardboard shell, with no panel hardware. It is a box of x +-0.25, y 0.50 to 0.95, z +-0.18, in cardboard, built from a hollow-looking shell: thin walls with a cardboardInner rim at the open bottom hem (y 0.50) and a dark opening where the legs enter. Corrugated edges show as thin cardboardDark strips on all vertical corners and the hem, with a few shallow ridge lines (thin boxes in cardboardLight and cardboardDark) running across the front, back and sides. Packing-tape strips (tape colour, 0.01 proud) cover the vertical corner seams and run in an 'X' pattern over a patched corner on the back. The top has four folded flaps that frame the neck hole: front and back flaps lean outward at about 20 degrees and the side flaps are folded in, showing cardboardInner undersides and tape tabs. Two round arm holes in the side faces at (+-0.25, 0.85) have a marker-outlined ring and a cardboardInner collar of radius about 0.065. Over the shoulders go two shoulder-strap loops (tape and a tapeBrown string) that go up over the top flaps. A tapeBrown shipping-label rectangle with marker lines on the lower left side, a stamped 'THIS SIDE UP' arrow, a red 'FRAGILE' sticker, a few hot-glue blobs and some scuff patches in cardboardDark on the corners. Inside the neck hole, a dark ring shows the kid's blue-shirt collar (leggings colour). Everything sits on the box faces; the front face z = 0.18 is left clear in the centre rectangle x +-0.16, y 0.60 to 0.86 for the gadget panel.
parts.attaches: Sits on legs at the hem (torsoBase) and under the helmet at torsoTop / helmetBase. Arm holes at armHoleL and armHoleR; the arms start inside them. The chest panel mounts on torsoFrontFace and the backpack on torsoBackFace; both are built by the gadgets part.

parts.builds: All the craft hardware on the torso, built outside the torso volume only. FRONT: a control panel board of cardboardDark (about 0.32 wide, 0.24 tall, 0.02 thick, z 0.18 to 0.20) with a tape border, centred on chestPanelCenter. On it: a row of three round dials made of bottle caps (red, blue, yellow) with marker tick marks and a small needle bar each; a big central 'screen' of a black marker-framed rectangle with a glowCyan inner pane and a marker zigzag line; two rows of 4 small bottle-cap buttons (green, yellow, red, blue) with marker rings; a pull-switch made from a clothespin and a tapeBrown string; three round LEDs in glowRed, glowLime and glowCyan (glowing); a hand-drawn marker speaker grille of six thin parallel bars; a drawn heart or a smiley, a bolt-and-gear emblem and a 'B-07' style label made from thin marker bars, all seated on the board. SIDES: a rectangular foil-patched vent flap on each side below the arm hole at y 0.62. BACK: a backpack box (about 0.34 wide, 0.34 tall, 0.12 deep, z -0.30 to -0.18, centred on backpackCenter) in cardboardLight with tape corners and a lid flap, two foil-wrapped tubes (radius 0.03) bent up and over the top like exhaust pipes with foilDark rings, a round foil dish or vent, a red painted 'ON/OFF' switch, a dangling curly cord (swept thin coil in marker) and two tapeBrown backpack straps that reach the shoulders over the top flaps. Small hot-glue blobs, tape tabs and marker scribbles on the back finish it.
parts.attaches: Panel back face sits flush on torsoFrontFace (z 0.18) at chestPanelCenter. Backpack front face sits flush on torsoBackFace (z -0.18) at backpackCenter. Side vents sit on x = +-0.25. Rides chest and spine joints. Nothing may block the arm holes at armHoleL/R (radius 0.07) or the neck hole.

parts.builds: The kid's head and the cardboard helmet box. KID: a round, slightly chubby head (radius about 0.10, centred on kidHeadCenter) in skin, a short neck in skinShade, ears, a small nose, rosy cheeks (mouth colour, subtle), two big eyes (white sphere, iris-coloured iris, black pupil, a tiny white highlight) set at x +-0.045, a thick brow pair in hair colour, and a wide open grin. The mouth is a separate lower jaw (rides the jaw joint) and an upper jaw/lip, with a mouth-colour interior, two small white teeth rows and a small tongue. Hair in hair colour: a solid cap plus a modest number of overlapping tufts and a fringe that sticks out above the eyes. HELMET: a box of x +-0.19, y 0.95 to 1.30, z +-0.19 in cardboard, built as thin walls with a cardboardInner rim round a rectangular face window (x +-0.115, y 1.04 to 1.21 on the front), with thick marker outline round the window and tape strips on corners and seams. A hinged cardboard visor flap above the window (rides visor joint) tilted slightly up, with a foil strip and a red stripe. Corrugated edge strips on every corner, ridge lines, tape X over the back seam, a marker mouth-grille pattern of five bars on the front chin area under the window, two drawn marker 'eyebrow' bars above and a red-painted 'B' on the forehead. EARS: toilet-paper-roll tubes (radius 0.05, length 0.07) on the sides at earTubeL and earTubeR, painted red on the left and blue on the right, with foil end caps and a marker spiral. ANTENNAE: two foil-wrapped straws (radius 0.008) from antennaBase at x +-0.07 leaning outward 12 degrees to y 1.42, one topped by a yellow bottle-cap disc and one by a red pom-pom sphere, and a small coil spring (thin swept spiral in foilDark) on one. A little foil dish on the very top centre. Hot-glue blobs where the antennae and ears attach.
parts.attaches: Neck base and helmet base sit on the torso top at neckBase / helmetBase (y 0.95); the helmet's bottom rests on the torso top flaps. The kid's head rides head and jaw; the helmet rides head; the visor flap rides visor; the neck rides neck. The face window faces +Z at faceWindowCenter.

parts.builds: Both arms, mirrored (left is +X), from the arm holes out to the claw tips. UPPER ARM: a paper-towel tube (radius 0.055) from x +-0.23 (inside the hole) to x +-0.45, in cardboardLight with a spiral-seam line in cardboardDark, two painted stripe bands (yellow and red), and a tape collar at the shoulder end. ELBOW: a segmented dryer-hose joint, five stacked thin rings or a ribbed tube (radius 0.05) in foilDark with foil highlights between x +-0.45 and +-0.50 around elbowL/R. FOREARM: a foil-wrapped tube (radius 0.05, low-poly crinkled faceting, 6 to 8 sides) to x +-0.68 with tape cuffs at both ends, three little rivet bottle-cap buttons in blue, and a marker 'wristwatch' band. HAND: a cardboard pincer claw, a palm block (box about 0.06 wide) at x +-0.69 to +-0.73 with tape, and two jaws made from flat extruded cardboard shapes (curved crab-claw outlines with a cardboardDark edge, a foil tip, and serrated marker 'teeth' ticks): the top jaw rides clawTop*1 and clawTop*2 and the bottom jaw rides clawBot*1 and clawBot*2, open in a V with tips near x +-0.86 and about 0.08 apart in y. A tiny glowLime LED sits on the back of each palm. Small hot-glue blobs and tape tabs at each join. Kid's skin shows only in a small gap at the wrist cuff (a skinShade ring).
parts.attaches: Starts inside the torso arm holes at armHoleL/armHoleR (x +-0.25, y 0.85); the collar sits flush against the box wall at x = +-0.25. Rides shoulder*, elbow*, wrist* and the claw* joints. Nothing is built for |x| < 0.23.

spec.name: Tulip Mill
spec.description: A stylized Dutch windmill in Animal Crossing proportions: a cream plaster tower on a stone plinth, a balcony gallery, a slate-blue onion cap with a tail-pole winch, four lattice sails, and tulips by the door.
spec.layout: The mill faces +Z. From the ground up: a chunky stone plinth (y 0-0.65) with a tapered cream plaster shaft above it (radius 1.05 at the base narrowing to 0.72 at y 3.35, axis through z=0); the arched front door and round-topped windows sit on the front face, with a cobble apron and tulips at the foot. A timber gallery ring wraps the tower at y 2.45 with a white-balustrade railing. On top sits a stepped slate-blue onion dome cap (y 3.35-4.55) with a gold finial and a small weather vane; the sail axle exits the front of the cap at the hub [0, 3.95, 1.05], and four lattice sails (blades 1.9 long) face the viewer, one pair vertical and one pair horizontal in rest pose, so the sail tips reach y 5.9 and set the silhouette's top. A stout timber tail pole runs from the cap's rear down to the ground behind the mill, ending in a windlass drum on a small A-frame - it reaches y=0, so the cap part also touches the floor. The style shows everywhere as chunky rounded shapes, a warm cream-and-terracotta body against the cool slate cap, white window frames, gold fittings, and little flat-colour flowers and trim seated on the surfaces.

parts.builds: Stone plinth plus the tapered plaster tower and its entrance, resting on y=0. Plinth: two courses of chunky rounded stone blocks (stone, with stoneDark inset rings as mortar gaps between blocks) from y=0 to 0.65, half-width about 1.3, corners rounded, with a chamfered top edge. Shaft: a smooth lathe/loft body from y=0.65 (radius 1.05) to y=3.35 (radius 0.72) on the axis x=0, z=0, in plaster, with a plasterShade band over the lowest 0.5 m of the shaft, a brick base course ring at y 0.65-0.78, and brick quoin stones (brick, alternating with brickDark) stepping up both front corners. Entrance on the front (+Z), centred on the doorFront mount: an arched door y 0.12-1.5, width 0.62, panelled in door with timberDark frame, a ring of brick voussoirs around the arch, a small gold ring handle, and a white doorstep slab. Windows: a round-topped window at y 2.0 and a smaller one at y 2.95, both white-framed with glass panes and timberDark sills; one small square white-framed window on each flank at y 1.6. Top: a flared plaster eaves ring from y 3.2 to 3.35 flaring out to radius 0.8, plasterShade on its underside, finishing flat on the towerTop mount at y 3.35.
parts.attaches: Plinth sits on the floor. Top rim meets the cap part on the towerTop mount; the front face meets the dooryard at the doorFront mount; the galleryRing mount sits inside this part's shaft at y 2.45 where the gallery wraps it.

parts.builds: The ring walkway balcony around the tower at y 2.45, wrapping the shaft at the galleryRing mount. Deck: an annular timber deck (top y 2.5, thickness 0.08) from inner radius 0.82 to outer radius 1.45, built as timber planks with thin timberDark gaps, supported by 8 carved timberDark brackets hugging the tower at even angles. Railing on the outer edge: 12 chunky timber posts (about 0.5 tall with rounded caps), a rounded timber top rail at y 2.98 and a mid rail at y 2.78, with small white balusters between them; every third post gets a small gold ball finial on its cap. On the front of the gallery, centred above the door, hang a white window-box with flowerPink blooms and leafGreen leaves spilling over its rim. Everything sits above the floor, inside the box.
parts.attaches: Inner edge hugs the tower shaft around the galleryRing mount; the deck does not touch the cap or the sails.

parts.builds: The onion dome cap, its finial and weather vane, and the tail pole with winch. Dome: a lathe onion dome seated on the towerTop mount at y 3.35, base radius 0.85, drawn as 4 stepped shingle tiers rising to y 4.35, alternating roof and roofDark bands, each tier's lower edge scalloped with small ridge bumps; a white trim band runs around the very bottom of the cap and a small round attic window (glass in a white frame) sits on the dome front at y 4.0. Finial: a gold ball (r 0.09) at y 4.5 on a short roof-coloured neck, topped by a simple weather vane at y 4.6-4.8 (a white arrow and tail on a gold rod). Axle exit: a white collar ring where the sail axle passes through the dome front toward the sailHub mount, and the hub-side bearing plate there. Tail pole (staart): a stout timber pole from the cap's rear at about [0, 3.6, -0.55] down to [0, 0.12, -2.0], with 4 short timberDark rungs, a small white rope coil (rope) around the drum, and a windlass drum (timberDark, radius 0.14) with two crank handles; the pole's lower end rests in a small A-frame of two timber posts with stone feet planted on y=0, so this part touches the floor.
parts.attaches: Dome base seats over the tower top ring on the towerTop mount; the axle collar opens onto the sailHub mount in front; the tail pole and A-frame stand on the ground behind the tower without touching it.

parts.builds: The four lattice sails on the sailHub mount at [0, 3.95, 1.05], facing +Z. Hub: a timberDark drum cylinder (r 0.17, depth 0.34 along z) with gold band rings on both faces and a small gold domed cap on the front. Four blades at 90-degree steps around the z axis, in rest pose one pair vertical (up and down) and one pair horizontal (left and right): each blade is a main spar (rounded timber box, 1.9 long, 0.16 wide, 0.07 thick) running from r 0.15 to r 1.9 from the hub with a rounded tip cap, carrying 7 evenly spaced cross-slats (timber), and 3 sail cloth panels (cloth, 0.05 thick, mounted slightly forward of the spar plane at z +0.04) filling the lattice with one gap left empty so the lattice reads; small white tie knots (white) at each panel corner. All blades share one construction, rotated around the hub. Lowest sail tip is at y 2.05, so nothing hangs below the floor and the sails are clearly above the gallery.
parts.attaches: Hub rides the sailHub joint exactly at the sailHub mount, in front of the cap's axle collar.

parts.builds: The doorstep scene in front of the door. Apron: a flat cobble doorstep from z 1.05 to 1.75 at the doorFront mount, width 1.6, made of flattened rounded cobble stones (alternating stone and stoneDark, top at y 0.1). Lantern post: a timber post 0.9 tall at [0.75, 0, 1.55] with a white-framed lantern box (glass panes) holding a warm glowing core (glow) under a small gold cap. Tulips: 3 tulips (tulipStem stems, leafGreen leaves, cups of tulipRed and tulipOrange) on the left of the apron and 2 on the right, plus a small leafGreen bush tucked at the plinth's front corner. All grounded on y=0.
parts.attaches: Apron sits on the floor against the tower's front face at the doorFront mount; nothing else in this part.

spec.name: Starry Mill
spec.description: A Dutch smock windmill in Animal Crossing style: a chunky brick tower with a flower-boxed gallery ring, a cream battened smock, a dark red cap and four lattice-and-cloth sails frozen in an X, its windows glowing warm.
spec.layout: The mill stands centred on x=0, front facing +Z. From the ground up: a tapered round brick tower (radius 1.35 at y=0 to 1.15 at y=1.55) with an arched plank door and stone steps at the front, small glowing windows, and cream mortar/trim bands; a wooden gallery ring wrapping the tower at y 1.55-1.78 (deck overhanging to radius 1.6) with a railing, brackets and hanging flower boxes; a cream plaster smock tapering from radius 1.05 at y=1.78 to 0.62 at y=3.35 with dark wooden battens and small glowing windows; a dark red dome cap y 3.35-3.95 with a cream rim band, a finial ball on top and a tail pole angling down to the back. At the front of the cap, a wooden hub at mount capHub carries four sails as one rigid assembly on the sailAxle hinge, resting as an X (blades at 45, 135, 225, 315 degrees), each a wooden spar with cream lattice frame and white cloth panels, sweeping in the x-y plane at z about 0.6. Style: Animal Crossing toylike chunky proportions, every surface one flat colour, bold trim bands, dot-like flowers in pink and yellow on green foliage, warm glowing window panes, faceted low-poly curves. Only the base part and its stone steps touch the floor at y=0.

parts.builds: The brick ground tower of the mill, y 0 to 1.55, riding joint mill. Build the tower as a faceted low-poly taper (b.lathe or a swept frustum, ~16 sides): radius 1.35 at y=0, radius 1.25 at y=0.8, radius 1.15 at y=1.55, main colour brick. Seat small darker brick patches (tiny slightly-protruding slabs, colour brickDark) scattered over the surface, denser low down and near the door edges. Add three horizontal cream mortar/trim bands as thin protruding rings (colour trim) at y 0.45, 0.95 and a wider one at y 1.45 just under the top. Front face, facing +Z: an arched door recess centred at x=0, the arch of trim-coloured stones (small wedge slabs around the semicircular top), door leaf colour door with three vertical plank seams as thin dark slats, a small round cream knob, the door filling roughly x -0.32..0.32, y 0.02..0.95. Two stone steps (colour stone) in front of the door, stacked blocks whose lowest faces rest exactly on y=0, with the top step meeting the door sill. Flank the door with two small round-arch windows at x about +/-0.75, y about 1.1: dark windowFrame surround, glass pane, and a slightly inset warm glow pane colour glow so the light reads as lit from inside. The tower bottom edge and the steps are the only floor contact of the whole model: everything rests exactly on y=0.
parts.attaches: Stands alone on the floor; its top face at y=1.55 is mount baseTop, which the gallery deck sits on and the smock rises from behind.

parts.builds: The wooden balcony ring that wraps the tower at y 1.55 to 1.78, riding joint mill. Build a flat annular deck: inner radius 1.16 (hugging the tower), outer radius 1.6, thickness 0.14, made of wedge-shaped plank sectors (about 16 planks, alternating wood and a slightly lighter wood tone by mixing wood with trim for a subtle two-tone, separated by thin woodDark gaps). A bold rim band of woodDark runs around the outer edge top and bottom. Under the deck, 8 small wooden brackets (small angled boxes, woodDark) step inward to the tower wall. On the outer edge stands a railing: evenly spaced square posts (woodDark) around the full circle, joined by a continuous top rail (wood) and a mid rail, with tiny cream trim caps on each post top for the toy look. Hang flower boxes on the railing at 6 angles (skip the exact front centre where the door sightline is): each box a small wooden trough (wood, woodDark rim) filled with a low mound of leaf-coloured foliage blobs and 5-8 round flower dots, alternating flowerPink and flowerYellow. Add two small hanging lanterns at the front-left and front-right posts (tiny dark frame, glowing glow pane) for warmth.
parts.attaches: The deck's inner top edge rests on the tower at mount baseTop (tower top y=1.55); the deck top face at y=1.78 is mount deckTop, where the smock stands.

parts.builds: The cream upper tower and the cap, y 1.78 to 3.98, riding joint mill. Build the smock as a faceted taper (about 14 sides): radius 1.05 at y=1.78, 0.85 at y=2.55, 0.62 at y=3.35, colour plaster. Cover it with vertical wooden battens: about 20 thin strips (colour batten) running up the surface, following the taper, plus 4 slightly wider corner pilasters for rhythm. A cream trim band (colour trim) rings the bottom at y 1.78-1.92 meeting mount deckTop, and a second thin trim ring sits at y 3.25 just under the cap. Windows: two small square windows at the front (z+), x about +/-0.45, y about 2.4, dark windowFrame surround, glass pane with a warm glow pane behind it; one round porthole window at the front, x=0, y about 3.05, same treatment with a cream ring trim. The cap at mount capSeat y 3.35: a dome (b.lathe) from radius 0.68 at its rim, curving up to a rounded top at y 3.9, colour cap, with a cream trim band at its bottom rim and a small ball finial (trim) on a tiny stem at the apex. At the front of the cap, a round wooden hub drum (colour axle, with a metal-toned ring of axle and a small cream centre cap) protrudes to z=0.55, centred exactly on mount capHub [0, 3.62, 0.55]; the sail blades mount into this hub but the hub itself is built here. At the back, a tail pole: a long wooden pole (woodDark) from the cap's rear angling down and back to about [0, 3.0, -1.1], with three small cross rungs, the classic cap-turning tail.
parts.attaches: Its bottom trim band stands on the gallery deck at mount deckTop (y=1.78); its dome sits on the smock top at mount capSeat (y=3.35); its front hub is centred on mount capHub where the sail assembly meets it.

parts.builds: The four sail blades, one rigid assembly riding joint sailAxle, whose origin is mount capHub [0, 3.62, 0.55] with the axle pointing +Z out of the cap. Build the blades in the x-y plane at the axle: at rest the four blades sit at 45, 135, 225 and 315 degrees (an X). Each blade: a main wooden spar from radius 0.1 to 1.45 out from the hub (colour sailFrame, a shallow-tapered frustum box about 0.34 wide at the root narrowing to 0.24 at the tip, lying flat in the sail plane with a little thickness); 4 crossbars (sailFrame) spaced evenly along it at right angles to the spar; and between the crossbars, alternating white cloth panels (colour sailCloth, thin flat quads with slightly rounded corners, giving a puffy patchwork look) and open lattice gaps, so each blade reads as 3 cloth patches with cream framing. Add a small cream tip cap on each blade end and a tiny dot detail (sailFrame stud) at the outer end of each crossbar. Give every blade exactly the same construction, only rotated about the axle, so the assembly is perfectly symmetric; keep all geometry within z 0.42..0.72 so the blades sweep clear of the smock surface (which bows out to z about 0.8 at its widest) and of the cap dome.
parts.attaches: Roots into the hub at mount capHub, riding joint sailAxle so the whole assembly can spin; at rest the blades form an X in the x-y plane in front of the smock and cap.

spec.layout:
Static architecture, +Y up, front +Z, x = 0 centred, z from -1.65 to +2.15. A stylized toy windmill ~5.5 m tall: fat rounded silhouettes, flat-shaded 10-segment facets on the round bodies, bold flat colours, warm glowing windows, zero grime.

Front to back: a 3-stone stepping path (z 1.25/1.55/1.85) leads to a blue split Dutch door with cream frame on the tower front; a lantern hangs beside the door; one warm-glow window sits on the tower front at y 1.25 and two more on the tower sides. The round brick tower (y 0-2.2, r 0.98 at base with a bulging plinth y 0-0.06, r 0.90 at y 0.25, tapering to r 0.70 at y 2.2; r(y) = 0.90 - 0.205*(y-0.25)/1.95 between) rises through a grass mound (dome r 1.6, h 0.32). A wooden upper storey (y 2.18-3.0, r 0.72 to 0.62) is girdled by a narrow walkway: deck ring r 0.60-1.02 at y 2.52-2.60, 12 picket posts at r 0.94 (y 2.60-2.88), mid-rail y 2.66-2.69, top rail y 2.84-2.90, 8 brackets underneath, two flower boxes on the deck at (±0.566, y, 0.566), one small window on the front at (0, 2.80, 0.665). A squat thatched dome cap (y 3.0-3.82, r 0.70 bulging to 0.74 at y 3.12 then closing to 0.10 at y 3.78) wears 4 dark thatch bands, an eaves ring with a fringe of little cones, and a cream finial ball at (0, 4.0). A square wooden windshaft (0.14 across) runs from inside the dome front to an iron hub at [0, 3.6, 1.1]; four sail units sweep the vertical XY plane at z = 1.1 (canvas centred at z 1.18): whips 1.9 long along ±X and ±Y with crossbars at r 0.5, 1.0, 1.5 and canvas panels r 0.55-0.98 and 1.02-1.48; the bottom sail tip hovers at (0, 1.7, 1.1) just in front of the door lintel, the top tip reaches y 5.5, the side tips x ±1.9. A wooden tail pole runs from the cap rear (0, 3.45, -0.45) down to a short post standing on the mound at (0, ~0.1, -1.5), with 4 ladder rungs and a small wheel (r 0.17) at its lower end, behind the mill.

Animal Crossing tone on every part: brick tower in warm terracotta with cream mortar bands and quoins, cream trim, glowing amber window glass, golden thatch, bright grass with pink/yellow tulips, daisies and a bush. The mound, path, flowers and bushes are simpler than the windmill itself and sized to its footprint.

spec.name: Dutch Windmill
spec.description: A cozy Animal Crossing-style Dutch tower windmill: a tapered octagonal terracotta brick tower with a wooden gallery and stairs, a mint boat-shaped cap with a weathervane and tail pole, and four cloth-and-lattice sails in a plus shape on a spinning rotor.
spec.layout: Units are meters. +Z is the front, with the door, the sails and the stair foot. The sails sit in the plane z=3.6, so the cap is in the middle and the tail pole slopes down behind it. Everything is centred on x=0 and rests on y=0 at the stone plinth, the gallery stairs and the barrels. The tower is an 8-sided tapered octagon with flat faces toward +Z, -Z, +X and -X. WALL RULE shared by every part: the apothem (centre to flat face) at height y is A(y) = 2.30 - 0.1316*(y-0.5), from A(0.5)=2.30 to A(6.2)=1.55. The front face is z=A(y), the left face is x=+A(y) and the right face is x=-A(y). Anything seated on a wall sits at A(y)+0.01. The octagon tower builder must make its flat faces land exactly on these values (the circumradius is apothem*1.0824; if an 8-segment lathe puts vertices on the axes, spin it 22.5 deg). A plinth ring of apothem 2.65 runs from y=0 to 0.5. The cap has a rounded boat-shaped dome over the tower top, about 1.8 m in radius and elongated in z, from y=6.2 to 8.0. The rotating hub is at [0,7.2,3.6]. The sails reach radius 4.2 from the hub in a plus shape, so the tips are at y=11.4, y=3.0 and x=+-4.2. Proportions are chunky and toy-like, with a slightly bulbous round-looking cap. Nothing is thinner than 0.1 m, so the thinnest bars stay readable, and edges look soft because of wide trim bands, bevel-like stacked rims and pill shapes. STYLE (Animal Crossing): warm pastel flat colours, a simple base shape with little cute details on top, and a hand-made crafted feel with wooden pegs, planks, patches and flower boxes. Colours go warmer on top and cooler or darker below, with moss and mud only at the plinth. Facets are low (8 to 12 sides). Every detail is a small separate part in its own colour: dark-outline layer, main colour, highlight. Lantern glass and windows use the glow kit sparingly (lanterns warm yellow, window panes a faint blue glow). No ground slab or scenery beyond the listed items.

parts.builds: The brick tower and plinth. (1) An octagonal stone plinth with apothem 2.65 from y=0 to 0.5, in stone, with a darker stoneDark course on its lower 0.15 and small moss patches on its upward faces and at the corners. A few rounded boulders or flagstone blocks at the foot are fine. (2) The tapered octagonal tower body from y=0.5 to 6.2 following the WALL RULE A(y) exactly, in brick. Brick detail: thin brickDark mortar bands every 0.3 m as shallow octagonal ring plates, alternating lighter and darker brick pads (brickLight) as small seated rectangles on every face in a staggered brick pattern (at least 3 rows on each of the 8 faces, kept low in count), brickDark shaded corner edges, and eight thin pilaster strips up the corners in brickLight. (3) A plaster whitewash band from y=0.5 to 0.9 around the base and a wider plaster cornice at the top (y=5.95 to 6.2, apothem 1.55 to 1.75) with a stepped plasterShade underside. (4) Two iron tie-rod anchor plates (small plaster-ringed iron discs) on the front face at y=5.2, x=+-0.9. Do not build the door, windows, gallery or cap.
parts.attaches: Plinth sits on y=0. The tower top meets the cap at towerTop/capBase. The doorBase, galleryFloor and gallery door mounts lie on its surface. Rides joint tower.

parts.builds: Everything seated on the front and side walls below the cap, using the WALL RULE. (1) The front door at doorBase: a plaster surround 1.3 wide and 1.9 tall with a rounded arch top (stacked slab or lathe half-disc). Inside it are two door leaves of doorRed planks with doorRedDark plank seams, a brass handle and hinge straps in iron, a rounded wood step in stone, and a small wooden awning of woodLight with woodDark supports above. (2) Three windows on the front wall: two at y 4.4 to 5.4, x=+-0.75, and one round attic window at y=5.7, x=0, with a plaster frame, glass panes with a glassLight highlight and a cross mullion in woodDark. Each has shutterTeal shutters, each with a heart or diamond cutout in plaster, and a woodDark flower box under it with flowerPink and flowerYellow blossoms and leaf buds. The windows are small and the shutters big, so they read as cute. (3) The same style of one window at y 1.4 on the right (-X) and left (+X) faces and one at y 4.8 on the rear (-Z) face. Mind the gallery: nothing on the left (+X) face between y=3.05 and 4.4 near z=0, since the gallery builder puts its door there. (4) A hanging wooden sign bracket to the right of the door at [-1.35,2.1,2.12+] holding a little board with a simple bread-loaf or windmill emblem in brass and plaster. (5) Props at the door: two barrels (woodDark bands, wood staves) at [-1.45,0,2.9] and [-1.9,0,2.5], and two plump sacks (sack, rope tie) at [1.35,0,2.8] and [1.8,0,2.55]. A potted tulip or two is fine, using the flower and leaf colours. Everything stays within +-2.4 in x and below y=5.9.
parts.attaches: Seated on the walls of towerBody by the WALL RULE; the door stands on the plinth/floor at doorBase (barrels and sacks rest on y=0). Rides joint tower.

parts.builds: The wooden stage gallery and stairs. (1) An octagonal ring floor at galleryFloor y=2.9 to 3.05 from apothem 1.95 out to 3.0, in wood, with plank seams as thin woodDark strips and a darker rim band. (2) Eight diagonal wooden brackets (woodDark) under the floor, from the wall at y 2.1 out to the ring edge at y 2.9. (3) The railing: posts every octagon corner and mid-edge (woodLight posts with brass-capped tops, 0.12 square, 0.9 tall to y=4.0), two horizontal rails (top and mid) in wood, with a gap for the gate at the stair top at +X, z -0.1 to 0.7. (4) The left-side (+X) gallery door on the wall at galleryDoor (y 3.05 to 4.4, 0.8 wide) in doorRed with a woodDark frame, a small brass knob, and a tiny plaster-framed arch. (5) Stairs on the +X side: a wooden staircase 0.9 wide centred at x=3.45, rising from stairBottom (z=3.2, y=0) to stairTop (z=0.3, y=3.0) with about 12 treads in woodLight and risers in wood, two woodDark side stringers, and a railing on the outer side (+x edge, x=3.9) with posts and a handrail, ending at the gallery gate. Two stone feet blocks at the bottom. (6) Two hanging lanterns (iron cap, lanternGlow glass cube with glow, brass ring) from gallery posts at the front corners, y 3.7, and one at the stair foot post. (7) A coil of rope (rope-coloured stacked torus pieces) and a small woodDark hook on the rail near the back.
parts.attaches: Ring floor butts the tower wall at galleryFloor, per the WALL RULE; the gallery door sits on the wall at galleryDoor; stairs land on y=0 at stairBottom and meet the gate at stairTop. Rides joint tower. It must stay clear of the sail plane z>=3.45 (the stair foot ends at z=3.2).

parts.builds: The turning cap and tail. Rides joint cap. (1) A base ring (plaster, apothem about 1.75, y 6.2 to 6.45) and an eave ring of roofMintDark at y 6.45 to 6.7, radius 1.9. (2) A boat-shaped domed roof from y=6.5 to capTop y=8.0, made of roofMint: a lathe or loft squashed to x radius 1.8 and z radius 2.0, with its front more rounded and a ridge line running front to back. Add ribbed seams as thin roofMintDark curved strips (8 to 10 ribs), a roofMintLight highlight cap on top, and a scalloped (shingle-like) row of small rounded roofMintLight shingles around the eave. (3) A front gable face visor over the hub opening: a wooden beam frame (woodDark) around a round opening at [0,7.2,1.9], with a plaster collar. (4) Two round dormer windows on the sides at y 7.0, x=+-1.7 (plaster frame, glass pane, mint mini-roof). (5) A finial: an iron pole from y=8.0 to 8.6 with a brass ball and a small weathervane (an extruded rooster or arrow in brass, with an N/S cross bar) on top. (6) The tail pole: a long wooden beam (wood, 0.2 thick) from tailPoleTop [0,7.0,-1.7] to tailPoleEnd [0,1.2,-4.2], with woodDark rungs/ladder steps every 0.45 m, two woodDark bracing struts under it near the cap, a capstan wheel (woodLight spokes, woodDark rim, radius 0.4, horizontal axle) at tailPoleEnd, and a rope loop (rope colour) around the wheel. Do not build the windshaft, hub or sails.
parts.attaches: Sits on the tower top at capBase; the hub opening aligns with the windshaft (rotor part) on the line y=7.2, x=0, which exits through the visor at z=1.9. The tail pole's top meets the cap at the tailPoleTop mount. The wheel hangs clear of the floor. Rides joint cap.

parts.builds: The spinning sail assembly, riding joint rotor, with local rest layout as follows. (1) A windshaft: a wood cylinder (radius 0.18) from windshaftBack z=0.9 to z=3.9 along the line y=7.2, x=0, with woodDark iron-band rings every 0.5 and a brake wheel (a disc of woodLight with spokes, radius 0.8) at z=1.2, hidden inside the cap. (2) The hub at z=3.6: a plaster cylinder drum (radius 0.55, length 0.5), a brass cone spinner nose to z=4.4 (it ends at z=4.3), a woodDark ring and eight brass bolts around the drum. (3) Four sail arms at angles 0, 90, 180 and 270 deg in a + shape (up, left, down, right), each in the plane z=3.6. Every arm has: a main stock beam (wood, 0.18 square) from radius 0.5 to the tip at radius 4.2; a lattice sail frame that starts at radius 1.1 and ends at 4.1, 0.95 wide on the trailing side (counter-clockwise from the viewer's side, the same tangential side on every arm), with two long woodDark rails, a woodDark tip bar and rungs every 0.3; and sailCloth panels in the gaps: three or four stretched cloth panels alternating sailCloth and sailClothAlt, thin slabs seated on the lattice. Add a lighter woodLight leading board along the stock, a small iron tip cap, and two or three rope-tie details per arm. Every arm should be a recognisable cartoon blade, with joints between lattice and stock marked by small brass studs. The overall silhouette extends to exactly radius 4.2.
parts.attaches: The windshaft enters the cap visor (capRoof) on the line y=7.2, x=0; the hub is the rotor joint at the hub mount [0,7.2,3.6] and rides joint rotor. Sails must clear the gallery railing and the stair (they sit at z>=3.45 and the stair foot ends at z=3.2).

spec.name: Dutch Windmill
spec.description: A chunky, cheerful Animal Crossing-style Dutch tower windmill with a red-brick octagonal tower, a teal cap roof, a wraparound gallery, a tail pole and four cream-cloth lattice sails.
spec.layout:
Toy-like and chunky. Sides are 8-sided (octagonal), edges are beveled, and nothing is thinner than about 0.05 m. Palette is warm and pastel. Everything is centred on x=0 and the front is +Z.

From the bottom up: a stone plinth (r 2.1, y 0-0.5), then a tapering octagonal brick tower (r 1.9 at y 0.4 to r 1.3 at y 5.0). The lower tower is brick red. Above the gallery the tower turns cream plaster, with a wavy brick/plaster boundary at about y 3.1. A wooden gallery deck (r 2.6, y 1.0-1.2) rings the tower with a railing (top y 1.9). Three wooden steps lead down the front, from z 2.6 to z 3.2. The arched green door is on the front of the tower at deck level, y 1.2-2.5. Small round-topped windows with white frames and flower boxes sit at y 2.9 and y 4.1 on four faces.

On top is a teal cap roof. It is a short drum (r 1.5, y 5.0-5.5) with a dome above it up to y 6.9, plus a finial/weather vane to 7.4. The cap's front is slightly bulged and has a shaft opening. A long sloping wooden tail pole runs from the back of the cap (y 5.2, z -1.4) down to a small post and wheel at y 0.45, z -3.3, with a ladder rail and a rope loop.

The sail shaft exits the cap at [0, 5.7, 1.2]. A round hub/spinner cap (r 0.3) sits at z 1.75. Four sail arms (stocks) of length 3.8 m radiate from the hub, rotated to a rest pose of 45 degrees (an X shape, never straight up/down). Each arm carries a cream cloth lattice panel (0.9 wide, 2.8 long, starting 0.9 from the hub on the trailing edge) framed in wood with cross-bars and a golden trim strip. The sail plane is at z 1.95.

Small props (flour sacks, barrel, lantern, flower pots and tufts at the base) sit on the gallery and around the plinth. The whole model is made of flat-colour primitives. Style cues: puffy proportions, soft rounded tops on windows and door, warm light-coloured trim details, and small flowers and leaf tufts in clusters.

parts.builds: The turning cap roof, riding joint 'cap'. A drum at capBase: octagonal, r 1.5, y 5.0-5.5, in roofDark, with a roofLight rim ring at the bottom. Above it a dome (lathe, 8-12 segments, roof colour) from r 1.5 at y 5.5 to a top at y 6.9, with roofLight shingle rows (thin tapered stripes or overlapping scale bands) and roofDark seam ribs running up the dome. The front of the cap bulges forward with a rounded woodDark bay around the shaft opening at shaftExit (a ring r 0.45, iron inside as a dark hole, plus a woodWarm bearing collar). His right arm (model -X) is raised high behind his head gripping a big smith hammer with a steel head at y≈1.6, mid-swing; his left arm reaches forward so the tongs in his hand grip a glowing orange bar lying across the anvil face. Directly in front of him at z≈0.42 sits the anvil station: a wooden stump, the iron anvil with its horn pointing +X, the ember-hot bar on the face, and scattered tools (a spare hammer head, a horseshoe, tongs) leaning against the stump. Everything rests on a low stone flagstone forge floor box (z from -0.55 to 0.62) with dark grout seams, soot stains around the anvil, spilled coal lumps and hairline ember cracks glowing near the stump. The only glow comes from the bar, the ember cracks and spilled coals.

pitch:
Category: Humanoid character.
Subject: dwarf blacksmith at an anvil.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.

spec.name: Stormpeak Forge-Master
spec.description: A stocky Warcraft-style dwarf blacksmith stands hammer raised over an anvil on its stump, beside a coal-glowing forge on a stone workshop ring.
spec.layout: Faces +Z. The dwarf stands centred at x=0, z=-0.15: short massive legs planted apart on the floor, a barrel torso nearly as wide as it is tall, and the head (large, Warcraft proportions) from y1.24 to 1.9 with a tall braided beard spilling down the chest and a steel helm with brass horns. His right arm (world -X) is raised high and back holding a heavy hammer overhead; his left arm reaches forward-and-out to brace a fist on the anvil. The anvil sits on an oak stump at his left-front (x0.6, z0.6), a steel anvil with horn, hardie hole and glowing hot-strip on the face, with an iron-banded quench bucket and a pair of tongs leaning on the stump behind it. Behind the dwarf, the forge: a squat stone furnace fronting +Z, its hearth mouth a bed of glowing embers, with a tapering chimney rising to y2.25 capped in brass, a bellows bolted to its side and tools hanging from a front beam. The whole scene stands on a low circular ring of stone slabs (diameter about 2 m, height 0.14) with moss in the cracks and scattered ember specks; forge, stump and boots rest on y0 inside the ring. The Blizzard style reads in exaggerated proportions (huge shoulders, short legs, big head and beard), chunky faceted shapes, bold gold trim on steel and leather, and warm ember glow against cool grey stone.

parts.builds: A low round ring of workshop ground under the whole scene: 10 to 14 chunky stone slabs laid edge to edge in a circle of radius about 0.95 (use slabs or swept stones, flat tops at y0.14, slightly uneven heights), stone on top faces, stoneDark on sides and gaps; tufts and thin patches of moss seated in three or four slab cracks (moss); inside the ring the packed dark floor (ironDark, very low, or leave the slabs to enclose it); scatter 6 to 8 small ember specks (ember, tiny glowing octahedra or discs) and one or two fallen coal lumps (ironDark) near the forge side and one scorch mark (ink, thin flat disc) between dwarf and forge. Keep it simple: this is the base, not the hero.
parts.attaches: Rests on y=0 itself and is the floor for everything; boots read groundDwarf, forge reads groundForge, stump reads groundAnvil, all inside or beside the ring.

parts.builds: A squat stone forge furnace at z about -1.05 facing +Z: a rounded rectangular stone body (loft or stacked frustum boxes) about 0.9 wide, 0.75 deep, 1.15 tall, built from 8 to 12 visible stone blocks with staggered joints (stone, mortar lines as thin stoneDark inset slabs), a wide arched hearth mouth on the +Z face holding a bed of coals: an ember heap (ironDark mound) topped with 5 to 7 glowing coal chunks (ember with a few emberHot cores, glow applied). A tapering square chimney rises from the back of the body to y2.25 in 3 shrinking stone stages, capped by a brass ring and short flue (gold, with a thin emberHot glow rim under the cap). A heavy leather bellows (two wood boards, wood and woodDark, hinged on an iron pivot at the forge's -X side, leather skin between) angled down toward the hearth with an iron nozzle. A front beam (wood) across the hearth arch with 2 hanging tools: a poker and a shovel (iron rods with ironDark handles) hanging from iron hooks. Gold band across the hearth arch as trim. Glow the coals and the flue rim.
parts.attaches: Forge base rests on the floor at mount groundForge inside the ground ring; its +Z face looks toward the dwarf's back.

parts.builds: The anvil on its stump at x0.6, z0.6, plus its props. The stump: a turned oak trunk section (lathe or faceted cylinder) radius 0.2, height 0.45, wood with vertical woodDark bark streaks and a ring of growth ridges, standing on y=0. The anvil itself on top of the stump: classic shape as a loft or swept body about 0.6 long along +Z-ish (angled about 15 degrees toward the viewer), face height y0.92, with a flat steel face (helmSteel, top facets steelEdge), a tapered horn pointing away from the dwarf (+X side), a hardie hole (small dark square, ironDark) on the face heel, a waisted midsection (iron) and a footed base (ironDark) with a slight flare. On the face, a thin glowing hot-strip (emberHot, glow) near the horn where a red-hot bar lies: a small bent bar (ember, glow) being worked. Props beside the stump: an iron-banded quench bucket (wood body, iron hoops top and bottom, water surface disc) half a meter to the stump's +Z side, with a thin steam wisp hint (one or two small water-tinted puffs); a pair of tongs (two iron rods joined at a rivet, gold rivet) leaning against the stump's -Z side. Keep the anvil crisp and hero-quality: bands, plate and fittings as separate small parts.
parts.attaches: Stump rests on the floor at mount groundAnvil on the ground ring; the anvil face at y0.92 sits just below the dwarf's braced left fist at handL, and the hot bar lies under the raised hammer's swing arc.

parts.builds: The dwarf's lower body and torso, rigged to hips/spine/chest and the leg chains. Legs: short, thick and planted, one sweep or two-segment tube per leg down hipL/kneeL/ankleL and mirrored, ending in chunky boots (frustumBox or stacked boxes) with big squared toes resting flat on the floor at groundDwarf, boots leather with woodDark soles and a small gold buckle on each ankle strap. Torso: a wide barrel chest from a loft or lathe, roughly 0.62 wide at the shoulders and 0.5 deep, barely tapering to the hips, wearing a tunic (tunic) with a lighter chest panel (tunicDark seams as thin inset strips) and a deep V or crossed lacing on the upper chest (leather strips). Over it a heavy blacksmith apron (apron): a broad bib panel from the chest down with a zig-zag or scalloped lower edge (extrude with smoothing, apronDark border strip seated as a separate edge part), hanging from a neck strap; a few tool-scuff patches as small darker inset slabs. Belt: a wide leather belt (leather) with a big gold buckle (gold) and 3 small tool loops (apronDark) around the hips, plus a heavy mallet hanging at the back-left hip (iron head, wood handle). Shoulders: massive pauldron plates (helmSteel with steelEdge rims and gold rivet studs) built at the two shoulder mounts to meet the arms part; a thick fur or leather collar (beardDark) round the neck at neckTop so the head part seats into it. Chest hair tufts or a chain shirt hint at the neckline in beardDark.
parts.attaches: Boots rest on the floor at groundDwarf; the neck collar builds up to mount neckTop where the head part begins; the pauldrons cover the shoulder sockets at mounts shoulderL and shoulderR; the legs ride joints hipL/kneeL/ankleL and hipR/kneeR/ankleR, torso rides hips, spine and chest.

parts.builds: The head and everything on it, riding the head joint (plus jaw). Skull: a big round head (sphere or lathe, radius about 0.17) in skin, squashed slightly wide, with a broad blunt nose (a rounded wedge, skin, skinShadow nostrils as two tiny dark discs), heavy dark brows (two thick ink-to-beardDark slabs angled in a scowl), and small deep-set eyes: two white almonds with dark pupils seated just under the brows, or a simple bold ink-and-white pair; bristling orange sideburn stubble (beardDark, small spikes or cards) along the cheeks. Ears: two small round ears (skin) poking from under the helm. The beard is the signature: a huge braided beard from chin to mid-chest, a solid silhouette mass (extrude or lofted wedge, beard) split into two thick braids plus a central moustache; each braid is a chain-like stack of 4 to 5 tapering segments (beard with beardDark gaps) ending in a gold ring (gold torus or short cylinder) and a small band; a strong chevron moustache (beard) sweeps out over the jaw on both sides of the nose; the beard's lower edge carries a beardDark trim. The jaw joint carries a separate lower-jaw/skin piece under the moustache so the mouth can open. Helm: a deep steel skullcap (lathe, helmSteel) with a nose guard down to the brows (steelEdge edge line), a brow ridge band, a gold band with a small emblazoned roundel at the front, and two short curved brass horns (swept spirals or curved rods, gold) sweeping out and up from the temples; rivet studs (gold dots) along the rim. Everything sits clear of the face: the horns rise above and beside the brows.
parts.attaches: Sits on mount neckTop above the body's collar; geometry rides joints neck, head and jaw; the beard's top tucks into the collar and its tip stops above the chest panel.

parts.builds: Both arms and the smith hammer, riding the arm chains. Right arm (shoulderR, elbowR, handR): raised high and bent back overhead, one tapering tube or two sweeps per segment in skin (bare forearm) with a rolled tunic sleeve cap at the shoulder (tunic) and a bracer (leather with gold buckle) on the forearm; the fist is a big chunky gauntlet (iron with steelEdge knuckle studs, 4 finger slabs plus thumb wrapping a haft). It grips a massive smith hammer held vertical, head up: a thick wood handle (wood with woodDark grip wrap) about 0.55 long and an oversized iron head (iron with steelDark striking faces and steelEdge bevels, a gold band at the neck of the head); the head sits clear at about y1.9, posed so its strike arc sweeps toward the anvil. Left arm (shoulderL, elbowL, handL): reaching forward-down to the anvil, same sleeve and bracer construction, fist (same gauntlet build) planted flat on the anvil face near the hot bar at mount side of the anvilStation part. Both deltoids hide under the body part's pauldrons: build only from the shoulder mount outward so the pauldron overlaps the socket. Elbow and knuckle details as small steelEdge plates. This part carries the silhouette's drama: make the raised arm and hammer read boldly from the front.
parts.attaches: Upper arms root at mounts shoulderR and shoulderL under the body's pauldrons; geometry rides shoulderR/elbowR/handR and shoulderL/elbowL/handL; the left fist lands on the anvil face of the anvilStation part and the hammer head hangs in the swing arc above it.

spec.name: Dwarf Blacksmith at the Anvil
spec.description: A stout, ginger-bearded Warcraft-style dwarf smith in oversized riveted pauldrons and a leather apron, raising a sledge over a glowing half-forged blade held in tongs on an anvil and tree stump.
spec.layout: Chunky, hand-painted Blizzard proportions: the dwarf is about 1.4 m to the top of his head and nearly as broad as he is tall, with short sturdy legs, a barrel chest, a round belly, huge shoulders, big fists and a big head. He faces +Z and stands with his belly at z≈0.2. In front of him (z≈0.62) is a tree stump topped by a classic anvil, long axis along X, with the horn pointing to +X (the model's left). The anvil face is at y=0.78, so it sits at about waist height. His right hand (-X) holds a sledgehammer raised up and over the anvil. His left hand (+X) holds long tongs gripping a glowing, half-forged blade that lies on the anvil face. A few ember sparks float above the blade. Silhouette: two giant studded pauldrons, a horned helmet, a long braided ginger beard falling to the belt, a leather apron, and the glowing orange blade as the focal accent. The bottom of the stump and both boots rest on y=0. Style on every part: saturated, painterly colours, with each material built as a dark outline/shade base, a main colour and a small lighter highlight piece, e.g. a gold rim on every steel edge, rivets and studs in rows, chunky bevelled slabs rather than smooth forms, and exaggerated bold shapes. Warm light colours on top faces and cooler darker ones below. Everything that glows (blade, embers, sparks, forge-lit eyes' glints) uses the glow kit.

parts.builds: Everything from the hips down plus the waist. Two short, thick legs (thigh 0.25 m, shin 0.23 m, each a smooth sweep on the leg chain) in clothDark trousers, with leather knee guards (leatherLight plate, leatherDark strap, gold rivet) and calf wraps. Chunky boots in leather/leatherDark with a wide toe cap, a thick sole slab in iron, a steel toe cap with a gold rim, and fold-over cuffs at the top with three studs. Boots stand parallel with the toes pointing +Z. Around the pelvis: a broad belt (leatherDark with leatherLight edge sweep) with a big gold-rimmed buckle at the front showing a small steel anvil emblem, five studs on each side, and a short blue tabard skirt (cloth with a clothDark border and a gold trim stripe) front and back. Hanging from the belt: a small hammer loop, a leather pouch on the left hip, and a coil of rope on the right hip.
parts.attaches: The legs hang from hipL/hipR on joint hips; boots rest on y=0 (floor) at footL/footR. The belt sits on beltLine and the torso apron starts just above it.

parts.builds: Barrel chest and round belly as a loft on the spine: a clothDark undershirt, a thick leather apron (leather, leatherDark border sweep, stitched seam parts, soot smudges near the bottom, a gold rivet at each upper corner, a hammer-and-flame emblem patch in the centre built from small parts) hanging from a neck strap from chestCenter down to just above the belt, and a cross-chest strap. Two huge Warcraft-style pauldrons at shoulderL/shoulderR: layered steel plates (steelDark base, steel mid, steelLight edge highlights, gold rims), a row of rivets, and 3 chunky cone spikes on each, with a blue cloth shoulder cape piece under each. A steel gorget ring collar round the neck base. A short blue cloak panel hanging down the back with a gold edge. Sleeve openings are left for the arms: the arm part provides upper arms starting at the shoulder joints and the pauldrons cover their tops. Bare skin of the chest shows as a small V below the collar, hidden mostly by the beard.
parts.attaches: Rides hips, spine1 and spine2. Pauldrons are centred on shoulderL/shoulderR. The neck gorget meets the head part at neckBase. The belt of legsAndBelt starts at beltLine. Beard hangs in front of the apron's upper part, z>0.19.

parts.builds: The signature part: a big chunky head built on head/neck/jaw joints with a separate upper head and lower jaw (jaw hinge near the ear line). Wide skin skull with a strong brow ridge in skinShade, a large rounded bulbous nose (skinLight with a small shade underside), cheekbones, small pointed ears with gold hoop earrings, big eyes of eyeWhite with eyeBlue iris and ink pupil plus tiny white highlight, thick bushy ginger eyebrows (beard/beardLight blades) angled in a determined frown, ink eye outline. A walrus moustache of broad overlapping blades in beardDark root, beard mid and beardLight tip, swept out to the sides with gold rings. The huge beard: a solid wedge from chin to belt line plus about a dozen overlapping broad blades (root-to-tip beardDark, beard, beardLight), with two thick braids each with gold clasps and a beaded tip hanging down the chest front to y≈0.8. Helmet: a steel dome (steelDark under steel with a steelLight highlight rim) with a gold brow band, a nose guard strip, a row of rivets, two curved bone-coloured steel horns (steelLight with gold tips) rising out of the sides to a height of about 1.5 m, and ginger hair tufts sticking out below the helm at the back and sides, with a short braid at the back. Face stays clear: nothing in front of eyes and nose. The mouth is a dark ink gap between moustache and jaw with a few teeth.
parts.attaches: Head sits on neck at neckBase (neck sweep from spine2 into the head); head centre at headCenter, jaw on joint jaw. The beard root is at beardRoot and hangs over the torso apron without touching the belt. Helmet horns and hair stay inside the box.

parts.builds: Both arms, thick and muscular, in the rest pose given by the joints. Upper arms are skin sweeps emerging from the pauldrons (shoulderL/R to elbowL/R), forearms from elbow to wrist are heavy sweeps (about 0.07 m radius) covered with leatherDark bracers with steel plates, gold rivets and a lace strap. Big gauntleted fists: wide palm block in leather, finger blocks (4 fingers plus thumb) curled around the grips on fingersL/R and thumbL/R, with knuckle studs; the right fist wraps round the hammer handle at gripR (ring of fingers closed, hammer shaft passing through), the left fist round the tongs handles at gripL. Skin tones (skin, skinShade underside, skinLight top highlights) on the bare upper arm, with a few scars as small lighter strips and a gold armband on each bicep. Soot smudges (leatherDark flat patches) on the forearms. The hand parts stay slightly open on the sides so the tool handles can be seen between fingers.
parts.attaches: Starts at shoulderL/shoulderR (covered by the torso pauldrons), ends at the fists at gripL and gripR where the tools part's handles pass through the hands.

parts.builds: The handheld tools and the work in progress. (1) The sledgehammer, riding wristR: a wooden handle (wood, woodDark grip wrap with leather wraps) from gripR up and across toward hammerHead (rising about 0.2 m over the anvil and leaning toward +X), ending in a big chunky steel head block (steelDark base, steel body, steelLight face highlights, gold bands at both ends of the head) whose long axis is perpendicular to the shaft in the XY plane, so one striking face points down toward the blade; a pommel cap at the grip end with a gold ring. (2) The tongs, riding wristL: two long iron arms (iron with ironlike highlights in steelDark) crossing at a rivet pivot near the middle, handles running back past gripL to about z=0.24 with leather grip wraps, the jaws closing on the end of the blade at tongsJaw. (3) The half-forged blade lying along X on the anvil face centred on bladeCenter (about 0.38 m long, 0.07 wide, 0.02 thick, resting on y=0.78): a tapering extruded shape, glowing with a gradient of emberHot at the core, ember in the middle, emberDark at the cooler tip, plus a thin tang at the tongs end; use the glow kit on it. A few chips of glowing scale lie beside it. (4) 8–10 sparks, small glowing emberHot/ember cubes and tetrahedra of varied size flying from the hit zone up and out (around y 0.85–1.25 near x 0..0.3), all glowing. No paint on glowing parts.
parts.attaches: Hammer handle passes through the right fist at gripR (joint wristR); tongs handles through the left fist at gripL (joint wristL); the blade lies on anvilTop at bladeCenter and is gripped at tongsJaw.

parts.builds: The base the dwarf works on, static on joint base. A large tree-stump: wide low-poly cylinder (radius 0.33, wood with woodDark bark ring made of vertical ridges, leather-brown top cut face with concentric ring lines in woodDark, root flares at the bottom, a few small moss-free chips), top at stumpTop (y≈0.36). An iron band hoop (iron, gold rivet row) round the stump's upper rim. On it a classic big anvil, long axis along X: a wide base plate with foot blocks, a narrower waist, a thick steel face plate (steel with steelLight top edge, steelDark underside, iron wedge body) ending at y=0.78 (anvilTop) and about 0.58 m long × 0.2 m wide, a stepped heel at -X end with a round hardy hole and a pritchel hole in the top face, and a long tapering conical horn toward +X ending at x≈0.56 (the horn slightly lower than the face). A gold maker's mark and small scratch/dent parts on the side. Scorch marks (ink flat patches) and glow-tinted ember reflection strips on the face near the blade. At the base of the stump a bucket of water (wood staves, iron bands, a rope handle) and a few coal lumps (ink with ember glowing cracks) are NOT included; keep to a small pile of 3 coal lumps with ember glints at the stump's side near x=-0.35, z=0.85.
parts.attaches: Stands on the floor at floor mount; the anvil face top is anvilTop and the tools part's blade rests exactly there. The dwarf's boots stay clear of the stump's front edge (z<0.28).

I'm sketching out a rigged dwarf blacksmith character at an anvil in a Warcraft-inspired style, planning the dwarf's size and positioning facing the anvil, with a hammer, tongs, and a glowing forge element to complete the scene.

Now I'm working through the full skeleton hierarchy—hips, spine, chest, neck, head, arms, and legs—mapping out precise y-coordinates for each joint from feet to helmet, and positioning the shoulders and arms so one hand raises a hammer while the other holds tongs over the anvil.

Positioning the anvil itself atop a stump at waist height, figuring out the right y-level for its top surface and centering it in front of the dwarf for the forging pose.

Shoulder at z=0 for a forward hunch, with upper arm and forearm each around 0.28 so hands fall forward-down naturally.

Now I'm dividing the model into five parts: legs/boots covering the lower body with trousers, kilt, and belt tools within a bounding box roughly x[-0.3,0.3], y[0,0.75], z[-0.3,0.4]; torso covering chest, leather apron, pauldrons, and bandolier above that in y[0.7,1.15]; and I'm about to define the head section next.

Head includes face, braided beard, mustache, horned helmet or mohawk hair, ears and jaw, boxed in y[1.1,1.55]. I'm reconsidering the part split to six pieces: legs, torso, head, arms (with gauntlets and hands), tools (hammer, tongs, glowing workpiece, sparks — rigged to the wrist joints), and anvilStage (stump and anvil), budgeting roughly 130/170/190/150/110/110 triangles for a total under 900. Working through the spine chain from hips through spine1, spine2, neck, and head, adjusting positions and directions to get a natural upward-forward curve, then adding the jaw joint hinged near the ear. For the arms, I'm placing shoulderL on spine2 and computing the elbow and hand positions by projecting along a normalized rest-pose direction vector to get a down-forward-out arm pose.

Positioning the left hand gripping tongs resting on the anvil top, computing the wrist from the elbow using the chain length so the arm reaches naturally to that point, then setting up the shoulderL/elbowL/wristL chain with their own direction vectors, plus adding finger and thumb joints under the wrist with a digit role. Now starting on the right arm, which will be raised holding a hammer, beginning with the shoulderR position.

Still working out the hammer's grip and raised angle relative to the anvil...

I'll have the striking face point roughly downward toward the anvil, with the head perpendicular to the handle axis at its top end.

Now I'm placing the anvil with its horn extending toward +x, adjusting the workpiece so it sits realistically on the anvil face and horn transition, and nudging the tongs jaws and hammer head position so the strike point lands correctly on the blade.

Checking the stump radius against the dwarf's boot position so the base doesn't clip the feet, then working out the overall bounding box — depth from the back at z=-0.32 to the stump front at z=0.95 gives about 1.3 total length, and I'm now checking the width from the pauldrons outward.

I'm breaking the figure into parts: lower body with boots and apron, torso with pauldrons, head with beard and helmet, arms holding hammer and tongs, plus the anvil, stump, and sparks. I'm also pinning down joint positions, starting with the hip root and overall height including the helmet.

For pose, I'm going with a relaxed working stance rather than a T-pose — arms bent forward with the right hand resting the hammer on the anvil face and the left holding tongs gripping a glowing bar, keeping shoulder, elbow, wrist, and basic hand joints.

Now I'm working out the anvil geometry: centered at z=0.72 with the top surface at y=0.80, sitting on a 0.45-tall stump, with its long axis running along x and the horn pointing toward +X since the dwarf stands facing it from the side.

I'm sizing up the overall figure's bounding box, deciding the dwarf's back-to-front depth, total width including pauldrons and the anvil horn, and settling on roughly 1.4 width by 1.75 height before moving to the joint rig names.

Setting up the skeleton joints...

Toe joint continues the leg chain with a forward direction and leg role. Now I'm placing the arms: shoulderL angled forward-down toward the chest, with elbow and wrist positions sized to match upper arm and forearm lengths, aiming the left hand toward the anvil area since it holds tongs.

I'm leaning toward an asymmetric pose for liveliness, but keeping it close to symmetric and neutral for rigging: the left arm lowered toward the anvil, the right arm raised with elbow bent so the hand can hold the hammer upward near the anvil's working height. I'm defining ownership between parts: the arms own the hammer and tongs, while the anvil part owns the workpiece bar, with a shared mount point marking where the tongs' jaws grip the bar's end near the anvil face.

Adjusting positions so the hammer head sits just above and slightly behind the anvil's left half, cocked back in position; the anvil itself is sized oversized for a stylized dwarf-forge look, around 1.1 units wide with the stump and body stacked to a face height near 0.86.
