spec.name: Cathedral Gargoyle
spec.description: A weathered gothic stone gargoyle crouched on a carved cathedral cornice ledge, wings folded high behind it, glowing amber eyes under a heavy brow, moss in every crevice.
spec.layout: The model is a crouched gargoyle perched on a fragment of cathedral cornice, facing +Z. The ledge is the only floor part: a block 2.4 m wide (x -1.2..1.2), 0.62 m tall, 1.7 m deep (z -0.85..0.85), its top surface at y = 0.55 with a wider cornice lip (front edge z 0.85, back edge z -0.78). Everything else rests on that top. The gargoyle crouches in the classic pose: digitigrade legs folded with knees drawn up beside the chest and clawed feet planted flat on the ledge top around z 0.14; the belly hangs low between haunches (hips at [0, 0.95, 0.02]); the chest leans forward over the front lip; the arms reach down-forward and the hands grip the cornice lip at z ~0.78 with claws hooked over the front face. The head sits forward and low at [0, 1.34, 0.52], snout toward +Z, heavy brow over glowing amber eyes, two ribbed horns sweeping back and up to y ~1.95, tall bat ears flaring outward. The wings are the silhouette's second read: folded bat wings rising in a high V behind the shoulders to y ~2.05, x to +/-0.95, slate-dark membranes hanging down the back to the haunches. The tail leaves the rump, drapes over the ledge back edge at z -0.78 and curls to the model's right below the ledge to y ~0.15. Style everywhere is carved stone: blocky faceted primitives, flat colours per part, chipped corners, cracks as thin dark slivers, moss and lichen sitting only on upward and side faces, rust drip stains below the iron straps, warm worn highlights on top edges and cold deep shade underneath. The only non-stone notes are the rusted iron straps, a small brass consecration plaque, bone-coloured horns, claws and teeth, and the glowing amber eyes.

parts.builds: The stone stage: a fragment of cathedral cornice in stoneMid. Build the base block as a slab from y 0 to 0.5 (x -1.2..1.2, z -0.8..0.75), then the cornice profile on top as three stacked stepped slabs: a stoneDark lower ogee band to y 0.56 pulled forward to z 0.85 (the dripping lip) and back to z -0.78, a stoneMid fillet, and a thin stoneLight worn top course whose upper edges are chipped (small stoneDark nubs at the corners). Under the front lip: three chamfered corbel brackets (frustum boxes, stoneDark) at x -0.7, 0, 0.7, and a row of 9 small dentil tooth blocks (stoneLight) between them. Two rusted iron reinforcement straps (iron) run vertically down the front face at x -0.55 and 0.55 with three round rivet heads (rust) each, and rust bleed streaks (rust) run down from them. Weathering sits where water goes: moss patches (moss with mossDark rims) along the top course edges and in the molding shadow line, pale lichen crust spots (lichen) on the side faces, dark drip stains (stain) running from the lip down the front face. Under the front lip, three chunky corbel brackets (tapered frustumBoxes in stoneDark) stepping down to y 0.05. The front face carries a carved band: a row of small rosette bosses (low cylinders in stonePale) separated by dark soot-inlaid grooves (thin soot boxes seated 3 mm proud). Corners of the coping are chipped: small angular missing-corner wedges in stoneDark. Moss grows where stone meets sky: thin irregular moss patches (flat extruded blobs, moss and mossDark) on the top surface near the back edge and seeping over the coping's front rim; a green streak runs down one front corner. The gargoyle's feet and knuckles rest on the coping top at y 0.36, so leave the top clear of tall debris. All stone reads chiseled: box and ngon-section shapes, flat facets, no smooth spheres.
parts.attaches: floor: true; everything else rests on mount ledgeTop (y 0.36).

parts.builds: The gargoyle's core: spine, ribcage, neck, head, face, horns and jaw. Build the torso as a loft over the spine chain (core at [0,0.62,-0.35], chest at [0,0.95,-0.05]): a heavy hunched chest, elliptical sections about 0.55 wide and 0.45 tall at the chest narrowing to 0.3 at the hips, in stoneMid with a countershaded paint - warmLit on up-facing surfaces, stoneDark below and in the hollows. Carved furrow lines: thin soot strips seated along the chest's front and around the shoulders. Two small pebbled pectoral slabs in stoneLight sit on the chest front. The neck is a short thick swept tube from chest to head in stoneMid with a ring of carved fold ridges (thin torus-like swept rings in stoneDark) at its base. The head is a blocky chiseled skull: a stoneLight brow mass with deep overhanging brow ledge (a protruding frustumBox in stoneLight casting the eye sockets into soot), two deep eye sockets holding small glowing ember spheres (ember, glowing via the glow kit, strength 1.6) each with a tiny emberCore glint sphere in front. The muzzle projects forward: a squared snout frustum in stoneLight with flared nostril recesses (small soot wedges), and a wide open mouth built as separate upper and lower jaws: the upper jaw (riding head) carries a row of blocky teeth (teeth, small triangular extrudes) and the lower jaw rides the jaw joint, hinged open about 30 degrees showing a tongue (tongue) and lower teeth, so the mouth can open. Long fangs at the upper jaw corners in teeth. The jaw's underside and throat are stoneDark. Two curled ram-like horns sprout from the head's upper sides: swept tubes (sprout) in clawHorn ridged with thin darker rings, spiraling back and out to about 0.22 m radius. Small carved ear fins behind the horns in stoneDark. The whole head reads as a cathedral spout: the mouth's floor extends forward into a small square spout lip in stoneDark.
parts.attaches: Rises from mount hipSeat over the core and chest joints; shoulders at mounts shoulderL and shoulderR are the limb part's roots; neck and head continue from chest; wings bolt to the back at mounts wingRootL and wingRootR; the tail starts at mount tailRoot.

parts.builds: Arms, legs, hands and feet, all digitigrade and crouched. Arms: from mounts shoulderL and shoulderR (riding shoulderL/R) build thick upper-arm tubes (sweep, stoneMid) forward-down to elbows at [0.42,0.78,0.38] and [-0.42,0.78,0.38], then forearms slightly slimmer (stoneLight tops, stoneMid sides) down to knuckles planted on the ledge at about [0.35,0.40,0.68] and mirrored. Each arm carries carved boulder-like muscle bosses: 2-3 overlapping low spheres or frustum slabs in stoneLight on the upper arm and shoulder, and a soot furrow groove at the elbow crease. Hands are clenched fist-knuckles: a blocky hand mass (frustumBox, stoneLight) with three big forward claw talons per hand (curved swept cones in clawHorn, tips touching the ledge top) plus a small rear dewclaw. Legs: from hipL/hipR build the folded digitigrade crouch - thigh tube forward-up to kneeL/kneeR at [0.37,0.6,0.02] (knee carried high and forward, a big blocky knee cap slab in stoneLight), shin down and back to ankleL/ankleR at [0.35,0.37,-0.22], then the foot segment forward to toeL/toeR at [0.35,0.37,0.05]; feet are broad three-toed claw feet (blocky toe masses in stoneLight) whose talons (clawHorn curved cones) grip over the ledge coping's front edge at y 0.36. Haunches: two large teardrop muscle masses (big flattened spheres or loft blobs in stoneMid with stoneLight tops) flanking the tail root at about x plus/minus 0.33, z -0.45, with carved concentric furrow grooves (thin soot strips) - the classic gargoyle thigh read. Moss flecks (tiny flat moss patches) sit in the ankle creases and on top of the knee caps.
parts.attaches: Arm chains root at mounts shoulderL and shoulderR on the chest; leg chains root at mount hipSeat on the core; every claw tip and foot sole rests exactly on the ledge top (mount ledgeTop, y 0.36).

parts.builds: The folded wings rising behind the shoulders. Each wing roots at mounts wingRootL and wingRootR (riding wingL/wingR): a short muscular upper-arm tube (stoneMid) up and out to wingElbowL/wingElbowR at about [0.62,1.5,-0.5], then a slim forearm folding back down-inward, ending in a small clawed thumb knob (clawHorn spike) at about [0.95,1.1,-0.35]. From the wrist, three bony finger spars fan out folded and back: swept tapering tubes (clawHorn joint knobs, stoneDark membrane surfaces) running down and back toward the haunches, the longest reaching about z -0.85, x plus/minus 1.25. Between the spars, the wing membrane is built with b.membrane between adjacent finger paths (and between the leading-edge arm and the first finger), in soot-dark stone: color stoneDark with countershade paint lifting stoneMid on up-facing panels; membrane thickness about 0.015 with a slight scallop at the trailing edge. Along the leading edge of each wing add two rows of small carved ridge studs (stonePale low cylinders) and a darker trim seam (thin swept soot line). At the membrane roots near the spine, moss patches creep onto the webbing's upper face. Two short back spikes (clawHorn cones) ride the spine between the wing roots, and a small ornamental carved finial disc (stonePale lathe rosette) caps each elbow joint. Wings read as carved stone sheets: angular, thick-edged, faceted.
parts.attaches: Wing roots bolt to the torso's back at mounts wingRootL and wingRootR, riding joints wingL, wingElbowL, wingR, wingElbowR; the folded membranes fall behind the arms and over the haunches without touching the ledge top.

parts.builds: The tail curling around the right (+X) rear corner of the ledge. Build a chain over tail1..tail3..tailTip and sweep it: thick at the root (radius about 0.09 at tail1) tapering to 0.03, sections as 6- or 8-sided ngon for the chiseled stone look, color stoneMid with countershade (warmLit on top, stoneDark beneath). Ridges: thin swept soot rings at each joint, and a dorsal row of small triangular carved spikes (stoneDark frustum spikes) along the top of the first two thirds. The last third is plain, ending in a leaf-shaped stone spade tip: a flat extruded diamond blade in stoneLight (about 0.16 long, 0.1 wide, thickness 0.02) with a carved center groove (thin soot strip seated in it), angled upward at about 30 degrees like a scorpion's barb. The tail path: from tailRoot [0,0.55,-0.62] back and down to [0.33,0.45,-0.9], out along the ledge's back-right to [0.58,0.44,-0.75] then curling forward to tailTip [0.75,0.5,-0.15], the whole tail resting on the ledge top (its lowest points at y 0.36, sinking no more than 2 cm into the coping). Moss flecks on the tail's upper surface near the root and one moss tuft where the tail meets the haunch.
parts.attaches: Roots at mount tailRoot on the core joint; rides joints tail1, tail2, tail3, tailTip; the tail's underside lies on the ledge top at y 0.36 within the ledge's back-right quadrant.

spec.description: A hunched gothic stone gargoyle crouched on a cathedral ledge, wings folded high, hands gripping the front edge, tail curled on the stone, with weathered chisel-carved facets, moss and ember eyes.
spec.layout: Everything is carved stone: bold chunky faceted primitives with low segment counts (6-8 sides), a flat stone colour per part, and darker tones where the form turns down and into crevices. spec.name: Cathedral Gargoyle
spec.description: A weathered gothic stone gargoyle crouched on a cathedral ledge, wings spread in a rest pose, fangs bared, with moss and rain stains in the crevices.
spec.layout: Everything is carved stone: chunky, faceted, chisel-blocky shapes with bold readable proportions and no soft organic detail. A stone ledge (1.7 wide, 0.22 high, z -0.8..0.85) is the only floor contact. The gargoyle crouches on it in a predatory squat. The heavy haunches and hind feet are planted at z -0.1..0.15. The tail runs back from the hips along the ledge, then curls to the model's left (+X) and ends in a spade. The barrel chest rises forward of the hips. Massive shoulders carry long forearms that are planted on the ledge, with big clawed hands at z about 0.6. The neck rises from the chest. The oversized head thrusts forward and slightly up, with a broad snout, an open mouth with a separate upper and lower jaw, big fangs, heavy brow ridges, curled ram-like horns, bat-like pointed ears and glaring amber eyes. A pair of bat wings with bony fingers is spread up and back from the shoulders in a rest T-pose, reaching x +-0.95, with stone-slab membranes. The silhouette is a hunched triangle topped by wings and horns. Style on every part: facets and flat planes, visible chisel-edge highlights as small lighter wedge parts, cracks as thin dark parts, and weathering coloured by place. Moss and lichen sit on upward faces and in crevices, soot and rain streaks run down vertical faces below ledges and brows, and the underside and the feet are darker. A gothic ornament motif (pointed arch, trefoil or quatrefoil) repeats on the ledge front, the chest plate, the bracers and the wing membrane ribs. The model is left-right symmetric: build the L side (+X) and the R side (-X) with `for (const s of [1, -1])`. Parts may add their own finer joints (fingers, toes, wing fingers, jaw bones) under the listed joints, with names prefixed by their part (e.g. fingerL1, toeL1, wfingerL1).

parts.builds: The cathedral ledge the gargoyle crouches on, carved stone in 'ledge' with 'mortar' joints. A chunky slab (x +-0.85, z -0.8..0.85, y 0..0.22) with a stepped cornice lip along the front and sides (small stacked boxes in stoneLight with stoneHi chisel-edge wedges on top). Dentil blocks run along the front lip. A row of three pointed-arch or quatrefoil relief panels is built from small dark extrudes in stoneDark on the front face. Two corbel blocks sit under the front corners. Mortar lines appear as thin dark boxes forming block courses on the front and side faces. One iron cramp (iron) is set into the top near the back. Weathering: moss and lichen patches on the top (moss, mossDark, lichen) especially at the back corners and around the feet and hand contact points (leave the contact spots as bare stone), rain stain and soot streaks running down the front face below the gargoyle, thin crack parts. A small worn drain groove runs under the front lip. Do not build anything above y 0.25 except moss tufts and small stone chips.
parts.attaches: Top face at mount ledgeTop (y 0.22) carries the hands (handContactL/R), feet (footContactL/R) and tail. No joints: rigid static geometry on the root joint (bone hips) at its own absolute coordinates.

parts.builds: The torso and tail, in stone/stoneDark. A bulky loft/sweep body from the hipsCenter through spine1 to the chestCenter (spine2), with a barrel chest (wider, about 0.4 across), a narrower waist and a heavy pelvis block of the hips, all with faceted chisel planes. A paler belly plate (stoneLight) with horizontal rib-band relief. A chest plate with a trefoil or pointed-arch emblem built from small dark parts in stoneDark outlined in stoneHi. A dorsal ridge of overlapping triangular spine blades running from the neck base along the back to the tail root (stoneDark, with stoneHi edges). Pec and trapezius masses that blend into the shoulders (the arms part starts at the shoulder joints). A hip mass with a loincloth-like stone slab hanging between the legs is optional. The tail follows the tail1..tail4 joints along the ledge and curls to +X, tapering with small ridge fins on top, and ends in a carved spade-shaped tip (extruded diamond, stoneDark with stoneHi rim). Weathering: moss on the top of the shoulders and back, soot under the belly, cracks across the chest and tail, rain stains on the flanks.
parts.attaches: Neck begins at neckBase on spine2 (the head part builds the neck). Thighs start at hipSocketL/R and shoulders at shoulderL/R, and wing roots start at wingRootL/R, all built by other parts. The tail lies on the ledge top (ledgeTop, y 0.22, tail axis y >= 0.3). Rides hips, spine1, spine2, tail1..tail4.

parts.builds: The neck and head, the signature feature with the richest construction. The neck is a thick sweep over neck1 and neck2 with a stone mane ridge of blades. The head is a big blocky skull at headCenter (about 0.36 wide, 0.3 tall) with a broad flat snout reaching to z about 0.9 and a heavy brow ridge, so the eyes sit under it with nothing in front of them. Build a SEPARATE upper jaw and lower jaw (lower jaw on the jaw joint, hinged at jawHinge). The mouth is open slightly, with 'mouth' dark interior parts, a stone tongue slab, and upper fangs and lower tusks (stoneHi, 6-8 sided cones, large and readable) plus a row of smaller teeth. Two big amber eyes (eyeGlow with an eyePupil slit and a dark stoneShadow socket ring, glowing) sit under angry slanted brow wedges. Nostril holes on the snout tip, a cheek plate and cheekbone ridges. A pair of big curled ram-like horns (stoneDark to stoneLight tips) sweeping back and out. A pair of tall bat-like pointed ears. A chin beard of 3-5 stone icicle spikes and a chin boss. The face is carved with chisel facets, cracks, and moss on the brow top and between the horns, soot and rain stains under the eyes.
parts.attaches: Neck starts at mount neckBase (the torso chest top, spine2) and rides neck1 and neck2. The skull rides head and the lower jaw rides jaw (hinge at jawHinge). No contact with the ledge. Nothing may be placed in front of the face.

parts.builds: Both forelimbs (build L at +X and R at -X), in stone/stoneDark. A massive shoulder pauldron block with chiselled ridge plates (a stoneHi edge wedge and a spike) at shoulderL/R, an upper arm sweep to elbowL/R (with an elbow spike), a long muscular forearm to wristL/R, and a gothic bracer on each forearm: a band with a repeating pointed-arch or trefoil relief motif. Big chunky hands planted flat on the ledge at handContactL/R (x +-0.3, z about 0.62, y 0.25), each with 4 thick fingers fanned forward (digit chains, joints fingerL1.. / fingerR1.. under handL/R, 2 segments each) and a thick thumb, ending in curved claws (stoneHi, cone-shaped, gripping the ledge lip edge). Knuckle bumps. Weathering: moss in the elbow creases and on the pauldrons, rain stains on the forearms, soot on the underside.
parts.attaches: Starts at shoulderL/R on spine2 (the torso part builds the chest and trapezius up to there). Hands rest on mounts handContactL/R at ledgeTop (sink at most 1 cm). Rides shoulderL/R, elbowL/R, wristL/R, handL/R and its own finger joints.

parts.builds: Both hind legs, digitigrade and crouching (build L at +X and R at -X), in stone/stoneDark. A thick thigh haunch from hipSocketL/R to kneeL/R with a big rounded-faceted muscle block and a knee spike, a shin back to ankleL/R, an ankle spur, then a long foot to footL/R. Each foot has three forward toes (digit chains under footL/R, e.g. toeL1.., 2 segments each) plus a rear dewclaw, all with thick stoneHi claws gripping the ledge. The feet rest at footContactL/R (x +-0.34, z about 0.12, y 0.25). Thigh striations as thin dark parts, a gothic leaf-trim band at the knee. Weathering: moss on top of the thighs and toes, soot and rain stains on the shins, cracks, and darker stone at the underside.
parts.attaches: Starts at hipSocketL/R on hips (the torso part builds the pelvis). Feet rest on mounts footContactL/R at ledgeTop (sink at most 1 cm). Rides hipL/R, kneeL/R, ankleL/R, footL/R and its own toe joints.

parts.builds: Two large bat-like wings (build L at +X and R at -X), spread upward and back from wingRootL/R in a rest pose. Each wing has a thick bony arm sweep over wingShoulder -> wingElbow -> wingWrist (a stone bone with knuckle bumps and a wrist spike/thumb claw), then four long tapered finger bones (digit chains, joints wfingerL1.. / wfingerR1.. under wingWrist, 2 segments each) that fan out and down and back to wingtips (reaching x +-0.95, y >= 0.5, z down to -0.65). Stone-slab membranes ('membrane' with 'membraneEdge' trim, via b.membrane) are stretched between the fingers and body with scalloped trailing edges. Each membrane panel gets an inset gothic motif: a pointed-arch tracery rib and small trefoil cutouts as thin dark parts in stoneDark seated on the surface, plus a feather-like chisel rib pattern. Weathering: moss on the upper arm bone tops and wing root, rain stain streaks running down the membranes, cracks and chipped edges (small notches).
parts.attaches: Roots at wingRootL/R on spine2 (the torso's upper back, between the shoulder blades). Rides wingShoulderL/R, wingElbowL/R, wingWristL/R and its own finger joints. The wing must clear the head (keep |x| > 0.25 above y 0.9 for z > 0).

spec.name: Lionheart Gunblade
spec.description: A Final Fantasy-style revolver gunblade planted point-down in the ground after battle, its silver chain hanging slack behind the blade.
spec.layout: One vertical gunblade standing on its planted tip at x=0, front (+Z) is the polished cutting edge. From the ground up: a steel blade tapering from 0.16 m wide at the guard seat to a point sunk 2 cm into the floor, carrying a dark blood groove, a light polished edge strip and a row of spine teeth on the back (−Z) edge. At y 1.28–1.56 the ornate guard wraps the blade and carries the revolver mechanism: an 8-fluted drum with its axis along Z at [0, 1.42, 0.02], a brass-banded barrel pointing forward to a muzzle at z 0.34, a curved spur hammer at the back top and a trigger in a brass loop under the drum. Above the guard a back-leaning leather grip rises to a gold pommel dome with a glowing ruby at y 1.90. From the pommel a silver chain hangs down the back of the model, swaying behind the blade to about y 0.72 at z −0.56. The style is faceted low-poly metalwork: cool steel against warm brass and gold trim, dark gunmetal mechanism, ivory side-plate medallions, a glowing blue rune near the blade base and a glowing ruby pommel stone as the only magic.

parts.builds: The planted blade, tip down. Main body: a flat tapered slab drawn as a faceted extrude facing ±X, silhouette from the point at y 0.02 rising to full width 0.16 m at the guardSeat mount y 1.30, with a gentle forward (+Z) sweep of the edge and a slight recurve near the tip; thickness about 0.035 m; wears steel. Details as their own seated parts: a polished cutting-edge strip (edge) running the full +Z edge from tip to guard; a narrow blood groove (gunmetalDark) inset down the blade centre face on both sides; the back spine (−Z) shaded steelDark. Seven staggered triangular teeth (steelDark bodies, brassLight tips) project backward from the −Z edge between y 0.35 and y 1.05, largest near the base. At y 0.22 a winged emblem plate on both flats: an ivory disc with a gold winged lion silhouette in gold over it, held by two silver rivets. Two faint chevron runes (runeGlow, glowing) flanking the emblem at y 0.32 and y 0.14, small extrudes seated flush on the flats. Two brass collar rivets at the top where the blade enters the guard.
parts.attaches: The blade's top face ends exactly at mount guardSeat [0, 1.30, 0], where the gunCore's wing plates and drum wrap around it; the tip sinks 2 cm below y 0.

parts.builds: The guard and revolver mechanism. Guard: two broad swept wing plates (faceted extrudes facing ±X, gunmetal) rising from the blade seat to wrap the drum, each trimmed with a brass edge band, three brassLight rivets and a small steelDark underline shadow where the wing meets the drum. Revolver drum: a lathe cylinder, axis +Z, centre at mount cylinderAxis, radius 0.085, length 0.20, gunmetal, with eight brass flute ridges running its length and a brassLight centre band; its rear face is a gunmetalDark plate. Barrel: a gunmetal tube radius 0.032 from z 0.10 to z 0.34 forward (+Z), with a brassLight muzzle ring, a black bore disc, and a small brass front-sight blade on top. Hammer: rides joint hammer, a curved gunmetalDark spur with a steelDark face and a brassLight pin at its pivot, swept up and back from the drum's top rear. Trigger: rides joint trigger, a small curved steelDark trigger blade hanging inside a brass trigger-guard loop that arcs from the drum's underside forward to the gripSeat mount. Side plates: an ivory plate with a gold lion-head medallion and three silver screws on each flat of the drum. A small steelDark rear-sight notch sits on the drum top.
parts.attaches: Wing plates clamp the blade at mount guardSeat; the drum barrel axis runs through mount cylinderAxis; the trigger-guard loop lands on mount gripSeat where the grip enters.

parts.builds: The grip and pommel above the mechanism. Grip core: a slightly back-leaning tapered frustum sweep from mount gripSeat [0, 1.56, 0.02] to mount pommelCap [0, 1.90, -0.06], square-ish section 0.055 m at the collar shrinking to 0.04 m at the pommel, wearing gripLeather. Wraps: five diagonal leather bands (gripWrap) evenly spaced up the grip, each with a tiny brass stud at both ends, plus a diamond column of ivory inlay studs (four, alternating offsets) down the front (+Z) face. Collar: a brass ring with a brassLight bevel where the grip enters the guard at gripSeat. Pommel: a gold lathe dome cap with a brassLight rim ring seated on the pommel joint at pommelCap, holding a faceted emberRed ruby (glowing) set into its back face; a small brass ring mount projects from the pommel's back at chainRoot [0, 1.88, -0.09] where the chain roots.
parts.attaches: Bottom of the grip enters the gunCore at mount gripSeat inside the trigger-guard loop; the pommel cap closes on mount pommelCap and hands the chain off at mount chainRoot.

parts.builds: The hanging chain and charm. Chain: about fourteen alternating links swept along the chain1..chain4 joints from mount chainRoot downward behind the blade — short silver capsules (rod sweeps) alternating 90° orientation link to link, each with a tiny steelDark inner shadow ring so the links read as open metal. The chain follows the joints' gentle backward sway, ending at the last link around y 0.72, z −0.56. Charm: from the final link hangs a talisman — a small gold triangle frame (extrude) with a faceted emberRed crystal (glowing) inside it, a brassLight cap on the crystal, and two ivory beads on a short silver drop wire above the frame.
parts.attaches: Roots at mount chainRoot on the pommel's ring mount and hangs clear behind the blade, never touching it; the lowest link stays above y 0.62.

The cutting edge runs down the left side (+X) with a fine lit edge line; the spine on the right (+X negative) is heavier with gold trim bolts. At the top, the blade enters the revolver gun-housing (y 1.95 to 2.25): a chunky dark iron block with a brass revolver drum around the blade root whose axis is vertical, six chamber bores facing forward, a short barrel stub and a front sight above the blade exit, and an ink-outlined panelled surface with rivets. Back from the housing the grip curves down and back to z -0.5, wrapped in red leather bands with gold studs, ending in a gold lion-headed pommel whose mane reads from the front. A large gold crossguard with a lion-head emblem faces forward at the blade root, with a hanging gold chain draping down the blade's spine side. Trigger and trigger guard hang on the right side (-X) of the housing. Style everywhere is bold low-poly FF metalwork: every stripe, stud, rune and emblem is its own small flat-coloured part seated on the surface, cyan glow on the blade edge and chamber bores.

Right side is the blunt spine, thicker, with small gold trim bolts spaced along it. parts.builds: The curved grip and trigger assembly. spec.name: Lionheart Gunblade
spec.description: A Final Fantasy style gunblade standing upright on its pommel: a chrome revolve-chamber below, a long blued blade above, trimmed in gold with a crimson lion emblem and glowing runes.
spec.layout: A trophy pose: the gunblade stands vertical, dead centred on x = 0, pommel resting on the floor and the blade tip up at y = 2.2. From the bottom up: a wrapped grip with a flared pommel and a hanging tassel (y 0 to 0.55), a gold trigger guard looped forward with a curved trigger inside (y 0.15 to 0.5, forward of +Z), then the gun mechanism (y 0.5 to 1.0): a six-shot revolver drum with its axle along Y, a barrel housing rising into the blade root, a cocked hammer at the back (−Z), and a side plate carrying the crimson lion emblem. A gold crossguard flare crowns the mechanism (y 0.9 to 1.05), and from it the long blade rises to a pointed tip (y 1.05 to 2.2). The blade's wide flat face looks toward +Z and its width runs along X, so the front view shows the full silhouette: dark steel with a bright polished fuller down the centre, a gold edge inlay, and five glowing amber runes marching up the flat. Everything reads as heavy sculpted metal: faceted low-poly forms, gold fittings at every joint between parts, dark ink seams, crimson accents only on the emblem and grip knot. Rests on the floor only at the pommel base and the trigger guard's lowest curve.

parts.builds: The handle assembly from pommel to the top of the grip. A flared faceted pommel cap (steel, 6-8 sided frustum) sitting exactly on y = 0 at pommelBase, with a gold ring under it and a small gold lion-face stud on each flank. The grip itself: a slightly tapering frustumBox column in gripLeather, wrapped with four evenly spaced raised gripWrap bands and one gold wire band near the top; a crimson cord knot with two short hanging tails (crimson rods, tips in gold) ties off below the guard. The trigger guard: a gold arc swept from the grip front down and forward to a round gold front post at z ≈ +0.14, flat in the XZ plane, thick enough to read as forged (a swept tube with faceted section); inside it hangs the trigger, a curved crimson-steel hook on the trigger joint, with an ink-dark inner face. A small gold ring at the guard's rear top where it meets gripTop.
parts.attaches: Pommel base sits on the floor at pommelBase; the grip's top face meets mechanism at gripTop (y 0.55); the trigger guard's rear ring bolts to gripTop's lower rim.

parts.builds: The gun heart of the weapon, from gripTop to bladeRoot. The revolver drum: a 6-sided faceted cylinder, axis along Y centred on cylinderAxis, radius 0.13, height 0.2, in steelDark with a steel top and bottom cap plate; each of its six flanks carries one recessed chamber: a small steelDark-to-steelInk cylinder stub, and one chamber bears a live brass-gold round head peeking out (gold disc). Gold band rings clamp the drum top and bottom. Behind the drum at the back (−Z), the hammer: a steel forging swept up and back from the mechanism body, a faceted cocked spur with a crimson inlay stripe, riding the hammer joint so it reads as spring-loaded. The barrel housing: a rectangular steel block rising from barrelRoot toward bladeRoot, flanked by two steelInk side plates with three silver hex screw heads each, and a small gold plate on the right flank. The front (facing +Z) carries a barrel muzzle ring (gold) around a dark steelInk bore that continues up into the blade root, and a tiny bone sight bead on top. The lion emblem: a crimson shield-shaped plate (extrude, about 0.16 wide and 0.2 tall) seated proud on the front-right flank of the housing, with a gold stylized lion head built from a few bold extruded blades: a ring mane, a muzzle, two ears and two gold eyes, all seated on the plate, plus ink outline pieces so the emblem reads from two meters.
parts.attaches: Bottom sits on gripTop (y 0.55) centred on cylinderAxis; the hammer hinges at the back of the housing; the top face (barrelRoot to bladeRoot) is covered by the guard part; the drum centre spins on the cylinder joint.

parts.builds: The crossguard and blade root collar, the gold crown of the piece. A swept-back flared guard: two mirrored gold extruded wings (smoothing 2, bevelled, about 0.22 long each) sweeping from the blade root down and back over the drum shoulders like a comb, sharp at their tips, plus one straight gold bar across the front just above the muzzle ring. Where the guard meets the blade at guardTop, a gold collar ring (short faceted lathe) grips the blade root, with a row of eight small steelInk studs studded around it via a ring, and one crimson gem (small octahedron, gold bezel) set at the front centre of the collar. Under the collar, three short steel cooling fins (thin extruded blades) step down the barrel housing so the transition from gun to sword is layered, not abrupt.
parts.attaches: Sits over mechanism's top: the wings land on the drum shoulders at y 0.86-0.9, the collar clamps the blade at guardTop (y 1.05), gem and front bar sit forward toward +Z.

parts.builds: The great blade from guardTop to the tip at y 2.2. One long extruded silhouette in steel, drawn in the XY plane (width along X, thickness along Z about 0.035): root width 0.11 swelling to 0.14 at the mid-blade, then a long taper to a sharp point, with a subtle gunblade recurve on the cutting edge (+X side: gentle S through the length) and a straighter back edge. A raised steelInk fuller rail: a second thin extruded strip seated proud down the centre flat, in steelDark, from collar to the last quarter. The cutting edge wears a silver inlay: a slim silver extruded strip seated along the +X edge face for the whole length. The back (−X) edge carries a short row of three gold serration wedges near the mid-blade. A gold ricasso band crosses the blade just above the collar, and a pierced steelDark rectangle cutout (a small extruded frame) sits mid-blade as a balance hole. The tip's last 0.2 m is capped in silver. Flat shading throughout so the facets read as ground and honed steel.
parts.attaches: Blade root enters the guard's collar at guardTop (y 1.05), riding the bladeJ joint up from bladeRoot.

parts.builds: The magic and finishing details that live on the blade and hilt. Five glowing amber runes (runeGlow, emissive): small extruded angular glyphs, each a different simple mark (chevron, triangle, cross, bar pair, diamond), seated proud on the blade's +Z flat face in a vertical march from y 1.25 to 2.0, each with a thin steelInk outline plate slightly larger behind it so the glow is rimmed. The runes' glow is doubled at the blade root where a faint amber glow seam (a thin glowing strip) runs around the collar, as if the chamber feeds the blade. On the pommel, a hanging tassel upgrade: three bone-coloured cords with crimson tips dangle from the gold pommel ring, each a thin swept rod with a small gold cap bead. A single silver inlaid streak runs diagonally across the mid-blade fuller rail as a battle scar.
parts.attaches: Runes and scar seat on the blade's front flat (blade part); the glow seam wraps the guard collar at guardTop; the tassel hangs from grip's pommel ring at pommelBase.

spec.description: A Final Fantasy-style gunblade standing upright on its pommel: a revolver mechanism fused to a greatsword, barrel running along the blade's spine to a muzzle at the tip, brass filigree and a glowing cyan magic stone.
spec.layout: The weapon stands bolt upright on its pommel at the origin, fully vertical, model front (+Z) is the blade's cutting-edge side, back (−Z) is the spine where the barrel runs. From the floor upward: brass-capped pommel with a red gem at y 0-0.1; the leather-wrapped grip tapering up to y 0.62 with a brass trigger guard loop facing +Z and a steel trigger inside it; the revolver mechanism block y 0.62-1.02 with a six-flute dark drum at its centre, a brass stud ring, a top strap bridging over the drum and a hammer cocked back at −Z; the crossguard with wing-like quillons and a glowing cyan crystal seated where blade meets mechanism at y ~1.05; the greatsword blade slab rising to y 2.18, widest at the ricasso and sweeping to a spear tip, its polished cutting edge facing +Z, a dark fuller groove running up the flats, a brass heraldic wing emblem engraved on both sides near the base and a column of rune studs marching up one flat; the octagonal gunmetal barrel clamped to the blade's spine (−Z side) by two brass bands, terminating in a ringed muzzle brake and front sight just below the tip. Style everywhere: cold faceted low-poly steel with hard black seams, warm brass fittings with rivets and engraved trim, dark oiled leather on the grip, one strong cyan magic glow at the guard crystal and a fainter glow down the muzzle bore.

parts.builds: The lower hilt standing on the floor. Pommel: a small turned dome (lathe) of brass with a dark steelLow collar under it and a faceted ruby cabochon set in its cap, its lowest point touching y=0. Grip body: a tapered octagonal prism (frustumBox or sweep with 8 sides) in gripWood from y 0.08 to 0.6, leaning a hair toward −Z so the weapon balances over the drum. Leather wrap: 4 broad diagonal straps (thin swept bands or slabs) of leather wrapping the grip at a spiral, each edged with a hairline of leatherDark, and 3 brass band stitches crossing them. Trigger guard: a flat brass loop (swept arc or extruded band, ~8 mm thick) bulging forward (+Z) from the grip front down to the guard bow, with a small brass rivet at each end. Trigger: a slender curved steelMid blade hanging inside the guard on the trigger joint, with an ink outline sliver. Lanyard: a small brass ring on the pommel's left side (+X) with a 4-link dark chain and a short leather tassel hanging free but never touching the floor (ends above y=0.02). Every piece rides the weapon joint except the trigger, which rides the trigger joint.
parts.attaches: Pommel bottom rests on y=0 (floor part). Grip top end caps onto the mechanism's frame at mount gripTop [0, 0.62, 0]; the trigger hinge sits inside the guard bow.

parts.builds: The revolver action block between grip and blade. Drum: a six-flute cylinder (lathe with 6 flat segments, radius 0.13, axis vertical) in gunmetal riding the drum joint, each flute face wearing an ink seam line, with a ring of 6 small brass bolt heads around its top face and a steelLight ejector star on its centre cap. Frame: a gunmetal housing (loft or frustumBox pair) that wraps the drum from the grip top up to drumTop, with steelDark side plates on both flats (±X), each plate carrying a panel of brass inlay lines and 4 rivets. Top strap: a steelMid bridge arching over the drum front-to-back with an ink slot and a brass screw at each end. Hammer: a steelDark spur cocked back over the −Z side at the top of the frame, pivoting visually on a brass pin, with a steelLight notch on its face. Loading gate: a small hinged brass plate on the frame's right flat (−X) with a knurled thumb piece. Barrel breech: a short stout steelDark collar at the frame's top-centre where the barrel will slot in, facing up. Everything rides the weapon joint except the drum itself.
parts.attaches: Frame bottom sockets down over mount gripTop [0, 0.62, 0]; frame top hands off to blade and fittings at mount drumTop [0, 1.02, 0]; the barrel breech collar meets the barrel part at mount barrelRoot [0, 1.06, -0.1].

parts.builds: The greatsword blade. Main slab: an extruded blade silhouette (wide ricasso ~0.24 m across at the base in Z, gentle forward curve, sweeping to a spear point at y 2.18) built along +Y with its thickness along X (thickness tapering 0.05 to 0.02, bevelled), faceted in steelMid. Cutting edge: a polished edgePolished strip (thin extrude or swept bevel) running the full +Z face of the blade from ricasso to tip. Fuller: a recessed groove (a slim ink-topped steelDark inset slab) running up the centre of each flat from y 1.1 to y 1.7. Ricasso etch: a brass heraldic wing emblem built from 6-10 small angled slabs and a round brass boss, mirrored on both flats at y ~1.2. Runes: a column of 7 small glowing cyan rune studs (tiny extruded glyphs) marching up the +X flat from y 1.3 to 1.9. Spine cap: a steelLight strip along the blade's −Z spine that the barrel sits against, with an ink seam under it. Tip facet: the last 0.15 m of the blade split into two steelLight chamfer faces meeting the polished edge, so the point reads bright. All rides the weapon joint.
parts.attaches: Blade base seats down onto mount drumTop [0, 1.02, 0] inside the crossguard's ring; the spine strip (−Z face of the box) receives the barrel part along mount barrelRoot [0, 1.06, -0.1]; the crossguard from fittings wraps this box at mount guardPlane.

parts.builds: The gun barrel along the blade's back. Barrel body: an octagonal tube (sweep with 8 sides or stacked frustumBoxes) in gunmetal, radius ~0.045, running from the mechanism's breech at y 1.06 straight up to y 2.02, hugging the blade's spine at z ≈ −0.13, with 2 thin ink cooling-ring seams along its length. Muzzle: a brass reinforcing ring at the top, then a short steelDark crown cylinder with a recessed bore whose inner face is a glowing cyan disc (glow at strength 1) so the bore reads lit; a small steelLight front-sight blade rises from the ring toward the sword tip. Barrel bands: 2 brass clamp bands (short swept loops) wrapping barrel and spine strip together at y ~1.35 and y ~1.7, each with 3 rivet heads and an ink shadow line under the band. Rear sight: a tiny notched steelLight leaf on the first band. All rides the weapon joint.
parts.attaches: Barrel root slots into the mechanism's breech collar at mount barrelRoot [0, 1.06, -0.1] and its bands clamp onto the spine strip of the bladeCore box; its muzzle stops just below the blade tip.

parts.builds: The crossguard and magic furniture at the blade base. Crossguard: a broad swept brass plate (extrude or slab pair) wrapping the blade's base at y 1.02-1.12, flaring out ±X into two upturned wing-shaped quillons whose tips curl toward +Z, each wing edged with brassDark trim and 3 rivets, with an ink shadow line where it meets the drum top. Gem mount: at the guard's front-centre a brass rosette cradling a faceted cyan crystal (octahedron or low-seg lathe), glowing bright (glowCyan, glow strength 1.4) with a glowCore inner core part. Filigree: 4 slender brassDark filigree strips and 2 small wing fins laid on the guard's top face. Chains: two short 3-link dark chains (steelDark links) drooping from the guard's left and right quillon roots back to the mechanism's frame side plates, hanging within this box. Side plates: 2 small steelLight shoulder plates seating against the drum top, riveted in brass. All rides the weapon joint.
parts.attaches: Guard ring seats down onto mount drumTop [0, 1.02, 0] around the bladeCore base and against the mechanism's frame top; chain upper ends meet the mechanism frame's side plates, lower ends anchor at the quillon roots at mount guardPlane [0, 1.06, 0].

The shapes are bold and ornate, with an elegant tall silhouette. Polished steel in two or three tones (light top bevels, darker fuller and underside), gold filigree trim, dark gunmetal mechanics, small crimson and cyan accents, and glow on the core, the chamber rim and the runes. I'm designing a Final Fantasy-style gunblade, Squall's Revolver-like, as a static model with no joints, planted point-down so its tip touches the floor at y=0.

Actually I think the pommel-down orientation reads more iconic, with the blade pointing up and the grip resting on the floor at a total length of about 1.4m — cutting edge on +X, spine on -X, with the revolver cylinder and barrel mounted along the spine near the base of the blade and the trigger guard positioned below at the grip.

Now I'm laying out the full dimensions: grip, pommel, and trigger assembly spanning roughly y 0 to 0.42, with the trigger guard extending toward the edge side (+X) since the blade's flat face points toward the viewer (+Z) and the edge faces left.

Continuing upward, the receiver/gun mechanism housing sits around y 0.40-0.75, then the blade runs y 0.62-1.45, tapering from a wider base to a swept clipped point at the tip, with a spine rim, fuller groove, and light edge bevel. For ornamentation I'm planning a "Crest & Trim" piece: a lion-head pendant with chain, engraved runes, and emblems to echo the Revolver's iconic lion motif on the guard.

I'm working out a draping chain from the guard's side loop down to a lion-head medallion pendant, plus glowing blue magic gems embedded in the receiver and cylinder. I'm settling on four parts -- grip, mechanism, blade, and ornaments -- with a budget split of 150/200/250/150 for 750 total, and picking out a steel, gunmetal, gold, and leather color palette.

Now I'm placing mount points: grip-to-receiver junction, receiver center, blade base, guard center, and the revolver cylinder, reasoning through how the cylinder's axis should run parallel to the blade like a real gunblade design.

I'm recentering the blade geometry so the centerline sits near x=0, adjusting the pendant and spine offsets so the overall bounding box spans roughly -0.15 to 0.17 in width.

Now I'm defining the orientation convention: blade flats facing ±Z, edge at +X, spine at -X, lion pendant facing +Z, with the trigger guard loop lying flat in the XY plane and extending outward toward +X before curving back down to the grip, and the pendant chain attaching near the guard's outer edge.

I'm laying out the pommel, grip, trigger loop, and collar segments, then stacking the crossguard, receiver body with its hammer, and the blade ricasso up through the tip, defining the floor and spatial bounds for each part as I go.

Grouping ornaments next: a lion medallion, chain, and a feather or ribbon tassel tied near the pommel's lanyard ring, making sure the tassel stays above the floor line rather than hanging below zero.

spec.description: A Final Fantasy VIII-style gunblade standing upright on its pommel: a long single-edged silver blade with a revolver mechanism in the hilt, gold filigree, glowing crystals and a lion pendant on a chain.
spec.layout: Static prop, no joints, standing upright on its flat round pommel base (y=0) with the blade pointing up; the tip is at y=1.5. From bottom to top: pommel disc and wrapped grip (y 0-0.40), revolver mechanism (0.40-0.66), winged crossguard (0.66-0.80), blade (0.80-1.50). The single-edged blade is a thin slab in the YZ plane, about 0.03 thick in x. Its sharp edge faces -Z, and its thick spine faces +Z toward the front. The trigger, trigger guard and a protruding hammer all face +Z. The revolver cylinder sits just below the crossguard with its axis along X, and its six chambers show on both x sides. The lion pendant hangs from a ring at the pommel's +X side on a short chain and rests on the floor beside the base, leaning slightly. Silhouette: a slim, elegant, slightly ornate Final Fantasy blade. A tall, narrow blade is contrasted by a chunky gun block and flared gold wing-shaped guard tips (tips curve upward and slightly back). Every part follows one three-layer colour rule: dark ink outline or recess, main colour, bright highlight line. Metal is cool silver-blue and trim is warm gold. Glowing crystal accents in cyan (blade runes, guard gem) and ruby (pommel gem) use the glow kit. The lion motif repeats on the guard centre, the cylinder side plates, the pommel cap and the pendant. Blocky faceted primitives only; detail comes from small seated parts.

The spine (+Z side) is a thicker steelMid strip (0.05 thick) with a row of small ink notches. The upper third of the spine carries the revolver-style barrel ridge: a slim gunmetal bar with a dark muzzle slit at the tip's underside. On both x faces there is a long recessed fuller groove in fullerBlue with an edgeBright highlight line above it, tapering toward the tip. 4-5 tiny rune glyphs (crystalCyan, glowing) are inset along the fuller. A lion engraving (steelDark) sits near the ricasso. Two or three gold rivets. A jagged cut-out of 3 notches near the tip on the edge side (Squall-style), outlined in ink. The tang is a steelDark block hidden down into the guard (y 0.76-0.80). Very thin faceted bevel pieces, nothing round.
parts.attaches: The base sits on the guard at bladeBase (y=0.80), centred at z=-0.015. The tang drops into the guard's blade slot. Nothing else touches the blade.

spec.name: Ashen Hydra of the Nine Realms

Five serpentine necks rise from the hump and splay like a fan: the central hero neck is tallest (head at y = 3.5, z = 2.25, facing +Z with jaw open), a mid pair reaches y = 3.0 with heads at x = ±1.8, and an outer pair reaches y = 2.75 with heads at x = ±2.3; all heads face forward (+Z) with slightly splayed, snarling angles. Style on every part: deep pine-green scale hide with pale horn belly, bone-coloured horns, crest and fangs, gold trim rings and brow ornaments in the God of War manner, glowing ember-orange runes and eyes (kit glow), moss accents on upward faces, dark ink mouth interiors. Belly scutes: b.along over the body with pale belly frustumBox plates ringed in bellyShade, widest under the hump. Ember runes: 6-7 small extruded rune plates stuck on the flanks near the hump in ember colour, each glow()-ed at 1.4 with a tiny emberCore core dot. Tail tip: a paired bone barb. spec.name: Ashen Five-Headed Hydra
spec.description: A colossal God-of-War-style hydra: a moss-scaled serpent bulk with pale belly scutes, dark dorsal spikes, broken iron shackles and glowing teal runes, five horned heads with open fanged jaws and ember-lit throats rising spread from its shoulders.
spec.layout: Facing +Z the viewer sees a fan of five serpentine necks rising from the shoulders of a massive low serpent chest: the central neck tallest with its head highest at y≈4.0 staring straight ahead, two mid necks at x=±1.1 a head lower, and two outer necks splayed out to x=±1.8 lowest of all, all five jaws open showing teeth. Behind and below them the huge chest dominates the centre, its pale belly plates resting on the floor from z≈-0.8 to z≈2.0, with dark dorsal spikes along its spine and glowing teal rune sigils on each flank plus a broken iron shackle ring at its front. The tail sweeps back from z≈-0.6, tapering and curling upward to a bone spade fin near z=-4.6. Style on every part: ashen desaturated moss-greens with hard flat tonal breaks, weathered bone horn, dark forge-iron shackles and chain links, small glowing teal rune pieces and ember/yellow glow eyes as separate emissive parts, and deep-ink seams and outlines as their own seated pieces.

spec.description: A colossal five-headed Norse swamp hydra in a gritty, grim God of War style: scarred dark-green hide, bone and iron war-trophies, glowing blue runes, ember wounds and frost.
spec.layout: A squat, heavy four-legged reptilian beast, 9.9 m long, standing on y=0 and facing +Z. The torso is a low barrel (y 1.4–3.2, z -2.7 to 2.3) with a broad, armoured shoulder hump at z≈1.2. Five thick serpent necks root on that hump and fan out and up in a spread bouquet. Each neck rises, then arches forward, and ends in a head that dips slightly. The centre head (Mid) is the hero: tallest and biggest, head top at y≈5.8, horns to 6.2, snout tip z≈4.7. Inner heads LA (+X) and RA (-X) are about 80% scale at y≈4.6, x=±1.65, snout z≈4.5. Outer heads LB (+X) and RB (-X) are about 70% scale, lower at y≈3.8, flaring wide at x=±2.9, snout z≈4.0. A tail trails back and down to a bone-spiked club at z≈-5.2. Front legs are thick, elbows out and forward. Hind legs are digitigrade, hocks back. Each foot has 3 big claws and 1 dew-claw. The tail and legs are the only parts on the floor. A readable silhouette has a low heavy mass in the back, a fan of five necks and a clear gap between the heads. Palette use: the top of everything is darker green-grey (hideDark, hideMid) with moss on upward faces. Throats and bellies are pale bone-beige (belly, bellyShade), and mud (mud) sits at feet, belly edge and tail tip. Style (God of War 2018): desaturated, heavy, brutal and mythic. Chunky blocky scale plates are layered into overlapping armour rows, with torn flesh and old scars as pale (scarPale) thin sweeps. Hand-carved Nordic runes glow (runeBlue) on horns, bone bands and the back. Iron shackles and broken chain links hang from the body. Broken weapons (the Leviathan-style frost axe, spear shafts, arrows) are embedded in the hide. Orange ember (ember, emberGlow) glows in wounds, mouths and eyes, and frost blue (frost) rimes one head. Every head has its own identity (see parts). All details are small separate parts in their own flat colours seated on the surface, with a dark outline, then the main colour, then a fine highlight. Rest pose: all five heads face forward, jaws slightly parted and each lower jaw a separate part, necks spread, legs apart, tail straight back with a slight droop.

spec.name: Hydra of the Broken Spears
spec.description: A hulking five-headed hydra in God of War style: blackened scarred hide, bone-white horns and fangs, rune-brands and wounds glowing ember-red, bronze spears and chains still lodged in its flesh.
spec.layout:
A four-legged swamp-reptile titan facing +Z, front to back along z. The torso is a deep barrel (x +-1.5, y 1.5-3.6, z -2.4 to 2.4) with a heavy shoulder hump at the front. Four stout legs stand on y=0, hind legs digitigrade (knee forward, hock back), front legs with elbows back, each ending in three or four big bone claws. A thick tail leaves the rump, slopes down toward the floor and ends in a bone spade-blade at about z=-5.3.

Five necks leave the chest top at z~1.8 and fan out in a rest pose, separated and not tangled, each rising, arcing forward and ending in a head that looks forward and slightly down. Neck A is the centre (x=0, tallest, head y~4.9). Necks B and C are inner left (+x) and inner right (-x), heads at x=+-2.0, y~4.5. Necks D and E are outer left and right, lower and splayed, heads at x=+-3.2, y~3.7. Silhouette from the front is a crown fan: the centre is highest, the outer heads lowest, with a clear gap between heads. The overall profile is a bulky, heavy-shouldered mass with long thin necks. Every head has an upper jaw on headX and a separate lower jaw on jawX, mouths shut or very slightly open, because the rig opens them.

STYLE (God of War, grim Norse/Greek myth): desaturated, cold, battle-worn. Hide is blackened green-grey (dark on top and flanks, dirty pale belly and throat plates underneath). Blocky chunky shapes with faceted low-poly segments. Each part gets broad plate and scale shapes: big overlapping dorsal and neck plates in a hideDark -> hideMid -> hideLight root-to-tip order, never fine noise. Warm accents are used sparingly and glow: ember-red and rune-orange cracks, rune brands and mouth interiors (the builder should use glow() from the glow kit on rune brands, eyes and mouth ember). Wounds, claw-scar slashes and dried blood strips in scarFlesh and blood. Souvenirs of past heroes: broken bronze spears and a lodged axe in the back, iron shackles and snapped chains on the ankles and necks, bronze armour scraps bolted into the hide. Bone horns, fangs and claws are big and clear. Mud and grime go on the feet (hideDark patches), and the belly is paler. Every surface is one flat colour per part; scars, runes, seams, rivets and eyes are small separate parts seated on the surface.

What each part owns is listed under parts. Everything meets at the mounts: necks start at neckBase*, heads at head*, legs at hip*, tail at tailRoot.

parts.builds: The barrel torso and everything lodged in it. One smooth loft/sweep body skinned over hips, spine and chest (belly sags lower and is pale 'belly' colour via sectors; flanks hideMid, back hideDark) with a heavy shoulder hump at the front where the five necks sprout, and a thinner waist to the rump. Exposed rib ridges on the flanks (curved boneDark bars under the hide), a double row of big dorsal bone plates (hideDark root -> boneDark tip) along the spine from the shoulders to the rump (tailRoot), and pale belly plates (rows of flat 'belly' bands). Hide texture as chunky overlapping scale plates in hideMid/hideLight in patches, with mud/grime on the lower flanks in hideDark. Battle damage: three long diagonal claw-slash scars (scarFlesh strips with blood edges), a stitched leather-and-iron cauterised stump scar on the shoulder with glowing ember cracks (ember, glow), and rune brands (small runeGlow shapes of Norse-style angular glyphs, glow) on both flanks. Souvenirs: 3-4 broken bronze spears (bronzeDark shafts, bronze bands, iron heads) at slants in the back and flank, one big double-bladed iron axe (ironDark haft, iron head) buried in the left shoulder, a shattered bronze Spartan-style shield-rim shard bolted into the right flank with rivets, and two iron chains (chain, ironDark links as small torus/box links) wrapped around the chest and snapped, trailing links over the shoulder. Includes the neck-root collars: a thick scarred ring of hide plates around each of the five neck roots at neckBase*, sized to the neck radius (about 0.45 m for A, 0.4 m for B/C, 0.35 m for D/E) so the neck sweeps emerge from them. Belongs to joints hips, spine, chest. It does NOT build legs, tail, necks or heads.
parts.attaches: Neck roots at neckBaseA..E (chest joint). Leg tops at hipFL/FR (chest) and hipHL/HR (hips). Tail begins at tailRoot (hips). Dorsal plates run from shoulderHump to tailRoot along spineTop.

parts.builds: All four legs, standing on y=0 (claws sink up to 0.05 m into the floor). Front legs (FL, FR) elbow-back, heavy forearms, hind legs (HL, HR) digitigrade with big thighs, knee forward, hock back; use limb IK from the hip mounts to the foot mounts. Each leg is a smooth sweep on its joint chain (hip, knee, ankle, toe) with a muscular thigh/upper arm (radius about 0.5 at the hip tapering to 0.22 at the ankle), hideMid on the outside with hideDark underside; scale plates (hideLight edged) stacked down the front of each shin, a spiked knee/elbow spur (boneDark), and a broad four-toed foot with big curved bone claws (claw colour at the tip, boneDark base; 4 toes on front feet, 3 forward plus a dewclaw on hinds) spread out, plus toe pads and mud/grime patches in hideDark on the lower leg and foot. Details: an iron shackle ring (iron with ironDark rivets) around each ankle with a snapped chain stub dangling (chain links); fresh scars; rune bands (runeGlow, glow) on the thighs. The four legs are consistent mirrors (+x left): 2 of each. Belongs to joints hipFL..toeHR.
parts.attaches: Tops meet the torso underside at hipFL/FR and hipHL/HR (the leg radius at the hip should overlap the torso). Feet at footFL, footFR, footHL, footHR on the floor.

parts.builds: The long thick tail, a smooth sweep over tail1..tail6 starting at tailRoot with radius 0.6 and tapering to 0.12, sloping down toward the floor and ending in a bone spade-blade. Countershaded: back hideDark, flanks hideMid, underside belly colour (sectors). A row of dorsal plates along the top continuing the torso's row (hideDark root -> boneDark tip) shrinking to the tip, side ridges of hideLight scale plates, banded scars (scarFlesh ring cuts) and ember-glow cracks (ember, glow) between plates. Near the base an iron shackle band (iron + ironDark rivets) with a snapped chain hanging. At the tip (tailTip) a big flat bone spade/blade extrude (bone, with boneDark notched edge, a central ridge, and a runeGlow glyph, glow) plus two side barbs. Belongs to joints tail1..tail6.
parts.attaches: Starts at tailRoot, where the torso rump ends (overlap the rump radius slightly). Tip at tailTip.

parts.builds: The five neck tubes from the chest roots to the head joints, each a smooth sweep skinned over its three neck joints (A: neckA1..A3, B: neckB1..3, C: neckC1..3, D: neckD1..3, E: neckE1..3), starting at neckBase* and ending at head*, where the head's skull overlaps the neck end. Radii: A 0.4 to 0.28, B/C 0.36 to 0.26, D/E 0.32 to 0.24. Colours by place: the back is hideDark -> hideMid, the throat/underside is 'belly' with ladder bands of throat plates. Each neck has a row of dorsal spine plates (hideDark, boneDark tips) and a pair of small side frills. Each neck wears its own history: A has two iron bands with rivets and a snapped chain; B has scarFlesh slash scars with stitching; C has a lodged broken bronze spear tip and a bloody wound; D has a bronze armour scrap bolted on with leather straps; E has glowing ember cracks (glow) and a rune brand. Add neck rings of scale plates in hideLight and a few small bone spikes. Mirror B/C and D/E consistently (+x left). Belongs to the neck joints only (not heads or jaws).
parts.attaches: Roots at neckBaseA..E, which the torso collars surround. Each neck ends at headA..E, where the heads begin; necks stop at the head joint.

parts.builds: All five dragon-like heads, built with one reusable head helper scaled per head (A 1.15, B and C 1.0, D and E 0.9; each head about 1.4 m long including snout, 0.7 m wide), at the headA..E mounts, each facing its joint's dir. Each head is a skull (hideMid with hideDark top) and a blocky tapered snout on the head joint (upper jaw: palate, upper teeth row of 8-10 bone fangs plus two long fangs), and a SEPARATE lower jaw on the jaw joint (jawA..E; chin, lower teeth row, tongue in tongue colour, throat in mouthInner, with a small glowing ember ember (glow) inside the mouth). The mouth is shut or only slightly open. Face: two big angry eyes seated on the sides of the skull (eyeAmber glow, with an eyeSlit vertical pupil and a dark brow ridge hideDark over them for a scowl), nostril holes on the snout tip, a heavy brow ridge, cheek frill of bone spikes, and a pair of large swept-back horns (horn colour with hornTip ends, ringed with boneDark bands), plus 2 small side horns and a short crest of plates down the back of the skull. Individual traits: A is the largest with a crown of 4 horns and a bronze circlet scrap; B has a broken horn (stump) and a slashed cheek (scarFlesh); C has a blinded eye (frost milky eye with a scar slash across it); D has an iron muzzle band with rivets and a chain; E has extra spikes and glowing ember cracks (glow) on the brow. Mirror B/C and D/E (+x left). Heads' parts ride headX (skull, upper jaw, horns, eyes) and jawX (lower jaw, lower teeth, tongue). Details seated on the head surface: wrinkles, scale plates, rune brand on forehead of A (runeGlow, glow). Do NOT build any neck tube.
parts.attaches: Each head's back of skull sits on the neck end at headA..E; the jaw hinge is jawA..E, slightly below and behind the eye.

calls.reasoning:
I'm sketching the spec for a five-headed hydra in a God of War aesthetic—grim Norse/Greek styling with rune-carved bronze and iron, red accents, scars, and chains. I'm planning a quadruped body roughly 6 wide, 5.5 tall, and 8 long, with five necks splaying outward into heads in a resting pose, facing forward along +Z.

Now I'm breaking the model into parts: the torso with ribs, scars, chain harness, and spine ridge; four stout clawed legs; a long curving tail ending in a bone blade; and the five necks with scaled ridges. I'm weighing how to divide the heads across build functions since five is an awkward number—considering splitting them unevenly between two part-builders or just handling all five heads in a single dedicated function.

I'm settling on five total parts—body, legs, tail, necks, heads—and sketching a rough budget across them (roughly 190/170/100/180/260), while planning the joint hierarchy: hips and spine as roots, four joints per neck plus head and jaw joints for each of the five heads, three or four joints per leg, six for the tail. I'm now placing coordinates for the torso and spine chain, figuring out hip height and leg segment lengths so the creature's feet reach the floor properly.

Now I'm working out joint placement for each leg, naming hip/knee/ankle/toe chains per side (front legs stouter, hind legs bigger and more digitigrade), assigning rough XYZ coordinates for each joint so the stance looks like a reptilian hydra body.

Next I'm turning to the five necks, giving each an id (n0 center, n1/n2 inner left/right, n3/n4 outer left/right), setting their base coordinates spread across the chest, and planning a rising, arcing rest pose for them.

Then I'm placing the heads at the end of each neck: center head front-up, inner heads slightly lower and spread, outer heads widest and lowest. I'm checking the overall creature dimensions, settling on roughly 7 wide, 5.8 tall, 10 long, with z spanning -5 to 5.

I'm naming the five necks A through E (center, inner-left, inner-right, outer-left, outer-right), each with three joints plus a head, and working out coordinates for neck A's base, midpoints, and head position.

Still plotting neck coordinates...

Mirroring heads C and E to negative x, varying head heights for a fan shape, and maybe giving one head a scar for character. Now working out the tail path, curving it down from the neck base toward the floor where the tip could rest.

Continuing the tail curve down to z=-5, y=0.35, ending in a spade blade, keeping lateral movement minimal for a rest pose, and deciding the tip doesn't actually need to touch the floor since that's reserved for the legs. Moving on to defining the torso and leg boxes with their rough dimensions.

For style, I'm leaning heavily into a God of War Norse aesthetic — dark ash-grey or blackened green-grey scaly hide, bone-white horns and fangs, rust-red war paint with ember-glow accents in the mouth and cracks, a cold blue-grey palette offset by Kratos-red highlights, and armor made of blood-stained bronze Greek/Norse plates with embedded chains and carved runes.

The body carries embedded broken spears and swords stuck in like trophies, chains, scars, and a stitched cauterized stump, while the heads carry the horns, fangs, eyes, and jaw details. I'm laying out a limited palette of around 24 colors covering hide tones, pale belly, scar flesh, bone, horn, and claw shades to keep everything cohesive.

Rounding out the palette with amber eyes, dark eye slits, mouth and tongue reds, ember and rune glow oranges, iron and bronze metals, chain grey, blood red, frost blue, ink black, and leather wrap brown—tallying up to confirm it lands at exactly 24 distinct colors.

Now I'm mapping out the skeleton hierarchy: hips as root with spine and chest above it, tail joints branching off hips, hind legs attached to hips while front legs and necks attach to chest, heads capping the necks, and jaws hinging off heads. I'm also working out approximate 3D positions and forward-facing directions for each joint, starting with the hips and spine coordinates.

Still placing leg joints...

Letting the toes touch the floor with claws resting at ground level, then mirroring everything to the right side with negated x-coordinates. I'm naming each joint by role (leg segments, digits) and now moving on to the neck chain, placing neckA1 through neckA3 as they curve upward and forward from the chest base toward where the head will attach.

Head and jaw joints follow, with the skull plus snout forming the head length and the mouth hinging slightly below. I'm then laying out the B and D neck chains as offset mirrors sweeping outward in x, with C and E as their negative-x counterparts.

Now I'm defining bounding boxes for each body part—torso, legs, tail, necks, heads—checking that dorsal plates and spears stay within the torso's upper y bound and that the neck/head boxes extend far enough in x to cover the horns.

For surface detail I'm sketching torso features: a belly plate row, visible ribs at the flank, dorsal bone ridges, embedded broken spears and a lodged axe, chest chains with locks, glowing rune scars, stitched wounds, and shredded Spartan armor fragments bolted to the shoulders, plus blood-streaked cut marks. I'm starting on the legs now, describing muscular thighs and scale texture.

For the legs, tail, and necks I'm working out individual markings: knee spikes, bone claws, a broken ankle shackle, mud near the feet, and rune bands running along them. The tail gets dorsal spikes, ridge plates, a notched bone-spade tip with runes, and its own broken chain at the base, while each neck is given unique scarring -- cauterized rings, embedded arrowheads, bone frill fins, and throat markings that differ from head to head.

Now I'm designing the five heads individually: each gets its own skull shape, jaw, horns, brow, and glowing amber slit-eyes with ember light inside the mouth, but I'm giving them distinct personalities -- A is tallest with crown horns, B has a broken horn, C has a scarred blind eye, D wears an iron muzzle band, and E is spiked. I'm tallying the part budgets (190+170+100+180+260=900) to confirm everything fits, then structuring the compact JSON output with mounts, description, and style notes covering the dark, grimy, ember-lit, rune-covered aesthetic.

Writing joint hierarchy...

I'm figuring out how to build the legs since the joints already exist — I'll use sweep with the existing joint list as the bone chain rather than creating new ones, tracing a path through each joint's position.

For the front legs I'll follow the hip-knee-ankle-toe positions as given, and for the hind legs the zigzag path with the hock angled back, using a polyline instead of a smooth curve so the sweep rounds the corners naturally. I'm also planning the radius taper along each leg, picking a hide-toned color scheme, and layering in extra details like a knee spur spike and shin plates per leg.

Now I'm working out how to place small shin plate boxes along the tube at a fixed angle so they sit on the front-facing side of the limb, then building the toes as capsules fanning forward from the toe joint.

For each toe, I'm creating a tapered rod from base to tip with a dark bone material, plus a curved claw spike at the tip tilted downward, and double-checking that the foot pad and toe geometry stay clear of the floor plane.

Now I'm adding an iron shackle torus around the ankle oriented along the leg direction, with small rivet spheres and a short hanging chain of alternating torus links, then placing a glowing rune band torus around the upper thigh near the hip.

For the thigh rune glow, I'm computing the sweep position and tangent along the leg path to orient the torus correctly, sizing its radius slightly larger than the limb's local radius at that point so it wraps cleanly. I'm also adding scar marks and blood near the mid-thigh, plus mud patches on the lower leg using flattened dark spheres.

spec.description: The cramped, worn mess galley of a 1970s commercial towing vessel: a grated deck, a central mess table under a lit dome, a beverage dispenser wall, a prep counter and a hatch, all in worn beige panels with yellow trim and glowing green screens.
spec.layout: A one-room interior: +Z is the way a crew member faces when seated at the table looking at the dispenser wall. A grated metal deck platform (0.16 m thick) covers the whole footprint and is the only part on the floor; everything else stands on its top at y = 0.16. Centered at x = 0, z = 0.4 sits the mess table: a chunky pedestal with an octagonal top, an angled console wedge with glowing screens, and a curved bench seat around it; directly above at y = 2.3 a lit acrylic dome on a yellow rim frame reaches up to the ceiling. The back wall (z = -2.4) carries the beverage dispenser machine with cup shelf and glowing indicator lights, tall lockers and a conduit run. The port side wall (x = -1.6) carries a steel prep counter with overhead cabinets, an urn and hanging mugs. The starboard side wall (x = +1.6) carries the entry hatch frame, wall panels, a valve-and-pipe run and a wall lamp. A beam-grid ceiling with light strips and fat conduits closes the room at y = 2.3-2.85. Every part reads as worn 1979 industrial: beige and olive rectangular panels with recessed seams, yellow trim strips and hazard chevrons on edges, rivet rows on plate joins, glass screens glowing flat green or amber, all built from blocky primitives with the detail seated on top as small parts of their own colours.

spec.name: Nostromo Galley
spec.description: A retro-futuristic spaceship mess and galley corner from the USCSS Nostromo (Alien, 1979): ribbed bone-coloured walls, a cream counter with beverage and warming equipment, a wall bank of glowing CRT monitors, the iconic molded mess table with attached stools, and a bristling ceiling of pipes and conduit over a steel deck.
spec.layout: A cut-away room section: the viewer looks in through the open +Z face. A steel deck plate floor covers the whole footprint and rests on y = 0 (only floor-touching part). The back wall (z = -2.5) carries the galley: a counter run 0.95 m high with equipment, and above it a wall-mounted CRT monitor bank. The left wall (x = -2.3) carries lockers and stacked storage crates; the right wall (x = +2.3) carries a ribbed panel section and a round pressure hatch. A ceiling slab closes the top with pipes, conduit runs and two cone lamps hanging over the mess table, which stands centre-front with its cluster of attached swivel stools. Style on every part: warm bone and cream molded-plastic surfaces like airliner interiors, dark olive-grey machinery, corrugated ribbing on every flat wall, warning-yellow stripe accents, rust and copper fittings, amber and green glowing CRT screens, everything chunky, functional and 1979-industrial.

parts.builds: The room section itself. Steel deck floor of rectangular plates with seam grooves, a raised grating strip near the back, all in floor colour with rust stains and a warning-yellow painted stripe across the doorway end. Three walls: back wall, left wall, right wall, built as chunky ribbed panel walls — flat wall-coloured panels with repeated vertical rib slats in rib colour, dark seam lines, corner posts in iron, a black kick skirting at the bottom and a pipe-and-conduit raceway band at mid height with small valve wheels in brass and rust. The right wall holds a round pressure hatch: lathe-built ring, rivet ring, spokes, a warning-yellow and black chevron stripe band around it and a small stencil-style plate. The ceiling slab closes the top with recessed panel frames and two square light-well openings the ceiling-services part drops into. Wall edges frame the open +Z face with a thick girder border so the cut-away reads as a ship section.
parts.attaches: Owns the whole footprint; its floor top is mount deckTop that galleyCounter, messTable and lockersShelf stand on; its back wall face is mount backWallFace for galleyCounter and monitorBank; its left wall face is mount leftWallFace for lockersShelf; its ceiling underside is mount ceilingLine for ceilingServices.

parts.builds: Everything under the ceiling: a dense overhead services run. Two large parallel copper pipes (pipeCopper) running front-to-back with flanged ring joints every metre and elbow bends, a bundle of steel conduit pipes (pipeSteel) in a cable tray, a smaller olive cable duct, hanging black cable loops with clip rings, and two cone pendant lamps in iron hanging on short stems over the mess table position, each with a glowing warm lampGlow shade disc. Add a small junction box in machine grey with an orange stripe, a hanging hose reel with a coiled rubber hose, and riveted mounting brackets in iron connecting everything to mount ceilingLine. Pipes must not drop below y = 2.05 so the room stays open.
parts.attaches: Hangs from mount ceilingLine on the roomShell ceiling underside; its lamp cones hang above the messTable footprint.

parts.builds: The galley counter run along the back wall, standing on mount deckTop and backing onto mount backWallFace. A machine-grey cabinet base with cream cabinet doors (thin seam gaps, small black pulls), a chunky ivory worktop with a raised lip, and equipment across it: a tall beverage dispenser tower in chalk with an orange stripe band, two brass dispensing nozzles and a small drip tray; a countertop warming oven with a dark glass door, rust handle and amber indicator jewel lights; a sink recess with a steel tap and drying rack; a wall shelf above the worktop holding mugs and canisters in olive, rust and chalk. A tiled-ish backsplash strip in machine grey with a warning-yellow stripe, a rubber floor mat in front, and a small wall-mounted extinguisher in rust. Details read as seated parts: indicator lights, valve knobs, seams, stripe bands each their own colour.
parts.attaches: Stands on mount deckTop, backs onto mount backWallFace; its worktop height 1.2 m leaves clear wall above for monitorBank.

parts.builds: The wall-mounted monitor console above the galley counter, meeting mount backWallFace. An iron mounting frame bolted to the wall carries a bank of four CRT screens in dark casings: two larger green glowing screens with scanline frames and surrounding bezels, one amber glowing screen, one small amber data readout, all with glow (self-lit) treatment on the screen faces only. Below and beside the screens: a chunky control panel in machine grey with rows of chunky switches (black toggles with orange and warning-coloured caps), push buttons in brass and rust, and a stencil-style data placard. Cable ducts in black run from the frame into the wall, and a small reel of coiled cable hangs at one end. Everything sits between y 1.35 and 2.15, clear of the counter below.
parts.attaches: Bolts onto mount backWallFace above the galleyCounter worktop line; nothing below y 1.35 so the counter's shelf clears it.

parts.builds: The iconic Nostromo mess table, centre-front, standing on mount deckTop. A chunky ivory molded table top (rounded octagon-ish slab, tabletop colour) on a heavy dark iron pedestal base with a ribbed column and a round foot. Around it, six attached-style swivel stools: each a molded beige stool seat (stool colour) on a slim dark column with a weighted black base, arranged around the table at varied heights and slight rotations so it feels lived-in. On the table: small cream cups, a metal tray with recessed eating compartments, a small brass ashtray, a lidded beaker, and a pack of cards fan in chalk with black pips. A floor mat in rubber under the stool cluster. Keep the silhouette bold and readable from the front view.
parts.attaches: Stands on mount deckTop in the open centre of the room; its stools stay inside its box, clear of the counter at z < -1.45.

parts.builds: Left-wall storage against mount leftWallFace, standing on mount deckTop. A row of four tall crew lockers in olive with cream door frames, vent slats in black, small number plates and black latches; above them a wall-mounted rack of equipment cases in orange and rust with warning-yellow stripes. Beside the lockers a floor-standing stack: two olive supply crates with stencil-style plates and strap bands, a small drum in machine grey with a rust ring, and a few individually placed props — a black toolbox with a brass clasp, a stack of metal ration tins in chalk and machine grey, a hanging clip lamp in iron with a warm lampGlow bulb.
