spec.description: A cramped, greasy, lived-in 1979 Nostromo-style spaceship galley: fridge, prep counter with CRT, cooking range under a hood, a bolted mess table with stools and a cat, all in a beige-and-grey utilitarian shell with amber and fluorescent lights.
spec.layout: A corner of a working starship. Viewed from the front (+Z), looking at the back wall (z = -1.4 wall face). Along the back wall, left to right as the viewer sees it: the tall fridge/freezer block at x -1.8..-0.95 (the model's right), the prep counter with sink, CRT monitor and overhead cabinets at x -0.95..0.6, and the cooking range with extractor hood at x 0.6..1.8 (the model's left). A solid bulkhead wall stands on the model's left (x +1.8..+1.95, z -1.55..-0.1) with a hatch frame; the right side is open. The mess table, a bolted steel pedestal table 1.4 x 0.8 m with four round stools and a tabby cat, stands at floor centre-front (x ±1.25, z -0.1..1.3). Ceiling girders, ducts, pipes and strip lights hang from y 2.2..2.4, with no ceiling plate. The deck is a dark grey grated plate (y 0..0.08) with a yellow/black hazard edge at the front. Everything else rests on the deck top (y = 0.08). Style: Alien (1979) Nostromo. Truckers-in-space industrial, not sleek. Dirty cream and putty panels, dark grey and olive trim, stainless steel, rust-orange pipework, rivet rows, toggle switches, stencilled labels, amber warning lamps, a green phosphor CRT, strip fluorescents. Everything is boxy and blocky with chunky chamfered greebles and a lot of small bolted detail. Grime is built as small stain patches and scuff strips in the grease colour on lower faces and near the range. Glow (kits/glow) is used for lamps, strip lights, CRT and indicator lights only. Everything is static (no joints). Parts avoid each other's boxes; wall details of a part stay inside that part's x range. The shell owns the bare wall plane, and the zone parts mount their things in front of it at z > -1.39.

calls.reasoning:
I'm sketching a static prop for a spaceship galley kitchen in the Nostromo style: lived-in, 1979 retro-futurism, grey-green panels, amber lights, CRTs, toggles, and clutter. I'm also weighing whether it needs any joints, though static looks fine so far, and I'm roughing out a corner footprint around 3.6 by 2.4 by 3.0.

I'm laying out the galley module now: a deck floor plate, a back wall with counters, and a roughly 3.6 by 2.4 by 3.0 footprint sitting on y=0. I'm weighing whether to leave the side wall open and tracking the grating, conduits, and ceiling lamp strips as separate boxes that can overlap the floor.

I'm deciding how to divide the shell into parts: a deck floor, a bare back wall, and a ceiling with ducts and lights. Each one sits in its own layer, with the back wall running along the rear of the footprint, and I'm working out how to keep the wall surfaces clear of mounted objects between the floor and the ceiling.

I'm dividing the galley's zones along the x-axis: the cooking range on one side, a prep counter with overhead cabinets in the centre, and cold storage with a wall dispenser on the other. The front centre is reserved for a dining table.

I'm settling the parts list now: a shell, a cooking station, a prep counter with overhead cabinets and a CRT, a cold storage unit, and a mess table, each with a rough triangle budget that keeps the total under 900.

I'm placing the fridge at the left end of the back wall, the prep counter in the middle, and the cooking range at the right, with the hood above the range. The overhead cabinets sit above the prep counter, and the mess table goes at the centre front.

I'm working out where the stools and table sit: the table top is about 1.5 by 0.8, centred toward the front, with stools on both sides and one at the front. I'm also weighing whether to add a low side wall on the open edge, and I'm leaning toward keeping just the back wall and ceiling, with the shell carrying floor grating, hazard stripes, conduits, and vents.

I'm settling the galley's dimensions: widening the footprint to about 3.9 by 2.4 by 3.1, with the back wall set a little forward and the counters running back to it. I'm also weighing a bulkhead on the left side with a hatch frame, and leaving the right side open.

I'm settling on a side wall along the left (+X) edge that runs back to a hatch frame, leaving the right side open, which lets the cooking range sit against that wall. I'm also deciding against a full ceiling panel so the view from above stays clear, and I'll rely on cross beams and pipes for the overhead structure.

I'm picking out the colour palette now: grey-greens, cream, rust, copper, and amber for the lamps, plus CRT greens for the screens.

I'm fixing the back-wall layout now: the mount points go in a dictionary, and the wall shell keeps clear of counters and overhead cabinets. Its vertical details stay within the backsplash band between the counters and the cabinets, so nothing collides at the seams.

Next I'm deciding how the shell's wall seams and panels meet the zone items: the shell keeps seams and rivets across the whole back wall, while the other parts sit in front of it on their own x ranges. I'm also considering whether ceiling strips and glow effects, maybe for the lamps and CRTs, can carry the steel look.

Still writing the box definitions...

Still settling the mess table and its stools: the table top is about 1.4 by 0.8 near the centre front, with stools at the sides and two at the front. I'm also budgeting the shell at around 170.

Still assigning the budgets for the cold storage, prep counter, cooking station, and mess table, then describing the shell's details: grating on the floor, yellow hazard stripes along the front edge, beige wall panels with seams and rivets, and a hatch frame on the left bulkhead.

I'm adding a cat, Jones the tabby, perched on the front-right stool beside the mess table, and I'll keep the bowl on the table as the main prop. Then I'm writing the whole layout up as JSON with the palette, mount points, and colour names spelled out.

I'm settling on the coordinate convention now: +X is the model's left side, so the bulkhead and cooking range sit on that edge.

I'm writing the buildColdStorage function that produces the fridge, keeping it fairly detailed but lean, with static parts attached straight to the root and no joints.

I'm settling the cabinet's footprint inside the box: the body narrows to make room for a thin dispenser on the right side, and the pipes will run up to 2.2 so they attach to the ceiling.

I'm laying out the fridge's body and doors: a plinth at the base, a body spanning the box's width up to just short of the counter, and the front doors split into a lower fridge section and an upper freezer section with a thin control strip at the top.

Still writing the door and handle details...

Still writing the fridge's helper functions and visual details.

Still writing the buildColdStorage details: the dispenser buttons sit on the outer face of the dispenser, and two copper pipes run up at the cabinet's back edge with insulation rings around them.

Still writing the cylinder placements and the gauge mount, with the pipes set at slightly different x positions.

I'm writing one function that builds the mess table part, aiming for an efficient but detailed build of up to about 160 parts. It'll be static with no joints, so each piece is placed with b.part at a set position, and since there are no joints there's no bone and the parts stay in model space. I'll use the Ctx type as the module already provides it, without declaring it myself.

I'm laying out the stools next: four of them at set spots around the table, each with a base plate, a column, a footrest ring, and a cushioned seat sitting within the deck bounds. The table top sits at the stated height with its pedestal and flared foot, and I'm adding a hazard ring near the base.

Still working out the cat on the stool: the body is an egg-shaped sphere sitting on the seat, with the head placed a little lower and the ears kept just under the top limit. The chest is a cream sphere on the front, the front paws are cylinders and the back haunches are spheres at the sides, and the curled tail is an arc of torus geometry.

Still laying out the cat's markings, eyes, nose, and ears, then the table's place settings: four trays with compartments and food, arranged around the top.

Still building out the table's details: the trays beside the settings, mugs, a flask at the centre, ration packs, salt and pepper, a tablet, a crumpled napkin, and a lit communicator. Then the grime rings and spills on the top, plus the frame with corner blocks at the rim.

Still working on the underside: the frame gets a panel-dark ring beneath the top and braces running to the pedestal. The rim goes on as thin strips with chamfered corner blocks, and I'm setting up a shared helper to place each part with its position and rotation.

Still working through the bowl placement: a bowl at the earlier spot would clash with the stool's base plate, so I'm shifting it outward along x to clear the stool.

Still counting the parts for the stools, which come to about 13 each, and checking the table build against the budget.

Still tallying the parts, now the table's own pieces: the top, rim and corner blocks, the frame, pedestal and flare, and the hazard ring, then the settings at about ten parts each. Trimming the stool bolts and the settings brings the total to roughly 170, so I'll need to cut a little more.

Trimming the stool bolts to three and merging them, cutting the settings' cutlery and dividers down, and dropping the grime rings and spills to two each should bring the total near 155.

Still writing the cat's tail as a partial torus, working out how its arc should wrap around the front of the seat.

Still settling the tail's arc, which I'll make a little larger than the paws so it clears them, then I'll start writing the code.

I'm writing the buildShell function and wondering whether Ctx should be defined locally or taken from the module, since a duplicate declaration could conflict. I'm leaning toward typing the destructured parameters inline instead.

Now I'm working out the batch collector: boxes grouped by colour and merged into one part per colour, so the deck grating stays within the 170-part budget.

Still writing the batch helper and merging geometry per colour...

Still sizing the grating and bolts: roughly 108 tiles and about 130 small bolt boxes should keep the mesh well under budget. I'm also thinking about the hazard band along the front edge, where slanted stripes would be ideal but boxes can only be rotated about one axis, so I'm weighing whether a simple rotated box approximation is good enough.

Still laying out the hazard band: alternating yellow and black slanted stripes, each rotated about the vertical axis so they stay inside the ±1.95 limit, with a black base strip underneath. Then the steel drain grate near the front edge and a few flat grime patches at the foot of the counters.

Now I'm sketching the back wall as a slab with vertical seam strips every 0.6 units, each thin and set just in front of the surface, plus rivets spaced along those seams.

Still placing the conduit and the label plates along the back wall, with the yellow stencil bars and the vertical cylinders by the fridge edge.

I'm placing a thin frame post at the back-right corner and considering a couple of front posts up near the ceiling girders, though I'm leaning toward keeping the right side open and adding very little there. After that I'm turning to the bulkhead along the right edge.

Still sketching the bulkhead's seams: horizontal strips at four heights on its front face, kept thin so they sit just proud of the surface where the range abuts it.

Now I'm placing the hatch on the bulkhead face: a frame of dark bars around a panel about 0.7 wide and 1.6 tall, with vertical seams set at two depths so the hatch sits between them.

Still placing the hatch's wheel-lock and hinges, plus an amber indicator lamp and bolts around the frame.

Next I'm wiring up the extinguisher and lever box near the front of the bulkhead, with the extinguisher cylinder and its black valve and hose as one part.

Now I'm placing the extinguisher, its hose, and the lever box beside the hatch. Next I'm turning to the ceiling girders, which run along x at two depths with bolted flanges.

Still sizing the girder flanges and the duct above them, so they clear the hood's top edge.

I'm placing the duct along the ceiling at the centre depth, split into four segments with flanges at the joints and clamp bands, plus a louvred vent grille underneath. Then I'm adding two strip-light housings under the girders, one near the middle and one at the front, with glowing tubes beneath them.

I'm sizing the hanger rods for the strip lights at the centre depth, since that housing isn't under a girder. Next I'm placing the light strips along x around the middle, then sketching the pipe bundle at the back-right corner.

Still working out the pipe bundle, sizing the three pipes so they clear the cabinets above them.

Still working out the pipe run: coupling rings every 0.6 units, with valves planned at two points along it.

Now I'm adding a shutoff valve to the rust pipe near the front, with a red handwheel on a short stem, and fitting U-clamps along the run every 0.9 units.

Still writing the hanging cable loops from the ceiling girder at z 0.9, and adding a few clips along them.

Still placing the amber lamps' caged housings near the bulkhead, and I'm weighing whether to add posts that drop from the girders to the walls, placing them clear of the stools and the table pedestals.

Now I'm sizing the posts that tie the girders down to the floor: thin dark steel columns at the far ends, with base plates, and checking they clear the bulkhead and the stools. I'm also tallying the parts budget, since merging by colour keeps the count low, and the triangle total for the deck tiles, bolts and rivets still looks comfortably under 12,000.

Still writing the helper functions for the geometry buckets, with cylinders at a low segment count to keep the triangle total down.

Still writing the helper code, with the merge step pulled in and a separate bucket for the glow parts.

Still writing the helper code: a collector factory with a regular and a glowing variant, plus put and box functions that place each part with a position and rotation.

Still writing the helper code: a collector that buckets geometry by colour, with cylinders at a low segment count to keep triangles down.

Still writing the deck and its geometry buckets, with the flush step merging each colour into one part.

Still laying out the deck tiles in a grid, and placing the bolt intersections between them.

Still working out the deck details: a steel trim along the side edges, and then the hazard band at the front, with a black base strip and yellow stripes angled around the vertical axis.

Still writing the drain grate: a dark frame with slats across it, plus bolts at the corners.

Still working out the deck's grime patches and the strip along the top of the back wall.

Still laying out the vertical seams along the back wall, every 0.6 units, each a thin strip just proud of the surface.

Still writing the wall's label plates and the stencil letters, placing a few yellow bars on each black plate.

Still writing the conduit and clips along the back wall.

Still placing the fire extinguisher's body and neck beside the hatch, sizing it to sit between the floor and the lever box.

Still writing the fire extinguisher's hose: a curved run from its head that drops down along the side of the bulkhead, clear of the hatch frame.

Still working out the extinguisher's bracket straps and the hose's path, making sure they clear the hatch frame.

Still working out the lever box and the hatch's frame bars.

Still working out the hatch panel: a steel door about 1.46 tall and 0.56 wide, set just proud of the bulkhead, with the frame bars around it and angled corner blocks at the inner corners of the opening.

Still working out the hatch wheel and its rim.

Still working out the wheel's spokes and the handle knobs.

Still working out the hatch's wheel rim and the hinge blocks along its left edge, then settling where the latch sits relative to the extinguisher body.

Still placing the hatch's amber lamp above the door and checking the extinguisher hose clears the frame bar.

Still placing the rivets along the bulkhead seams and the skirting panel at its base, then sizing the girder webs along the ceiling.

Still working out the girder flanges and web, with stiffeners every 0.65 units and bolts along the bottom flange; now I'm sizing the splice plates at the girder joints.

Still placing the posts that tie the girders to the floor: a steel post at the far end with a base plate and bolt heads, and I'm checking that it clears the bulkhead.

Still working out the duct: a single run along the ceiling with flange rings and clamp bands spaced between them.

Still placing the vent grille under the duct, with a dark frame and slats.

Still working out the strip lights: the housings sit in a row along x and hang from rods, with the rods running up toward the girder bottoms at the far end.

Still writing the strip light glow tubes and their rods, with the lamp housings and diffuser rails along them.

Still working out the loop placements for the cable hanging from the girder at z 0.9, nudging them to the front side so they clear the flange.

Still working out the loop placements for the cable hanging from the girder at z 0.9, and the remaining cable runs along the back.

I'm checking whether the pipe run along the back-right corner clears the hood, since the hood's top edge sits close to the pipes' height.

Still working out the pipe run: three pipes side by side at the back-right corner, with coupling rings staggered every 0.7 units and two valves planned on the rust pipe.

Still working out the valve on the rust pipe: a box body at the front, with a short stem and a red handwheel out in front of it.

Still working out the valves and clamps along the pipe run.

Still placing the amber lamps by the bulkhead: a steel base plate, a short bracket stub, and a glowing amber lens below each.

Still writing the lamp cage: six thin vertical bars in a ring, two thin rings at top and bottom, and a steel guard cap underneath.

Still writing the helper code, and checking the wall base: I'm weighing a few grime streaks along the lower back wall to match the stains already on the deck.

Still writing the helper code, now sketching the glyph function that draws each stencil letter from thin bars.

Still writing the helper code, now placing the wall's seam strips and rivets just proud of the back panel.

Flushing both collectors now, then I'll get the rest of the scene written.

subject: strandbeest
pitch:
Category: Abstract.
Subject: wind-walking beach creature of tubes.
Style: Theo Jansen kinetic sculpture.

spec.name: Strandwalker
spec.description: A Theo Jansen-style wind-walking beach creature built from pale PVC tube trusses, with a flapping spine wing, a wind-eating bow and two rows of linked legs striding the sand.
spec.layout: A long horizontal tube-truss spine runs the full 6.2 m from nose at z=+3.0 to tail at z=-3.0, riding 0.95 m above the beach on two parallel trains of walking legs (left legs at x≈+1.05, right at x≈-1.05), three legs per side spread along z from +2.4 to -2.4; each leg is the classic Strandbeest linkage — a triangle of rigid tubes from hip, a knee knuckle, a long lower shank and a flat paddle foot, feet flat on y=0. On top of the spine amidships sits a single great wing: a thin spar frame 2.2 m wide across x, rising to y=2.1, cloth panels stretched between tubes, hinged to flap. The bow at the front is the creature's mouth: a fan of short open tubes angled into the wind with a small red crank hub. The stern carries a bundle of wind-stomach bottles and one tall tail fin of stretched sail cloth. The style shows everywhere as skeletal tube frames: every member is a thin cylinder or slim box truss, every connection is a visible dark joint cuff or red pivot hub, pale canvas panels glow against the tubes, and nothing is skinned — the machine reads as bone and ligament from every angle. Front view: bow tubes flared, wing spreading left-right above, legs descending in a forest of thin tubes to paddle feet. The lowest points (the feet) touch y=0.

parts.builds: The full-length tube truss spine from nose to tail: a horizontal ladder of paired top and bottom chord tubes along z (top chord at y=1.55, bottom at y=1.15) joined by diagonal zig-zag web tubes and dark joint cuffs at every node, cross-braced triangles so the frame reads skeletal from every side. At the bow (z=+2.7..+3.05) the spine flares into the wind mouth: a fan of 9 short open tubes angled up and outward into the wind, ringed by a red crank hub disc, with a small mesh screen grille of thin crossed tubes. Mid-spine carries a row of small red pivot hubs on both sides at the hip mounts, plus a few tiny tube stubs and a hanging thin sensor antenna tube near the front. Colours: main chords in tube, diagonals in tubeShade, all cuffs and node blocks in jointDark, crank and hub details in crankRed, the antenna tip in crankRed.
parts.attaches: Roots at spineCenter and runs through spineF, spineB and nose joints; hands the hip sockets on hipLineL/hipLineR to the leg trains, the wingRoot platform to wingMast, noseMount to itself (bow ends there), and tailMount to the stern.

parts.builds: The great flapping wing above the spine: a central mast tube rising from the spine at wingRoot to y=2.05, carrying a horizontal main spar 2.2 m across x (from x=-1.1 to x=+1.1), with a lighter secondary spar behind it and thin rib tubes connecting them into four bays. Stretched between the spars are sail-cloth panels (thin flat slabs) in sail with darker sailEdge trim strips along the leading edge and a small red pennant flag at the left wingtip. Dark joint cuffs sit at the spar-mast crossings and at the wingHinge pivot; a small red crank arm connects mast to spine so the wing reads as wind-driven. The whole wing is tilted a few degrees and built to be flappable about the hinge.
parts.attaches: Roots on the spine's top chord at mount wingRoot and the joint wingHinge; meets spineCore only there, nothing below y=1.8.

parts.builds: The left row of three walking legs at x≈+1.05, one per hip joint (hipFL z=+1.9, hipFM z=+0.6, hipFB z=-0.7). Each leg is the Strandbeest linkage built from tubes: a short hip crank tube leaving the socket with a red pivot hub, a triangular rigid frame of three tubes down to a knee knuckle (dark joint cuff), a long lower shank tube angling down and forward, and a lower-joint cuff from which a flat paddle foot (a thin slab, 0.34 long × 0.16 wide) lands flat on y=0. A thin diagonal stay tube ties the leg frame back to a mid point so the triangle silhouette is unmistakable. All three legs are identical but phase-staggered slightly. Additional knee/shank joints are created inside this part parented to its hip. Colours: tubes and shanks in tube, diagonal stays in tubeShade, all knuckles, cuffs and hubs in jointDark, pivot hubs and foot edge strips in crankRed, paddle foot top in sail.
parts.attaches: One leg socket per hip joint (hipFL, hipFM, hipFB) at mount hipLineL; upper crank ends meet the spineCore side hubs; feet land flat on the floor.

parts.builds: The mirror of legTrainL on the right at x≈-1.05: three identical Strandbeest linkage legs on hipFR (z=+1.9), hipMR (z=+0.6), hipBR (z=-0.7), each with hip crank and red pivot hub, triangular tube frame to a dark knee knuckle, long lower shank, and a flat paddle foot landing on y=0, with a thin diagonal stay tube. Phase-staggered differently from the left row so the gait reads. Colours exactly as the left train: tube, tubeShade, jointDark, crankRed, sail foot tops.
parts.attaches: One leg socket per hip joint (hipFR, hipMR, hipBR) at mount hipLineR; upper crank ends meet the spineCore side hubs; feet land flat on the floor.

parts.builds: The tail assembly behind z=-2.7: a short horizontal tail boom of two tubes leaving the tailMount, then the wind-stomach — a tight bundle of 6 rounded bottles (capsules) in bottleTeal strapped to a small frame with dark straps and one red valve cap on the top bottle — plus a tall triangular tail fin of stretched sail cloth rising from the boom tip to y=2.0, panelled in sail with a sailEdge border and two thin batten tubes across it. The boom ends in a small dark tail knob. Colours: boom tubes in tube, frame in spineDark, straps and knob in jointDark, bottles in bottleTeal, valve in crankRed, fin in sail and sailEdge.
parts.attaches: Roots on the spine end at mount tailMount on joint tailRoot; overlaps spineCore only at the boom root z=-2.55..-2.7.

calls.reasoning:
I need to write a spec for a wind-walking beach creature in Theo Jansen style — a Strandbeest. Tubes, wind sails, walking legs. Category: Abstract, made of tubes.

Model: ~2.4m wide, ~2.1m tall, ~6.2m long? Actually a strandbeest walks along... front faces +Z, so the creature's walking direction is +Z. Legs along the sides, wind wing/sail on top.

Plan the parts (3–6):
1. spine/body core — horizontal tube frame spine with triangular bracing, nose/bowsprit, wind organ tubes (glowing? no, beach creature — maybe wing on top).
2. wing — top sail/awning flapping, pump wing.
3. leg frame left and right — the famous leg linkage: many tube segments per leg, feet. Could be one part "legGearL" and one "legGearR" but symmetric parts split evenly; maybe one part builds both sides via mirror? The spec says each part is self-contained; builders can mirror. Let's do: leftLegs, rightLegs as two parts (4 legs each side? Strandbeests have many legs per side). Or one part "legs" building all legs might be too big. Split: "legTrainL" and "legTrainR", each budget ~200.
4. tail/stern: wind stomach — PVC bottle array / sail tail, plus ground props? Brief says only subject. Tail part: rear frame, sail fin, pump bottles.

So parts: spineCore (budget 200), wingMast (150), legTrainL (200), legTrainR (200), stern (150). Total 900. Good — 5 parts.

Joints: root at spine center, spine joints along length, wing hinges, hip joints per leg, knee joints... The joints array defines skeleton before parts run; both leg parts reference hipL1 etc. But legs per side: strandbeests have legs in a row. Let's simplify: 3 legs per side, each with hip joint. Actually the front part of a strandbeest has one leg assembly per side driving many feet. For abstract: give each side a leg chain per foot? Simpler: per side 3 hips, each hip joint, plus knee per leg. That's a lot of joints in the spec. The spec joints are just top-level named ones; the builder may create more? Actually spec says "joints is the skeleton, created in this order before any part runs". Parts list joints their geometry rides. Builders probably create more joints via chain in their own part. To be safe, define main joints: root, spine segments, wingRoot, wingTip, hips per side, tail. Let the leg part builders create leg linkage joints themselves (they'd use b.joint with parents named). Hmm, risky but acceptable — parts can create additional joints parented to listed ones.

Mounts: spineNose [0,1.5,2.6], spineTail [0,1.5,-2.6], wingRoot [0,2.0,0.3], hipLineL x=+1.0, etc.

Palette: PVC yellow-white tubes (#e8dcc0), dark joints (#33383f), red accents (#c8452a), sail (#d9cfae), sand amber, sea foam trim.

Keep it tight. Sizes: width 2.4, height 2.1, length 6.2 (legs extend in z along length? Strandbeest is long: many legs along length). Yes legs spread along z from 2.8 to -2.8.

Joints list:
- root "spine0" at [0,1.5,0], dir [0,0,1], role spine.
- spine1 [0,1.5,1.5], spine2 [0,1.5,-1.5], neck/ bow "nose" [0,1.6,2.6], "tailRoot" [0,1.5,-2.8] role tail.
- "wingHinge" at [0,1.9,0.4], parent spine0, dir [0,0,1]? wing flaps about x-axis: hinge line along X. joint dir [1,0,0] role hinge. 
- hips: hipFL at [1.05,1.2,1.9], hipFM [1.05,1.2,0.6], hipFB [1.05,1.2,-0.7]? And mirrored right x=-1.05. Roles "leg". Give parent spine0/spine1.
That's ~11 joints fine.

Mounts: spineCenter [0,1.5,0], noseMount [0,1.55,2.6], tailMount [0,1.5,-2.8], wingRoot [0,1.95,0.4], axleL... hipSockets are joints already. Also footline? feet rest on floor: legs own floor:true.

Floor: legTrainL and legTrainR floor true. Spine rests above y ~0.9 min.

Boxes:
- spineCore: [[-0.5,0.9,-3.0],[0.5,1.9,3.1]]
- wingMast: [[-1.1,1.85,0.2],[1.1,2.1,1.4]] — wing spans wide: maybe [[-1.15,1.85,0.1],[1.15,2.1,1.5]]. Wing is a long horizontal wing along X that flaps — like Strandbeest wings. Yes.
- legTrainL: [[0.3,0,2.6],[1.25,1.45,-2.6]]
- legTrainR mirrored.
- stern: [[-0.6,1.0,-3.2],[0.6,2.0,-2.6]] — hmm tail sail should be tall: [[-0.7,0.95,-3.25],[0.7,2.0,-2.55]]. Stern includes wind-stomach bottles and a tail fin sail rising to 2.0.

Actually the nose part: front bow with wind organ / mouth that eats wind. spineCore covers full length including nose.

Budgets: spineCore 200, wingMast 150, legTrainL 220, legTrainR 220, stern 110 = 900.

Write layout text describing style: pale PVC tubes, dark joint cuffs, red crank hubs, sail cloth.

Behind it the hull is a shallow rectangular tube truss: two parallel top rails at x = ±0.28 arcing from y 1.52 at the front to y 1.62 mid-body down to y 1.45 at the rear, over lower rails at y 1.08, cross-rung every ~0.4 m from z -2.1 to z 1.85, with thin diagonal braces; a mid keel tube runs under the top rails. The four legs are the signature: at each hip mount [±0.55, 1.08, z] (front z 1.05, rear z -1.35) a lattice of yellow PVC tubes — thigh out to the knee [±0.95, 0.70, z+0.18], shank back down to the ankle [±0.72, 0.16, z-0.05], and a straight top strut hip-to-ankle closing the triangle — plus one secondary brace and a flat triangular shin web plate; each leg ends in a wide dark foot pad flat on the sand with three transverse teal grip bars. Above the mid-deck a mast rises from [0, 1.6, 0.1] to [0, 2.5, 0.1] carrying two triangular yellow sails (a forward one to a bow spreader at [0, 2.15, 1.1], an aft one to [0, 2.2, -1.2]), each with three tube battens, ink edge seams, and two horizontal wing spars reaching to x = ±1.0 at y 2.2 with small hanging membrane panels and thin ink guy lines. At the rear, two tail tubes drop back from [0, 1.7, -2.15] to [±0.15, 1.35, -2.55] braced by a cross strut, carrying a vertical sail-cloth rudder fin (peaking at y 2.5 around z -2.4) with a small orange pennant at its top and thin ink steering drag-lines running forward to the rear hips. The only parts touching y = 0 are the four foot pads; everything else stands above. Style on every part: pale PVC yellow tubes with white coupling discs and dark zip-tie collars at every connection, yellow sail cloth, dark feet and hardware, a single orange-red accent for the pennant and blade tips, small teal details — flat colours throughout, low-poly, joints and struts slightly oversized so the machine reads as a walking skeleton.

spec.name: Ventus Ambulans
spec.description: A Theo Jansen wind-walking beach creature: a long spine of pale PVC tubes carried on six articulated linkage legs, crowned with amber wing sails and a spinning nose propeller, marching on flat feet.
spec.layout: A kinetic beach animal built entirely from tubes and flat panels, low-poly and blocky. Front (+Z): the head end — two neck tubes rise from the spine up and forward to a small tube skull with a twin-tube beak, an amber sail-fin crest on top, round dark eyes with cream rings each side, and a small red pennant at the beak tip. Centre: the main spine runs along z at about y = 1.5 — a thick pale tube with black taped sleeve cuffs at every station, short cross ribs left and right, and a lower keel triangle of tubes hanging beneath it; on the three hip mounts (z = 1.55, 0, -1.55) cross-axle tubes run along x with yellow tape wraps, one per side. Above the spine amidships a wind mast of two braced tubes rises to a horizontal wing boom pivoting on its axle: two large scalloped amber sail panels hang laced to the boom with rope stays, a rack of three green recycled-bottle wind-organ tubes is lashed under the boom, and a four-blade cream propeller with red tips faces +Z at the mast top. Behind, the spine tapers into a tail of three splaying tubes ending in a second red pennant. Below, six legs (three per side) are triangle trusses of tubes — hip socket collar, paired upper rods to the knee, paired lower rods to the ankle, a foot rod to a flat dark foot pad with two small toe spikes — each leg wearing yellow tape wraps, a red ankle band and a dark steel counterweight block on the outer thigh; the feet pads rest flat on y = 0, the whole stance slightly staggered so it reads mid-stride. Style: every joint is a black taped collar, every accent a yellow caution-tape ring, every sail a flat amber or cream panel; pale warm bone tones below, amber and red accents above, nothing smooth.

parts.builds: The central body tube of the walker. One main spine tube swept smoothly along the body and tail joints from z = 1.5 back to z = -2.2, radius about 0.16 tapering to 0.1, in tubePale, with jointBlack sleeve cuffs (short wider tube rings) at every joint station and a tapeYellow caution ring between each pair of cuffs. Beneath it a keel triangle: two tubes running down-and-in from the spine at z = 1.0 and z = -1.6 meeting a short horizontal cross tube at y = 1.0, all tubeMid, braced by a thin rope-coloured diagonal each side. At each of the three hip mounts (hipFront, hipMid, hipRear) a cross-axle tube runs along x from x = -0.6 to x = 0.6 in tubeDark with a tapeYellow wrap at each end — the hip sockets the legs hang from; add a small jointBlack collar at the centre of each axle. Ribs: at z = 0.8 and z = -0.8 a short horizontal strut pair sticks out left and right to x = +/-0.34 with a tapeRed tip cap each. The tail: three tapering tubes from the tailBase mount fanning slightly apart backward (middle one along the tail joint, the outer two angling out by about 12 degrees), tubePale to tubeDark, each ending in a black cap, and a small extruded red flagCrimson pennant (a triangular fin about 0.25 long) at the tail tip. Every piece rides the body or tail joints via the spine sweep's bone list.

Each leg is a tube linkage truss: at the hip mount a jointBlack socket collar (a short wide ring around the hip joint point); from it two parallel upper rods about 0.03 apart in z run hip to knee — one tubePale, one tubeMid — braced by a short cross strut and a thin rope diagonal, with a tapeYellow wrap at mid-span. At the knee a jointBlack collar joins two lower rods running knee to ankle (tubeMid and tubeDark), again cross-braced, with a tapeRed band just above the ankle collar. The ankle collar carries a single foot rod down to the foot joint, and the foot joint carries the foot: a flat footPad slab about 0.3 long (z) by 0.18 wide lying flat on y = 0 with a slight forward toe bevel, plus two small dark toe spikes at its front edge. On the outer face of each thigh a small steelBlock counterweight box (about 0.1 by 0.08 by 0.05) with a tapeRed edge stripe. Also build one horizontal gallery tube along z linking the three hip collars on this side at y = 1.5, tubeDark with yellow wraps, swept across the three hip joints. Stagger the stance subtly: middle leg foot 4 cm forward of the front and rear feet, matching the given joint positions, so the walker reads mid-stride.

parts.builds: The three legs of the model's right side (-X), the mirror of the port legs, riding hipR1/R2/R3 and their knee, ankle and foot joints. spec.name: Strandbeest Wind Walker
spec.description: A Theo Jansen-style kinetic sculpture: a yellow PVC-tube beach creature on eight Holy-Number linkage legs, with crank axles, bottle lungs on its back, and cream wind sails on a mast.
spec.layout:
Everything is yellow PVC tube with dark elbow connectors, white zip ties, steel axles and cream sailcloth, like a beach sculpture built from pipe. +Z is the front; the creature walks toward it. From front to back: (1) a tapering tube prow or nose at z 1.9..2.6 with two bottle 'eyes' and a small wind vane. (2) Behind it the body: two long frame rails with zig-zag triangle bracing, at y about 1.0..1.4 and |x| about 0.38. (3) Four leg stations per side on that frame. (4) A bottle-lung rack (blue and green flat bottles with orange caps and little piston rods) along the top of the frame, y 1.4..1.8. (5) At the back, a mast at z about -1.4 rising to y about 2.5, carrying two big cream triangular sails that fan out to either side (|x| up to 1.0), with yellow battens, rope rigging and a bright pennant on top. Only the feet touch the floor.

LEG TEMPLATE (shared by all 8 legs, built in a plane). Each leg is a Jansen-style linkage of 2D nodes (u forward = +Z, v up = +Y, in meters, measured from its hip pivot P):
P(0,0) frame pivot; C(-0.30,-0.08) crank axle centre; K(-0.30,-0.26) crank pin, which hangs straight down from C at rest; A(-0.42,0.22); B(-0.80,-0.14); D(-0.46,-0.50); E(-0.10,-0.46); F(0.05,-1.11) foot.
Links (each a rod about 0.022 m radius, yellow): C-K (crank arm), P-A, K-A, A-B, K-B, B-D, P-E, E-D, D-F, E-F.
Nodes get dark connector spheres or elbows of radius 0.03, F gets a rubber ball foot of radius 0.05 with an orange cap, and a few white zip ties sit across the joints.
Model position of a node = (x = side * planeX, y = 1.15 + v, z = hipZ + u). Make each link a double rod, one at planeX - 0.03 and one at planeX + 0.03, joined by short spacer bolts at the nodes, so the legs read as thick sculpture. The foot centre is at y about 0.04, so the foot sinks about 0.01 m into the floor. All eight legs use the same rest pose.
Leg stations (hipZ, planeX magnitude): 1: (1.5, 0.62); 2: (0.5, 0.85); 3: (-0.5, 0.62); 4: (-1.5, 0.85). Left side is +X and right is -X; build both sides. Each crank axle runs along X at y 1.07, z = hipZ - 0.30, so it passes exactly through node C of both left and right legs. Each frame pivot axle runs along X at y 1.15, z = hipZ, through node P.

parts.builds: The chassis and the face. Two long yellow PVC side rails at x = ±0.38, y 1.22, from z -2.0 to 1.95. A lower keel tube at y 1.0 along x = 0. Vertical posts and a zig-zag of triangle bracing between the rails and keel (triangulated like a Jansen frame), dark elbow connectors at every junction, and white zip ties. Cross tubes at each pivotAxle station that carry the axle bearings (steel-dark pillow blocks where the axles pass through). At the front, a tapering tube prow runs from noseRoot to noseTip: a slim swept beak made of two converging tubes with a cross brace. Two big bottle 'eyes' (short cylinders with a dome, eyeWhite with rubber pupil discs and a teal ring) sit on either side of the nose root, facing forward, and a small brass wind-vane spinner (a cross of thin rods with a rubber tip) rises above the nose. Colours: pvcYellow for tubes, pvcYellowDark on the underside and keel, elbowInk connectors, zipWhite ties, steelDark bearings. No bottle rack, axles, legs or sail here.
parts.attaches: Rails carry the bearing blocks that the driveline's pivotAxle1..4 and crankAxle1..4 pass through; the rack stands on frameRailL/R at rackTop; the mast foot sits on the rails at mastBase. The face rides head and the frame rides body.

parts.builds: Four Jansen linkage legs, from stations 1 and 2 on both sides (legL1, legR1 at hipZ 1.5 with planeX 0.62; legL2, legR2 at hipZ 0.5 with planeX 0.85). Each leg is built from the LEG TEMPLATE in the layout: ten double yellow PVC link rods joined at the nodes P, C, K, A, B, D, E and F, with elbowInk connector spheres, spacer bolts, white zip ties at the joints, steelDark pin heads, and a pvcYellowDark band where the long links cross. At each foot there is a rubber ball foot with a capOrange cap and a small brass ankle collar. The pin node K gets a brass bushing. Do not build the axles, the crank arms or the discs on the axles, since the driveline owns them, but each leg's C and P node connector must sit on the axle line. The legs are the only parts that touch the floor.
parts.attaches: Hip nodes P at hipL1/R1 and hipL2/R2 sit on the pivot axles pivotAxle1 and pivotAxle2; node C sits on crankAxle1 and crankAxle2, and node K is the crank pin on the end of the driveline's crank arm.

parts.builds: Four Jansen linkage legs, from stations 3 and 4 on both sides (legL3, legR3 at hipZ -0.5 with planeX 0.62; legL4, legR4 at hipZ -1.5 with planeX 0.85), built identically to the LEG TEMPLATE in the layout: double yellow PVC link rods, elbowInk node connectors, spacer bolts, zip ties, steelDark pins, brass bushing on node K, rubber ball feet with capOrange caps. Add a driftwood-brown (use rope colour) wrapped grip band at the top of each leg's P-A rod as a sculpture detail. Do not build the axles, the crank arms or the discs on the axles.
parts.attaches: Hip nodes P at hipL3/R3 and hipL4/R4 sit on pivotAxle3 and pivotAxle4; node C sits on crankAxle3 and crankAxle4; node K is the crank pin on the end of the driveline's crank arm.

parts.builds: The mechanism and the lungs. (1) Four pivot axles (steel rods along X at pivotAxle1..4, running from x = -0.95 to 0.95, riding body) and four crank axles (along X at crankAxle1..4, same span, one per crank joint), with brass collars and end caps on the axle ends outside the legs, and steelDark nuts. (2) On each crank axle, at the planeX of each leg on both sides, a crank arm: a short brass bar 0.18 m long from the axle centre straight down to the crank pin K (crank axle y 1.07, pin at y 0.89, same z), with a pin cylinder pointing out along X, and a small brass disc at the axle hub. Add a few toothed cog discs (steel, 12 teeth) on the crank axles between the frame rails. (3) The bottle-lung rack on the back: two rows of 5 flat plastic bottles per side (bottleBlue and bottleGreen cylinders with tapered necks and capOrange caps, lying along Z on the rails between y 1.4 and 1.75), held by pvcYellow cradles and zip ties, with thin steel piston rods and tiny tube hoses (teal) running from the caps down toward the crank axles. Everything on the axles rides the crank joints; the rack and pivot axles ride body.
parts.attaches: The axles pass through the frame's bearing blocks at the pivotAxle and crankAxle mounts and through the leg nodes P and C. The crank pin heads at K meet the legs. The bottle rack sits on frameRailL/R at rackTop and stays clear of the mast base at z -1.4 (the rack ends at z -1.0).

parts.builds: The wind sails at the back. A yellow PVC mast at mastBase rising and leaning slightly back to mastTop (y 2.45), with a base block, dark elbow collars and zip ties. Two big triangular cream sails (thin extruded or membrane panels in sailCream, with shaded sailShade bands near the root and stitched seam strips) fan out left and right from the mast, each hung on a yellow leading spar that runs from the mast top out and down to a wing tip at about (±0.98, 1.75, -1.2), with a trailing spar to (±0.95, 1.65, -2.6). Add 4 yellow batten tubes across each sail, a small jib sail forward of the mast, brass grommets along the edges, and rope-coloured rigging lines from the mast top to the spar tips and to the frame. A bright pennantRed streamer flag flies from the mast top on a short spar, with a brass finial. At each sail tip hangs a small bottleBlue float with a capOrange cap. A rear arch of two tubes behind the mast at z -2.6 supports the sail trailing edges. The sail stays above the legs and the rack.
parts.attaches: The mast foot sits on the frame rails at mastBase and its foot block rides the mast joint, which is parented to body. Rigging lines end at frameRailL/R near z -1.9 and z -0.8.

calls.reasoning:
I'm sketching a Strandbeest-style wind-walking sculpture, aiming for roughly 2.6 wide, 2.2 tall, and 4.0 long, and I'm listing the parts it needs, starting with the yellow tubes, the sails at the back, and the leg linkages.

I'm laying out the creature's body in regions so each part can be built on its own: a central truss spine with crank shafts and cross-bracing, the front head with bottle sensors, and the cams. The legs will go in separate banks on each side, with each leg module a Jansen linkage given its own phase offset.

I'm working out how to split the creature into regions, with front and rear leg banks on each side and a sail structure at the back, rising to about 2.2 meters. I'm also thinking about whether the skeleton should have joints at all, since a kinetic sculpture might need a root body and crank hinges along the x axis.

I'm working out the leg layout now: three leg modules per side, spaced along the length at roughly 1.3 meters apart, with each leg's crank offset by 120 degrees from its neighbor.

subject: strandbeest
pitch:
Category: Abstract.
Subject: wind-walking beach creature of tubes.
Style: Theo Jansen kinetic sculpture.

spec.name: Strandbeest Windwalker
spec.description: A Theo Jansen–style kinetic beach creature: twelve Holy-Number-linkage legs of yellow PVC conduit walk on a crankshaft, driven by a bank of soda-bottle wind muscles and a pair of sail wings on a central mast.
spec.layout:
A wide, low, skeletal creature that is mostly empty space and straight tubes. It walks toward +Z. A steel crankshaft runs along X at y=1.35, z=0. Along it sit SIX leg planes (YZ-parallel) at x_k = (k-2.5)*0.54 for k=0..5, i.e. -1.35,-0.81,-0.27,0.27,0.81,1.35. Each plane holds one FRONT leg (reaching to +Z, plane x = x_k+0.05) and one REAR leg (the mirror image reaching to -Z, plane x = x_k-0.05), twelve legs in all. Feet stand on y=0 and the knees angle outward, so the legs fan out front and back like a many-legged water strider. Pose rule: front leg k uses the STANCE pose when k is even and the LIFT pose when k is odd; the rear leg uses LIFT when k is even and STANCE when k is odd. That gives six feet down in a zig-zag and six feet lifted 0.22 m, a mid-stride rest pose. Above the axle is a roof-shaped yellow tube frame: a long ridge tube at y=1.66, z=0, with two eave beams at y=1.44, z=+-0.46 that act as the fixed pivots for the legs. On the ridge stands a bank of upright pressure bottles (the wind muscles) with a manifold tube over them. From the middle of the ridge, a slim mast rises to y=3.0. Two white wing-sails spread left and right from it, with ribs, stays and a red pennant on top. Two springy feelers curl forward from the front of the frame as a face-less head. STYLE: everything is straight, evenly thick PVC conduit in saturated yellow, joined at nodes by small black connector spheres and elbows, with white zip-ties, steel bolts and grey bearings. Fabric and plastic stay pale. The model reads as a skeleton of straight rods, with no organic curves except the bottles and sails. Every rod is a thin cylinder or capsule built with b.rod or b.capsule. Alternate tube layers use slightly different yellows so overlapping rods read.

LEG POSE TABLES (FRONT leg; points are (z=f, y), the leg plane's x is added; the REAR leg uses z = -f for every point). Crank axle O=(z0,y1.35). Stance: A(0.46,1.44) B(0.64,1.06) C(0.90,1.36) D(1.00,0.84) E(0.55,0.64) F(0.78,0.07) P(0.127,1.223). Lift: A(0.46,1.44) B(0.50,1.10) C(0.84,1.40) D(0.92,0.98) E(0.46,0.80) F(0.74,0.29) P(-0.127,1.477). Rods (10 per leg, same in both poses): A-B, A-C, P-B, B-C, B-D, C-D, B-E, D-E, E-F, D-F. Rods at the odd-numbered positions in this list (A-B, P-B, B-C, B-D? no: A-B, P-B, B-D, D-E, D-F) sit at x offset -0.015 from the leg plane in the main yellow, and the rest (A-C, B-C, C-D, B-E, E-F) at +0.015 in the shade yellow. Node spheres (r 0.026) sit at A, B, C, D, E, F and P in black. The foot is a rubber pad box 0.07 wide x 0.045 high x 0.26 long, centred at (f=F.f+0.03, y=F.y-0.045+0.0225... i.e. its bottom is at F.y-0.07) so that in stance the bottom is at y=0.0 and in lift it is at y=0.22. Plain tube radius is 0.014 for leg rods.

parts.builds: The yellow tube chassis, the drive and the feelers. (1) The crankshaft: a steel capsule along X from x=-1.78 to 1.78 at the axleCentre line (radius 0.035), with grey bearing collars (short cylinders r 0.06) at x=+-1.64 and at x=0, and black end caps. On the 'crank' joint, one crank arm per leg: twelve steel-dark rods of radius 0.02 from the axle at that leg's plane x to that leg's crank pin P (front legs at x_k+0.05, rear legs at x_k-0.05; take the pin from the pose table with the pose rule: front k even = stance P(z=+0.127,y=1.223), front k odd = lift P(z=-0.127,y=1.477); rear k even = lift, P(z=+0.127,y=1.477), rear k odd = stance, P(z=-0.127,y=1.223)). Each arm gets a round steel hub disc on the axle and a bolt head at the pin end; the leg parts build the pin node itself. (2) The roof frame: two eave beams along X at y=1.44, z=+-0.46, from x=-1.72 to 1.72 (tube yellow, r 0.03) as the legs' fixed pivots, and a ridge tube at y=1.66, z=0, same length. At the cross-frame stations x = -1.64, -1.08, -0.54, 0, 0.54, 1.08, 1.64 add two sloping rods from each eave beam up to the ridge (a tent triangle), with black elbow-sphere connectors where they meet, and a zip-tie ring on each joint. Additional longitudinal braces: a thin tube from each eave beam end to the ridge end, and X-bracing in the two outermost bays. (3) The ends: at x=+-1.64 a bearing plate triangle of three rods from the axle bearing to the eave beams. Rope-yellow ties. (4) Feelers: two curved springy yellow tubes from feelerRootL/R curling forward and up to (+-0.62, 1.95, 1.05), radius 0.012 tapering to 0.008, each ending in a capBlue sphere r 0.04 with a white zip-tie ring near the root, plus a thin steel stay running from the front eave beam. Everything exposed is straight tube with black connector spheres at every junction. Do NOT build leg rods, bottles or sails.
parts.attaches: Eave beams at beamFront and beamRear are the leg pivots A; the ridge at ridgeCentre carries the bank (bankFloor) and the mast (mastBase). Crank arms end at the pin points of each leg (stance and lift pose tables).

parts.builds: The six FRONT Holy-Number legs (reaching to +Z). Use the LEG POSE TABLES in the layout: for plane k=0..5 at x = x_k + 0.05, use the stance pose when k is even and the lift pose when k is odd, using the mounts stanceFront_* and liftFront_* (z=f, y, with x added). For every leg: the 10 rods A-B, A-C, P-B, B-C, B-D, C-D, B-E, D-E, E-F, D-F as b.rod/b.capsule (radius 0.014) in tube yellow (x offset -0.015: A-B, P-B, B-D, D-E, D-F) and tubeShade yellow (x offset +0.015: A-C, B-C, C-D, B-E, E-F); black connector spheres (r 0.026) at A, B, C, D, E, F and P with a steel bolt cylinder across each along X; small white zip-tie rings at each rod end; the foot pad is a rubber box (0.07 x 0.045 x 0.26) under F as given in the layout, plus a short rubber toe wedge on its front end and a yellow-capped tube collar at the ankle. A hinge sleeve (short grey cylinder along X) at A that clamps onto the frame's beamFront tube, and a collar at P that the crank arm bolts into. Optionally a thin tubeLight highlight rod along the long shin. All legs are the same design so the six read as a team. Do NOT build the crank arms, the axle or the frame.
parts.attaches: Joint A of each leg wraps the beamFront eave beam (y=1.44, z=0.46). Joint P meets the crank arm tip from the frame part. Feet rest on y=0 in stance, 0.22 m above it in lift.

parts.builds: The six REAR legs, the exact mirror (z -> -z) of the front legs, in planes x = x_k - 0.05 for k=0..5. Pose rule: LIFT when k is even, STANCE when k is odd; use the same stanceFront_* and liftFront_* tables with every z negated (for example, stance rear A=(1.44 at z=-0.46), stance rear F=(y 0.07, z=-0.78), lift rear P=(y 1.477, z=+0.127), stance rear P=(y 1.223, z=-0.127)). Everything else is identical to legsFront: ten rods per leg in the two alternating yellows with +-0.015 x offsets, black connector spheres, bolts, zip-ties, rubber foot pads (toe wedge toward -Z), pivot sleeves on beamRear. Do NOT build the crank arms, the axle or the frame.
parts.attaches: Joint A of each leg wraps the beamRear eave beam (y=1.44, z=-0.46). Joint P meets the crank arm tip. Feet rest on y=0 in stance, 0.22 above in lift.

parts.builds: The pressure-bottle wind muscles on top of the ridge. Two rows of UPRIGHT 2-litre soda bottles (turned lathe profile: a base, a belly of r 0.052, a shoulder, a neck, 0.33 m tall) standing from bankFloor (y=1.69, resting on the ridge area) at z=+-0.2, x from -1.5 to 1.5 at 0.25 pitch, skipping |x|<0.14 where the mast stands (12 per row, 24 total). Alternate bottleClear and bottleGreen bottles, with capBlue/capRed caps (r 0.026), a white label band on each (short lathe collar) and a thin base cup. A yellow cradle under them: two tubes along X at z=+-0.2, y=1.69, resting on small posts to the ridge, and cross tubes every 0.5 m. Plumbing: a manifold tube along X at y=2.1 above each row (z=+-0.2) joined to every cap by a short thin tube with black valve boxes (small boxes) and a black T-connector, and tubeShade-coloured zip-ties; the two manifolds join through a thin cross tube at x=+-1.5, and a bicycle-pump style small cylinder with a steel rod at each end of the row (x=+-1.6). All on joint 'bank'. Do NOT build the mast, the sails or the frame.
parts.attaches: Rests on the ridge tube of the frame at bankFloor; the mast passes through the gap |x|<0.14 at the mast base.

parts.builds: The mast and the wing-sails. A slim yellow mast (r 0.03, two sections joined by a black collar with zip-ties) from mastBase (0,1.66,0) up to mastTop (y 3.0), with a steel finial. A yard: a horizontal yellow tube along X at y=2.75 (on joint 'yard'), x from -1.7 to 1.7 (r 0.02). Two big wing-sails, one left (+X) and one right (-X), each made of two overlapping pale fabric panels built with b.extrude/b.slab (thin, in the XY plane at z=+0.05 and z=-0.05): the upper panel from the yard (x 0.06..1.7, y 2.75) to a lower trailing corner (x 1.6, y 2.3) swept like a bird wing, and a lower panel hung from the stay line (y 2.3..2.55). Colours: sail for the main panels, sailTint for the second layer. Each sail has 5 radial yellow-rib battens (thin rods fanning from the mast), rib-wood tip caps, eyelets (tiny dark spheres), and rope stays: thin rope-coloured rods from mastTop to the yard ends and from the yard ends down to the corners of the frame at (+-1.64, 1.66, +-0.46) (frame's eave-beam corners) and a taut forestay to (0, 1.9, 0.5). At the very top, a red pennant (extrude, 0.3 long) on a thin whip rod and a small wind-vane arrow (steel). Keep the sails above y=2.2 so they clear the bottle manifold at y=2.1; only the mast and stays pass lower. Do NOT build the bottles, the frame or the legs.
parts.attaches: Mast foot sits on the ridge at mastBase (joint 'mast'); the stays end at the frame eave-beam corners (+-1.64, 1.44, +-0.46) and the feeler roots.
